data.diagnosis: Acute transverse myelitis, unspecified infectious or post-infectious
data.description: Acute inflammation of the spinal cord causing bilateral or asymmetric weakness, a defined sensory level, neuropathic pain, and bladder or bowel dysfunction. It may follow viral infection or occur as an isolated inflammatory syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Sensory level with loss of temperature sensation below T2 on the left and T4 on the right
Upper motor neuron sign with bilateral Hoffman signs
Spinal MRI abnormalities consistent with intramedullary inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: Conjunctival hyperaemia is not a typical manifestation of transverse myelitis itself
Frontal headache is not a defining feature of isolated transverse myelitis
High Zika viral PCR positivity indicates a specific viral cause rather than unspecified transverse myelitis
Normal CSF findings are less typical, although they do not exclude the diagnosis

data.description: An autoimmune inflammatory demyelinating disorder that can cause severe myelitis, often with longitudinally extensive spinal cord lesions, sensory deficits, weakness, and sphincter dysfunction. It is commonly associated with aquaporin-4 or MOG antibodies.
symptoms_in_common: Sensory level and impaired temperature sensation
Spinal cord MRI lesion compatible with inflammatory myelopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: No optic neuritis or visual loss
No area postrema symptoms such as persistent nausea, vomiting, or hiccups
Negative autoimmune testing
Strong evidence of acute Zika viral infection in serum, urine, and cerebrospinal fluid
Conjunctival hyperaemia and headache are more suggestive of an acute viral illness than NMOSD

data.diagnosis: Multiple sclerosis presenting with partial transverse myelitis
data.description: A chronic immune-mediated demyelinating disease of the central nervous system that may first present with a spinal cord lesion causing sensory symptoms, weakness, and bladder dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral Hoffman signs indicating central motor pathway involvement
Focal spinal cord lesion on MRI could occur in demyelinating disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt illness associated with Zika viral PCR positivity strongly favors infectious myelitis
Conjunctival hyperaemia is not typical of multiple sclerosis
Frontal headache and initial systemic viral-type symptoms are not typical presenting features
No reported prior neurologic episodes or brain lesions disseminated in time and space
Normal CSF examination without reported oligoclonal bands is less supportive of multiple sclerosis

data.description: Ischemic injury to the spinal cord, usually causing sudden severe back pain followed by weakness, dissociated sensory loss, and autonomic dysfunction. It is uncommon in adolescents without vascular risk factors or structural vascular disease.
symptoms_in_common: Loss of temperature sensation with relative dissociation of sensory modalities
Spinal cord MRI signal abnormality can be seen in cord ischemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Symptoms evolved progressively over several days rather than reaching maximal severity suddenly
Conjunctival hyperaemia and headache are not typical of spinal cord infarction
Positive Zika PCR in serum, urine, and cerebrospinal fluid supports viral neuroinvasion instead
No reported vascular risk factors, trauma, hypotension, or vascular malformation
Young age makes spinal cord infarction less likely

data.description: 27-year-old male presented with headache, dizziness, nausea, and vomiting for 3 days before admission. Physical examination showed no palpable lymph-node enlargement or hepatosplenomegaly. Laboratory findings showed: WBC count 49.5×109/L, hemoglobin 161 g/L, platelet count 36×109/L, with 95% blasts in peripheral blood smear. Serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) was markedly elevated to 13,022 IU/L. Flow cytometry showed leukemic blasts were positive for CD2, CD7, CD5, and CD3, and negative for TdT, CD34, CD13, CD33, CD10, CD19, CD20, and CD22.

data.diagnosis: T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (T-ALL/LBL), mature T-cell phenotype with t(X;14) involving TCRAD/IRS4
data.description: An aggressive precursor T-cell neoplasm presenting with marrow and peripheral-blood blasts. The CD2+, CD3+, CD5+, and CD7+ phenotype supports T-lineage leukemia; the cytogenetic/FISH findings are consistent with a T-cell receptor alpha/delta locus rearrangement involving Xq22.3/IRS4.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly elevated LDH indicating high tumor burden
Headache and dizziness, which can occur with hyperleukocytosis/leukostasis
Bone marrow and peripheral blood blast morphology
T-cell marker expression: CD2, CD3, CD5, and CD7 positivity
Absence of B-cell and myeloid markers
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative TdT expression, since many T-ALL cases are TdT positive
Negative CD34 expression, although this can be absent in more mature T-ALL
No lymph-node enlargement
No hepatosplenomegaly

data.description: A mature, aggressive T-cell leukemia characterized by marked lymphocytosis and expression of mature pan-T-cell markers, commonly CD2, CD3, CD5, and CD7. It is usually a disease of older adults and often has splenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, and skin involvement.
symptoms_in_common: TdT negativity and CD34 negativity, supporting a mature rather than precursor T-cell phenotype
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 27 years, whereas T-PLL usually occurs in older adults
Predominance of blasts rather than typical prolymphocytes
Severe thrombocytopenia at presentation
No hepatosplenomegaly
No palpable lymphadenopathy
Acute 3-day presentation with headache, dizziness, nausea, and vomiting
TCRAD/IRS4-associated t(X;14) rearrangement is not the classic T-PLL cytogenetic pattern

data.description: A mature peripheral T-cell malignancy caused by human T-cell lymphotropic virus type 1 (HTLV-1). The leukemic form can cause high white-cell counts, circulating malignant T cells, thrombocytopenia, elevated LDH, lymphadenopathy, organomegaly, skin lesions, and hypercalcemia.
symptoms_in_common: Leukocytosis with circulating malignant lymphoid cells
Mature T-cell antigen expression including CD2, CD3, CD5, and CD7
Possible neurologic symptoms related to marked leukocytosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 27 years, as ATLL more often develops in adults after a long latency period
Blastic morphology rather than characteristic multilobated 'flower' cells
No lymphadenopathy
No hepatosplenomegaly
No skin lesions reported
No hypercalcemia reported
CD7 is often reduced or absent in ATLL
No HTLV-1 infection information
TCRAD/IRS4 rearrangement is not typical of ATLL

data.description: 36-year-old Chinese man with a 1-month history of persistent fever. Previously healthy with no significant past medical history, no regular medications, and no travel abroad. On admission, he was acutely ill with tachycardia, hypotension, tachypnea, hypoxemia, and bilateral pulmonary rales. He had pancytopenia, hypofibrinogenemia, and marked hyperferritinemia, with clinical deterioration to acute respiratory failure.

data.diagnosis: Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) with secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
data.description: A systemic infection caused by Leishmania parasites that invade macrophages in the bone marrow, spleen, and liver. It can trigger secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH), producing severe inflammation, cytopenias, coagulopathy, and multiorgan failure. Intracellular amastigotes in macrophages on marrow smears support this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Findings consistent with hemophagocytosis/HLH in bone marrow
Severe systemic illness with hypotension and tachycardia
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure is less typical as an initial dominant manifestation
Diffuse bilateral pulmonary infiltrates are less common than reticuloendothelial organ involvement
No reported travel abroad or known sandfly exposure

data.diagnosis: Disseminated histoplasmosis with secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
data.description: A disseminated fungal infection caused by Histoplasma species, in which small intracellular yeasts may be found within macrophages in bone marrow or tissue. Severe disseminated disease can cause fever, pancytopenia, hepatosplenomegaly, diffuse lung disease, and secondary HLH.
symptoms_in_common: Marked hyperferritinemia and hypofibrinogenemia consistent with HLH
Possible intracellular organisms within macrophages on bone marrow smear
Sepsis-like presentation with tachycardia and hypotension
symptoms_not_in_common: Previously healthy immunocompetent status is less typical for severe disseminated disease
No travel to a recognized endemic region or reported bat/bird-dropping exposure
No reported mucocutaneous lesions, which can occur in disseminated infection

data.diagnosis: Talaromyces marneffei infection (talaromycosis) with secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
data.description: Talaromycosis is a disseminated dimorphic fungal infection endemic in parts of Southeast Asia and southern China. It commonly affects immunocompromised individuals but can occasionally occur in apparently immunocompetent patients. It may cause intracellular yeast-like organisms in macrophages, pulmonary infiltrates, cytopenias, hepatosplenomegaly, and HLH.
symptoms_in_common: Marked hyperferritinemia and hypofibrinogenemia compatible with HLH
Possible yeast-like intracellular organisms in macrophages
Residence in China, where infection can occur in endemic southern regions
symptoms_not_in_common: No known immunodeficiency, HIV infection, or immunosuppressive medication use
No reported characteristic papular or umbilicated skin lesions
No reported exposure to bamboo rats or other relevant environmental exposure

data.diagnosis: Secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) triggered by severe infection
data.description: HLH is a life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome characterized by uncontrolled immune activation and macrophage-mediated blood-cell destruction. It may be triggered by parasitic, fungal, viral, or bacterial infection and causes fever, cytopenias, hyperferritinemia, hypofibrinogenemia, organ enlargement, and multiorgan failure.
symptoms_in_common: Bone marrow findings compatible with hemophagocytosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral pulmonary infiltrates are not specific for HLH and suggest an underlying infectious pulmonary process
Intracellular organisms in macrophages would indicate a triggering infection rather than HLH alone
No reported neurologic manifestations, liver failure, rash, or lymphadenopathy

data.description: An 81-year-old man presented to the ICU 10 days after a 4-week cruise in New Caledonia, Vanuatu, the Solomon Islands, and New Zealand. He was reported to have been in perfect health during the cruise. On examination, he was febrile (39.1°C) and comatose with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 6. He exhibited hemiplegia of the left side, paresis of the right upper limb, normal tendon reflexes, and a Babinski sign on the left side. A transient rash was observed within 48 hours of admission. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed leukocyte count of 41/mm³ (98% polymorphonuclear leukocytes), protein level of 76 mg/dL, and CSF:blood glucose ratio of 0.75.

data.diagnosis: Varicella-zoster virus encephalitis with cerebral vasculopathy
data.description: Central nervous system infection/reactivation of varicella-zoster virus that can cause meningoencephalitis and inflammation of cerebral arteries, resulting in multifocal ischemic strokes.
symptoms_in_common: Coma with severely depressed Glasgow Coma Scale score
Focal neurologic deficits including left hemiplegia and right upper-limb paresis
CSF pleocytosis and elevated CSF protein
Imaging suggestive of multifocal ischemic brain lesions and cerebral arterial vasculopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: CSF predominance of polymorphonuclear leukocytes rather than the more usual lymphocytic pleocytosis
No reported preceding dermatomal zoster eruption or typical vesicular rash

data.description: A mosquito-borne flaviviral encephalitis acquired in endemic parts of Asia and the western Pacific, causing fever, encephalopathy, coma, and focal neurologic signs; deep gray-matter abnormalities are common on MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Recent travel in the western Pacific region
Focal motor deficits and Babinski sign
CSF pleocytosis with moderately elevated protein
MRI abnormalities involving cerebral parenchyma, including possible deep gray-matter involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Transient rash is uncommon
Predominantly neutrophilic CSF is less typical than lymphocytic CSF pleocytosis
Multifocal ischemic lesions and arterial narrowing/vasculopathy are not classic findings
No reported movement disorder, parkinsonism, tremor, or seizures

data.description: A mosquito-borne flavivirus infection that may cause meningitis, encephalitis, acute flaccid paralysis, and occasionally rash, particularly in older adults.
symptoms_in_common: Advanced age, which increases risk of severe neuroinvasive disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Hemiplegia with upper-motor-neuron signs is less typical than asymmetric flaccid weakness
Normal tendon reflexes do not support the classic acute flaccid paralysis pattern
Predominantly polymorphonuclear CSF may occur early but lymphocytic predominance is more typical later
Cerebral vasculopathy and multifocal ischemic infarction are not typical hallmark findings

data.diagnosis: Dengue encephalitis or dengue-associated cerebral vasculopathy
data.description: Neurologic dengue is an uncommon complication of dengue virus infection and can present with encephalitis, altered consciousness, seizures, stroke, or inflammatory vascular complications after travel to endemic tropical regions.
symptoms_in_common: Travel to tropical Pacific islands where dengue transmission can occur
Severe altered mental status progressing to coma
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, hemorrhage, or plasma leakage
No reported severe myalgia, retro-orbital pain, or arthralgia
Neutrophil-predominant CSF is not the usual pattern
No reported hepatic dysfunction or shock

data.diagnosis: Acute bacterial meningoencephalitis with infectious cerebral vasculitis
data.description: Bacterial infection of the meninges and brain can cause fever, depressed consciousness, focal deficits, and secondary inflammatory narrowing or thrombosis of intracranial vessels, leading to cerebral infarctions.
symptoms_in_common: Focal motor deficits and Babinski sign
Possible cerebral infarctions from infectious vasculitis
Transient rash could occur with meningococcal infection
symptoms_not_in_common: CSF leukocyte count is relatively low for typical untreated pyogenic meningitis
CSF:blood glucose ratio of 0.75 is normal rather than reduced
No reported meningismus, hypotension, petechiae, or septic shock
The rash was transient and not described as petechial or purpuric

data.description: 20-year-old man with Crohn’s disease diagnosed at age 10, previously treated with prolonged glucocorticoids and improved on weekly adalimumab over the past 3 years, presented with 3 weeks of upper respiratory symptoms (sore throat, nonproductive cough, rhinorrhea, chills), followed 2 weeks before presentation by cramping left calf pain that worsened over 2 days with swelling extending to the foot and a purpuric/erythematous rash on the dorsum of both feet. He also reported recurrent self-limited similar upper respiratory episodes over recent years. On exam, he was uncomfortable from left leg pain, with left ankle synovitis and normal peripheral pulses.

An immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis characterized by IgA deposition, typically causing palpable purpura of the lower extremities, arthralgia or arthritis, abdominal symptoms, and possible kidney involvement. It often follows an upper respiratory infection.
symptoms_in_common: Purpuric erythematous rash on both feet and lower legs
Acute painful swelling of the left calf and foot
Recent upper respiratory illness with sore throat, cough, rhinorrhea, and chills
Skin biopsy appearance consistent with leukocytoclastic small-vessel vasculitis
Direct immunofluorescence showing vascular IgA, C3, and fibrin deposition
symptoms_not_in_common: No abdominal pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, or renal symptoms were reported
Markedly unilateral calf pain and swelling is less typical than symmetric lower-extremity manifestations
History of Crohn's disease is not required for IgA vasculitis

data.description: A drug-associated form of IgA small-vessel vasculitis that can occur during treatment with TNF-alpha inhibitors such as adalimumab. It can present with palpable purpura and joint involvement, sometimes after prolonged exposure.
symptoms_in_common: Purpuric rash on the feet and lower extremities
Biopsy and immunofluorescence findings compatible with IgA-mediated leukocytoclastic vasculitis
symptoms_not_in_common: He had tolerated adalimumab for approximately 3 years before this episode, whereas drug reactions may occur closer to treatment initiation
Recent upper respiratory symptoms provide an alternative infectious trigger
No systemic drug-hypersensitivity features such as fever, diffuse rash, eosinophilia, or organ injury were reported

data.diagnosis: Cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis associated with Crohn's disease
data.description: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis is inflammation of small dermal blood vessels causing palpable purpura. It may occur as an extraintestinal manifestation of inflammatory bowel disease or in association with infection or medication exposure.
symptoms_in_common: Painful swelling of the affected leg and foot
Histologic appearance of small-vessel leukocytoclastic vasculitis
symptoms_not_in_common: IgA-dominant vascular deposition favors the more specific diagnosis of IgA vasculitis rather than nonspecific cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis
No evidence of an active Crohn's disease flare or gastrointestinal symptoms was provided
Upper respiratory infection preceding the rash is more characteristic of IgA vasculitis

data.description: A necrotizing systemic small- and medium-vessel vasculitis that commonly affects the upper airways, lungs, kidneys, skin, and peripheral nerves. It can cause purpura and sinonasal disease but usually has systemic organ involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Upper respiratory symptoms including sore throat and rhinorrhea
Leg pain and joint inflammation can occur with systemic vasculitis
symptoms_not_in_common: No chronic sinusitis, nasal ulceration, epistaxis, hearing loss, or destructive nasal disease was reported
No hematuria, proteinuria, renal impairment, hemoptysis, pulmonary infiltrates, or neuropathy was reported
IgA and C3 deposition in skin vessels supports IgA vasculitis rather than pauci-immune granulomatosis with polyangiitis
The temporal association with a respiratory infection and ankle synovitis is more typical of IgA vasculitis

data.description: A 47-year-old man presented to his primary care physician with a six-month history of left-sided sore throat, ipsilateral otalgia, and a six-week history of a left-sided neck mass. He had never smoked and drank less than 5 units of alcohol per week. On examination in the ENT clinic, a firm fixed lymph node was palpable in the upper anterior triangle.

data.diagnosis: HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (tonsillar carcinoma) with cervical lymph-node metastasis
data.description: A squamous-cell cancer arising in the palatine tonsil or adjacent oropharynx, commonly associated with high-risk HPV in younger nonsmokers. It often presents with unilateral throat pain, referred ear pain, and an upper-neck metastatic lymph node. The imaging appearance is consistent with an oropharyngeal primary lesion and ipsilateral nodal disease.
symptoms_in_common: Firm fixed upper anterior-triangle cervical lymph node
Never-smoker status, which is compatible with HPV-associated disease
Low alcohol intake, which is compatible with HPV-associated disease

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the oropharynx, including the tonsil and base of tongue, traditionally associated with tobacco and heavy alcohol exposure. It may invade locally and spread to upper cervical lymph nodes.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging evidence of a likely oropharyngeal mass with nodal involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Never smoked
Alcohol intake is low rather than heavy

data.diagnosis: Oropharyngeal lymphoma involving the tonsil with cervical lymphadenopathy
data.description: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma can involve Waldeyer's ring, including the tonsils, and may cause an oropharyngeal mass with cervical lymph-node enlargement.
symptoms_in_common: Neck mass due to cervical lymphadenopathy
Possible tonsillar or oropharyngeal soft-tissue mass on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Ipsilateral referred otalgia is less typical
A fixed node is more suggestive of metastatic carcinoma than lymphoma
No reported fever
No reported drenching night sweats
No reported unintentional weight loss
The unilateral focal throat symptoms and imaging pattern favor squamous-cell carcinoma

data.diagnosis: Metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma presenting as cervical lymphadenopathy
data.description: Papillary thyroid carcinoma frequently spreads to cervical lymph nodes, sometimes before a thyroid primary is clinically apparent. Metastatic nodes may be cystic or solid and occur in the lateral neck.
symptoms_in_common: Adult age group compatible with thyroid carcinoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent unilateral sore throat is not a typical presenting feature
Ipsilateral otalgia is not typical
Imaging suggests an oropharyngeal primary lesion rather than a thyroid lesion
Upper anterior-triangle nodal location with an oropharyngeal lesion favors metastatic oropharyngeal carcinoma

data.diagnosis: Deep neck infection or suppurative cervical lymphadenitis
data.description: Bacterial infection of the pharynx, tonsil, or cervical lymph nodes can produce throat pain and enlarged neck nodes; abscesses may appear as fluid-containing masses on imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Ear pain can occur with tonsillopharyngeal inflammation
Neck mass due to enlarged cervical lymph node
symptoms_not_in_common: Six-month duration of sore throat is unusually prolonged for an acute infection
Six-week persistent firm fixed lymph node is atypical for uncomplicated infection
No reported fever
No reported acute systemic illness
No reported leukocytosis or inflammatory symptoms
Imaging pattern of an oropharyngeal mass with nodal disease is more concerning for malignancy

data.description: 72-year-old white woman with 10-year history of recurrent cystitis. No systemic symptoms. Physical exam showed slight anemia. Urine cultures were positive for Escherichia coli. No hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy detected by CT and ultrasound. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy and subsequent biopsies were negative for both pathologic lymphoid infiltrate and Helicobacter pylori. Otolaryngologic examination and bone marrow biopsy were negative. Serology for hepatitis C virus and hepatitis B virus was negative. No monoclonal component found in serum protein electrophoresis.

data.diagnosis: Primary extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma) of the urinary bladder
data.description: An indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma arising in extranodal tissue, often associated with chronic antigenic stimulation. Primary bladder MALT lymphoma is rare and is associated with chronic/recurrent cystitis in older women.
symptoms_in_common: Repeated Escherichia coli-positive urine cultures indicating chronic bladder inflammation
No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly on imaging
Negative bone marrow biopsy, supporting localized extranodal disease
Bladder lesion with dense small-to-medium lymphoid infiltrate and apparent lymphoepithelial involvement on histology
symptoms_not_in_common: None strongly atypical; recurrent bacterial cystitis is a recognized predisposing setting

data.diagnosis: Primary diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the urinary bladder
data.description: An aggressive B-cell lymphoma that can involve the urinary bladder, either as primary disease or as transformation of a pre-existing low-grade MALT lymphoma. It usually shows large atypical lymphoid cells and may present as a bladder mass.
symptoms_in_common: Urinary tract symptoms related to recurrent cystitis
symptoms_not_in_common: No systemic symptoms such as fever, drenching night sweats, or weight loss
No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly
Negative bone marrow biopsy
Long-standing recurrent cystitis more strongly supports bladder MALT lymphoma
Histology appears dominated by small-to-medium lymphoid cells rather than diffuse sheets of large atypical cells

data.description: A benign reactive inflammatory bladder condition characterized by lymphoid follicle formation, typically caused by chronic infection or irritation. It can mimic lymphoma clinically and cystoscopically.
symptoms_in_common: Bladder mucosal abnormality in a setting of chronic inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: Dense atypical lymphoid infiltrate with features suggestive of lymphoepithelial lesions is less typical of a purely reactive process
Possible cytogenetic abnormality suggested by fluorescence in situ hybridization would favor lymphoma over reactive cystitis
Slight anemia is not a usual direct feature of localized follicular cystitis

data.diagnosis: Secondary urinary bladder involvement by systemic extranodal marginal zone lymphoma
data.description: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma can arise at another mucosal site and secondarily involve the bladder. Evaluation typically seeks disease in the stomach, salivary/ocular adnexal tissue, lymph nodes, marrow, and other extranodal sites.
symptoms_in_common: Histologic appearance compatible with marginal zone/MALT-type lymphoma
No monoclonal serum protein component, which can occur in localized lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly
Negative bone marrow biopsy
Negative upper gastrointestinal biopsies for lymphoid infiltrate and Helicobacter pylori
Negative otolaryngologic examination
No hepatitis C or hepatitis B infection
The apparent isolated bladder presentation favors primary rather than secondary bladder lymphoma

data.description: 95-year-old woman admitted after a fall. Medical history includes Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus (on metformin). Laboratory findings showed elevated white cell count and C reactive protein levels. Urine culture revealed Klebsiella pneumoniae infection. Blood cultures were negative.

data.diagnosis: Bilateral septic arthritis of the hips
data.description: Infection of one or both hip joints causing rapid cartilage loss, joint-space destruction, erosions, and possible subluxation. In frail older adults, presentation may be subtle and may occur from hematogenous spread or a urinary source.
symptoms_in_common: Klebsiella pneumoniae urinary infection, a possible infectious source
Radiographic destructive changes involving both hip joints
Advanced age and diabetes, which increase susceptibility to infection
Fall, which may be precipitated by acute illness or impaired mobility
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever is reported
No hip pain, reduced hip range of motion, or inability to bear weight is specifically reported
Blood cultures are negative

data.diagnosis: Osteomyelitis involving the femoral heads/acetabula secondary to contiguous septic arthritis
data.description: Bone infection involving the proximal femur and/or acetabulum, often occurring together with septic arthritis and producing progressive erosions and bone destruction on radiographs.
symptoms_in_common: Destructive osseous and articular abnormalities around both hips on imaging
Diabetes mellitus, a risk factor for severe infection
symptoms_not_in_common: No localized bone pain is reported
No fever or systemic septic symptoms are reported
Blood cultures are negative
No draining sinus, overlying skin infection, or prior hip procedure is reported

data.diagnosis: Rapidly destructive osteoarthritis of the hip
data.description: An aggressive form of hip osteoarthritis characterized by rapid loss of the femoral head and acetabular bone, severe joint-space narrowing, and progressive deformity. It is more common in older women and can mimic septic arthritis radiographically.
symptoms_in_common: Marked destructive and degenerative-appearing bilateral hip changes on radiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated white cell count is not typical
Elevated C-reactive protein is not typical
Klebsiella pneumoniae urinary infection is not explained by osteoarthritis
No chronic or rapidly progressive hip pain history is reported

data.description: Progressive joint destruction caused by loss of protective sensation and repetitive microtrauma. Diabetes is a major cause, although hip involvement is uncommon compared with foot and ankle involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Severe destructive joint changes affecting the hips
Fall, which may occur with gait instability or impaired proprioception
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated white cell count is not typical of uncomplicated Charcot arthropathy
Elevated C-reactive protein is not typical of uncomplicated Charcot arthropathy
Klebsiella pneumoniae urinary infection is not directly explained
No documented peripheral neuropathy, loss of sensation, or painless progressive hip deformity

data.description: 22-year-old athletic male presented with swelling and locking of the left knee. He had no recent trauma but had several football injuries as a child. Two years prior, he had experienced disabling knee pain.

data.diagnosis: Osteochondritis dissecans of the medial femoral condyle
data.description: A focal osteochondral disorder in which subchondral bone and overlying cartilage of the femoral condyle become damaged and may partially or completely detach, producing an unstable fragment or loose body. It commonly affects athletic adolescents and young adults and can cause mechanical knee symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Knee locking, suggesting an unstable osteochondral fragment or loose body

data.diagnosis: Intra-articular osteochondral loose body secondary to an osteochondral lesion
data.description: A free fragment of cartilage and bone within the knee joint, often arising from osteochondritis dissecans or prior osteochondral trauma. Loose bodies can intermittently obstruct joint motion and provoke synovitis and effusion.
symptoms_in_common: History of prior knee injuries during football
symptoms_not_in_common: No recent acute trauma is reported, although loose bodies may also arise after an acute osteochondral injury

data.diagnosis: Meniscal tear, particularly a displaced bucket-handle tear
data.description: A tear of the knee meniscus that may become displaced into the joint, causing locking, recurrent swelling, and pain. It is common in athletes and may follow twisting injury, although symptoms can occur after older injuries.
symptoms_in_common: Previous episode of severe knee pain
symptoms_not_in_common: No recent twisting or acute traumatic event is reported
The radiographic appearance of a focal osteochondral abnormality would be less typical for an isolated meniscal tear

data.description: 48-year-old male presented with 1-week history of jaundice, dark brown urine, pale stools, and nausea. Medical history and physical exam were unremarkable. Laboratory findings showed hepatic panel in cholestatic pattern: total bilirubin 117 μmol/L, conjugated bilirubin 66.8 μmol/L, alkaline phosphatase 173 IU/L, γ-Glutamyltransferase 380 IU/L, Alanine transaminase 468 IU/L. CA19-9 was 11783 IU/mL. Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and β2-microglobulin were normal.

data.diagnosis: Primary pancreatic follicular dendritic cell sarcoma
data.description: A rare malignant neoplasm of follicular dendritic cells that can arise extranodally, including in the pancreas. It may form a pancreatic head mass and cause biliary obstruction; histology commonly shows spindle to ovoid cells in whorled/storiform patterns with admixed lymphocytes and immunoreactivity for follicular dendritic-cell markers such as CD21, CD23, and CD35.
symptoms_in_common: Pancreatic head mass causing obstructive jaundice
Cholestatic liver-test pattern with elevated conjugated bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, and gamma-glutamyltransferase
Normal LDH and beta2-microglobulin, which does not strongly support aggressive systemic lymphoma
Histologic appearance of a spindle/ovoid-cell tumor with inflammatory-cell admixture
Immunohistochemical pattern suggestive of a dendritic-cell neoplasm
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated CA19-9, although this can occur secondarily from biliary obstruction
Very acute 1-week presentation, as these tumors may be clinically silent until large

data.description: The most common pancreatic malignancy, usually arising in the pancreatic head and producing extrahepatic biliary obstruction. CA19-9 may be markedly elevated, especially in the setting of obstructive jaundice.
symptoms_not_in_common: Histology does not appear to show typical infiltrating malignant gland formation and desmoplastic adenocarcinoma
Immunohistochemical appearance is more suggestive of a non-epithelial spindle/lymphoid-associated neoplasm
No reported weight loss, anorexia, abdominal pain, or palpable gallbladder

data.description: An uncommon extranodal lymphoma centered in the pancreas, most often diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. It can mimic pancreatic carcinoma and can cause jaundice when located in the pancreatic head.
symptoms_in_common: Tumor histology with a prominent cellular and lymphoid-appearing component
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal LDH and beta2-microglobulin, which are less supportive of clinically significant aggressive lymphoma
Marked CA19-9 elevation, which is less characteristic of lymphoma except when caused by biliary obstruction
No B symptoms such as fever, drenching night sweats, or weight loss
Histologic and immunohistochemical features may favor follicular dendritic cell sarcoma rather than a conventional B-cell lymphoma

data.description: A malignant tumor of the distal common bile duct that produces progressive extrahepatic biliary obstruction and may appear as, or be difficult to distinguish from, a pancreatic head lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Painless or minimally painful obstructive jaundice
symptoms_not_in_common: Imaging appears to demonstrate a pancreatic parenchymal mass rather than a primary bile-duct lesion
Histology does not appear to show typical malignant biliary glandular epithelium
No reported bile-duct wall thickening or dominant ductal stricture

diagnoses.name: Primary pancreatic T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma
diagnoses.title: T-cell/histiocyte rich large B-cell lymphoma

data.description: 80-year-old woman with 6-month history of slowly increasing asymptomatic lumbar subcutaneous mass. History of chronic renal failure requiring dialysis three times weekly for 10 years. Poor compliance with phosphate-binding medications and dietary restrictions. Physical exam showed firm, immobile subcutaneous nodule measuring 9 cm in major axis. Laboratory findings: serum calcium 1.95 mmol/L (normal: 2.05-2.55), serum phosphorus 3.3 mmol/L (normal: 0.74-1.52), serum intact parathyroid hormone 142 ng/L (normal: 10-65), serum creatinine 787 μmol/L (normal: 53-106).

data.diagnosis: Uremic tumoral calcinosis (secondary tumoral calcinosis due to chronic renal failure)
data.description: Periarticular or subcutaneous deposition of lobulated calcium-phosphate material, most often occurring in patients on long-term dialysis with hyperphosphatemia and secondary hyperparathyroidism.
symptoms_in_common: Long-term hemodialysis for chronic renal failure
Poor adherence to phosphate-binding medication and dietary phosphate restriction
Elevated intact parathyroid hormone consistent with secondary hyperparathyroidism
Slowly enlarging painless firm subcutaneous mass
Large lobulated calcified periarticular/subcutaneous mass on CT
Increased uptake in the calcified lesion on bone scintigraphy
symptoms_not_in_common: Mild hypocalcemia is less typical than normal or elevated calcium-phosphate product, although it can occur in dialysis patients
Lumbar/iliac location is less common than the hips, elbows, shoulders, hands, or feet

data.diagnosis: Calcinosis cutis secondary to chronic kidney disease
data.description: Deposition of insoluble calcium salts in the skin or subcutaneous tissue, often related to abnormal calcium-phosphate metabolism in renal failure.
symptoms_not_in_common: The very large 9 cm lobulated mass is more characteristic of tumoral calcinosis than typical calcinosis cutis
No reported skin ulceration, chalky discharge, inflammation, or multiple smaller cutaneous lesions
No known connective-tissue disease such as dermatomyositis, systemic sclerosis, or lupus

data.description: A severe dialysis-associated disorder involving calcification and thrombosis of small dermal and subcutaneous vessels, usually causing painful ischemic skin lesions and necrosis.
symptoms_in_common: End-stage chronic kidney disease on long-term dialysis
symptoms_not_in_common: Mass is painless rather than severely painful
No livedo reticularis, purpura, skin necrosis, ulceration, or black eschar
The lesion is a discrete large calcified mass rather than diffuse vascular/dermal calcification
Slow 6-month enlargement is not typical of calciphylaxis

data.description: Formation of mature bone within soft tissue, often after trauma, surgery, neurologic injury, or prolonged immobilization.
symptoms_in_common: Calcified or ossified lesion on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of trauma, surgery, neurologic injury, or local inflammation
The lesion is described as subcutaneous rather than intramuscular
Severe hyperphosphatemia and long-term dialysis strongly favor metastatic calcium-phosphate deposition instead
Imaging appearance of multilobulated amorphous calcification is more typical of tumoral calcinosis than organized peripheral ossification

data.description: 47-year-old female presented to emergency department after being hit while skiing by another skier at high speed from behind. Immediate pain and marked general swelling of the knee joint occurred after impact. Unable to bear weight. Physical exam showed neurovascularly intact limb with no broken skin. No relevant medical, family, or social history.

data.diagnosis: Lateral tibial plateau fracture (split-depression type, Schatzker II)
data.description: An intra-articular fracture of the lateral upper tibia involving a vertical split and depression of the lateral tibial plateau, typically caused by high-energy valgus or axial loading trauma.
symptoms_in_common: Radiographic fracture involving the lateral tibial plateau with articular surface depression
symptoms_not_in_common: No neurovascular deficit
No open skin wound

data.description: A high-energy intra-articular fracture involving both medial and lateral tibial plateaus, often associated with substantial swelling and potential ligamentous or neurovascular injury.
symptoms_not_in_common: Imaging predominantly demonstrates lateral plateau involvement rather than clear fractures of both condyles
No neurovascular compromise
No open injury

data.diagnosis: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury with hemarthrosis
data.description: A tear of the anterior cruciate ligament caused by pivoting, hyperextension, or high-energy knee trauma; it can produce immediate swelling from bleeding into the joint and difficulty bearing weight.
symptoms_in_common: Immediate marked knee swelling consistent with hemarthrosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Radiographs demonstrate a tibial plateau fracture, which better explains the presentation
No reported knee instability or giving-way sensation
No reported popping sensation at the time of injury

diagnoses.name: Tibial plateau fracture
diagnoses.title: Fracture of lower end of tibia[Tibial Plateau]

data.description: A 52-year-old woman presented with complaints of anal pain, constipation, and tenesmus for 3 months before being referred to the hospital. There were no relevant prior illnesses. Rectal digital examination revealed a 6-cm smooth elastic mass on the rectal posterior left side 2 cm from the anal verge. Colonoscopy showed a rectal submucosal bulging. Computed tomography scan and magnetic resonance imaging confirmed the presence of a single 6-cm well-delimited mass, compressing and infiltrating the wall of the medium to low rectum.

A mesenchymal tumor arising from interstitial cells of Cajal or related precursor cells, usually composed of spindle cells and often associated with KIT or PDGFRA mutations. Rectal GISTs commonly present as submucosal rectal masses.
symptoms_in_common: Well-delimited 6-cm mass involving the rectal wall
symptoms_not_in_common: No gastrointestinal bleeding was reported
No weight loss or systemic symptoms were reported

data.description: A benign smooth-muscle tumor of the rectum that usually appears as a well-circumscribed submucosal mass composed of bland spindle cells. Larger lesions may cause obstructive symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Well-delimited lesion on CT and MRI
Spindle-cell morphology consistent with smooth-muscle differentiation
symptoms_not_in_common: Imaging description of wall infiltration is less typical for a benign leiomyoma
A 6-cm size is relatively large for a benign rectal leiomyoma

data.description: A malignant smooth-muscle tumor of the rectum that may form a large intramural or submucosal mass and produce obstructive bowel symptoms. Histology typically shows atypia, increased mitotic activity, and/or necrosis.
symptoms_in_common: Possible infiltration of the rectal wall
symptoms_not_in_common: The mass was described as smooth, elastic, and well delimited, which can favor a less aggressive lesion
No rectal bleeding, weight loss, or metastatic disease was reported
No marked cellular atypia, tumor necrosis, or high mitotic activity was described

data.description: A rare mesenchymal tumor derived from peripheral nerve sheath cells. It can occur as a slow-growing, well-circumscribed submucosal colorectal mass and may cause pain or obstructive symptoms when large.
symptoms_not_in_common: Rectal wall infiltration is less characteristic of a benign schwannoma
The clinical and molecular evaluation pattern may be more suggestive of GIST than schwannoma
No lymphoid cuffing or other classic schwannoma histologic features were described

diagnoses.name: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
diagnoses.title: Gastrointestinal stromal tumour of unspecified gastrointestinal sites

data.description: Two-year-four-month-old female born at 39 weeks by Cesarean section for placental failure, with intrauterine growth restriction and very low birth weight/length/head circumference. She developed bilateral severe sensorineural hearing loss diagnosed at 3 months and received hearing aids at 4 months. During infancy, she had persistent short stature and low weight (<3rd percentile) with normal psychomotor development; MRI of the CNS was normal. Physical features included triangular face, prominent forehead, small chin, hypoplastic nasal alae, large mouth with thin downturned lips, low-set ears, deeply set eyes, delayed teething, microdontia, delayed bone age, thin wrinkled skin with visible vessels, and lipoatrophy. Genetic testing found a de novo heterozygous PIK3R1 variant c.1956dupT (p.Lys653*).

A rare autosomal dominant disorder caused by pathogenic PIK3R1 variants, characterized by intrauterine growth restriction, postnatal short stature, partial lipodystrophy, progeroid facial appearance, delayed dentition, and insulin-resistance risk.
symptoms_in_common: De novo heterozygous PIK3R1 c.1956dupT (p.Lys653*) variant
Intrauterine growth restriction and very low birth weight
Persistent postnatal short stature and low weight
Triangular face with prominent forehead and small chin
Deeply set eyes and hypoplastic nasal alae
Large mouth with thin downturned lips
Thin wrinkled skin with visible vessels
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral severe congenital sensorineural hearing loss is not a classic defining feature, although it has been reported in some affected individuals

data.description: A growth-restriction syndrome usually caused by abnormalities involving chromosome 11p15 or maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 7, featuring prenatal and postnatal growth failure, triangular facies, prominent forehead, and feeding difficulties.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent short stature and low weight
symptoms_not_in_common: De novo pathogenic PIK3R1 variant
Generalized or partial lipoatrophy
Thin wrinkled skin with prominent vessels
Hypoplastic nasal alae
Large mouth with thin downturned lips
Delayed teething with microdontia
Bilateral severe sensorineural hearing loss

data.description: A rare congenital progeroid disorder characterized by severe prenatal and postnatal growth failure, loss of subcutaneous fat, thin aged-appearing skin, sparse hair, and characteristic craniofacial features; it is typically associated with biallelic POLR3A variants.
symptoms_in_common: Thin wrinkled skin with visible blood vessels
symptoms_not_in_common: De novo heterozygous PIK3R1 variant rather than biallelic POLR3A variants
Normal psychomotor development is less typical in severe neonatal progeroid syndromes
Triangular facial appearance is more characteristic of SHORT syndrome
Microdontia is not a defining feature
Bilateral severe sensorineural hearing loss is not a typical core feature

data.description: A genetic lipodystrophy syndrome with near-complete absence of adipose tissue from birth or infancy, prominent musculature, metabolic complications including insulin resistance and hypertriglyceridemia, and accelerated growth in many patients.
symptoms_not_in_common: Intrauterine growth restriction is not typical
Short stature and delayed bone age are not typical
Triangular face with prominent forehead and small chin is not characteristic
Thin wrinkled progeroid skin is not typical
Delayed teething and microdontia are not typical
De novo PIK3R1 variant supports SHORT syndrome instead
Bilateral severe sensorineural hearing loss is not typical

data.description: A progeroid lipodystrophy disorder, most often caused by LMNA or ZMPSTE24 variants, characterized by growth retardation, craniofacial abnormalities including mandibular hypoplasia, skin changes, lipodystrophy, and skeletal abnormalities such as clavicular and acro-osteolysis changes.
symptoms_not_in_common: Intrauterine growth restriction is less typical
Triangular face with hypoplastic nasal alae and large downturned mouth more strongly suggests SHORT syndrome
No reported clavicular hypoplasia or acro-osteolysis
No reported joint contractures or skeletal deformities
De novo heterozygous PIK3R1 variant rather than LMNA or ZMPSTE24 variants
Bilateral severe sensorineural hearing loss is not typical

data.description: 56-year-old Ethiopian male with a history of type A thymoma resected 3 years earlier, presenting with persistent fever, chills, cough, night sweats, weight loss, fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, and recurrent sinopulmonary infections intermittently responsive to antibiotics, often recurring with diarrheal IBS-D symptoms. On admission, he had low-grade fever with otherwise normal vital signs and room-air oxygen saturation. Labs showed lymphopenia, mild anemia, low albumin/protein, and poor immune responses, including absent pneumococcal serotype antibody response and reduced lymphocyte proliferation to tetanus and candida. Extensive infectious workup was negative except for induced sputum positive for Pneumocystis jiroveci and Moraxella catarrhalis. Biopsy of a cavitary lesion showed ulceration with acute and chronic inflammation, with negative fungal stains, negative cultures, and no malignancy.

A rare combined immunodeficiency associated with thymoma, characterized by hypogammaglobulinemia, impaired B-cell and T-cell function, recurrent bacterial respiratory infections, and opportunistic infections.
symptoms_in_common: Reduced lymphocyte proliferation to tetanus and candida
symptoms_not_in_common: Diarrheal IBS-D symptoms are not a defining feature, although chronic diarrhea may occur with infections or autoimmune disease

data.description: A primary antibody deficiency disorder causing reduced immunoglobulin function, poor vaccine responses, recurrent bacterial respiratory infections, bronchiectasis, and sometimes gastrointestinal disease.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent response and recurrence after antibiotics
Chronic cough and dyspnea on exertion
Chronic diarrhea or IBS-like gastrointestinal symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: Prior thymoma is more specifically associated with Good syndrome
Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia is less typical in isolated CVID
Markedly reduced T-cell proliferation is less typical in classic CVID

data.description: An opportunistic fungal pneumonia occurring in patients with impaired cellular immunity, typically causing fever, nonproductive cough, progressive dyspnea, and diffuse pulmonary infiltrates.
symptoms_in_common: Induced sputum positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii
symptoms_not_in_common: Recurrent bacterial sinopulmonary infections over a prolonged period
Moraxella catarrhalis infection
Cavitary lung lesion is unusual for PJP
Bronchiectasis is not a typical primary manifestation
Diarrheal IBS-D symptoms

data.description: A chronic Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection that can cause constitutional symptoms, chronic cough, and cavitary pulmonary lesions, particularly in people from regions where tuberculosis is endemic or in immunocompromised patients.
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative extensive infectious evaluation and negative cultures
Positive Pneumocystis jirovecii sputum testing provides an alternate cause of pulmonary symptoms
Poor pneumococcal vaccine response is not explained by tuberculosis
Recurrent Moraxella-associated sinopulmonary infections are not typical of tuberculosis
Reduced lymphocyte responses to tetanus and candida suggest an underlying immune defect rather than tuberculosis alone

data.diagnosis: Chronic suppurative airway disease with bronchiectasis secondary to immunodeficiency
data.description: Permanent bronchial dilation and airway damage caused by recurrent infections, resulting in chronic cough, recurrent bacterial exacerbations, dyspnea, fatigue, and persistent inflammatory lung abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent improvement with antibiotics followed by recurrence
Imaging appearance compatible with bronchiectatic airway changes
Underlying impaired antibody and cellular immune responses
symptoms_not_in_common: Night sweats and substantial weight loss are not typical of uncomplicated bronchiectasis
Pneumocystis jirovecii infection indicates additional cellular immunodeficiency
Cavitary lesion is not typical of uncomplicated bronchiectasis
Diarrheal IBS-D symptoms are not directly caused by bronchiectasis

data.description: A 26-year-old man presented with a firm, nontender palpable lymph node in his left cervical area. The patient had no specific past medical history. On admission, his vital signs were stable with blood pressure 120/80 mmHg, pulse rate 80/min, respiratory rate 24/min, and body temperature 36.5°C. Routine laboratory investigations showed a normal complete blood count, serum chemical tests, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). Serologic tests for cytomegalovirus, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis of mycobacteria yielded negative results. Serum immunoglobulin levels were within normal ranges: IgG 1,680 mg/dL (normal 700-1,700 mg/dL), IgA 117 mg/dL (normal 70-400 mg/dL), IgM 129 mg/dL (normal 40-230 mg/dL), and IgE 33.8 IU/mL (normal 0-100 IU/mL). The patient had no history of fever during the clinical course.

A benign, self-limited lymphadenitis usually affecting young adults, characterized by cervical lymphadenopathy and histology showing patchy necrosis, karyorrhectic debris, histiocytes, plasmacytoid dendritic cells, and absence of neutrophils.
symptoms_in_common: Normal complete blood count and ESR can occur
Negative infectious testing for HIV, cytomegalovirus, and mycobacteria
No fever may occur in atypical or mild cases
Mediastinal lymphadenopathy can rarely accompany cervical disease
Histologic appearance is consistent with necrotizing histiocytic lymphadenitis
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of fever, which is common in typical cases
No reported leukopenia
No reported rash, fatigue, or upper-respiratory symptoms

data.diagnosis: Rosai-Dorfman disease (sinus histiocytosis with massive lymphadenopathy)
data.description: A non-Langerhans-cell histiocytic disorder that commonly presents with painless bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy and may involve mediastinal or extranodal sites; lymph nodes show abundant S100-positive histiocytes with emperipolesis.
symptoms_in_common: Painless firm cervical lymph node enlargement
Normal routine laboratory results may occur in localized disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Lymphadenopathy is unilateral rather than the more typical massive bilateral cervical involvement
No fever
No elevated ESR
No leukocytosis, anemia, hypergammaglobulinemia, or polyclonal immunoglobulin elevation
Histology described by necrotizing lymphadenitis would be less typical than sinus histiocytosis with emperipolesis

data.description: A lymphoid malignancy that often affects young adults and commonly presents with painless cervical and mediastinal lymphadenopathy; diagnosis requires identification of Reed-Sternberg cells in an appropriate inflammatory background.
symptoms_in_common: Mediastinal lymph node enlargement on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No night sweats
No unintentional weight loss
Normal ESR and routine blood tests
Histology appears to favor histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis rather than Reed-Sternberg-cell-containing lymphoma

data.description: Mycobacterial infection of lymph nodes, usually causing chronic cervical lymphadenopathy with granulomatous inflammation and caseous necrosis; mediastinal lymphadenopathy may also occur.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic painless lymph node enlargement can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Mycobacterial PCR is negative
No fever
Normal ESR
No constitutional symptoms such as weight loss or night sweats
No reported granulomas or caseating necrosis on histology
Normal blood studies

data.description: 26-year-old pregnant woman at 32 weeks’ gestation with monochorionic diamniotic twins, history of childhood asthma, obesity, anxiety, depression, gestational diabetes, polyhydramnios in one fetus, and two prior uncomplicated pregnancies. Three weeks before presentation, after her children had an ear infection and sore throat, she developed conjunctival erythema with green drainage, then nonproductive cough, sore throat, ear pain, and new leg edema. One week before admission, she developed progressive right leg pain, followed 5 days later by left leg tenderness, worsening bilateral leg edema, and severe coughing episodes. Initial exam showed tachycardia and pitting leg edema without erythema or warmth; later she had expiratory wheezes. She then developed sudden severe crushing chest pain, became unresponsive and pulseless, and was found in monomorphic ventricular tachycardia, leading to cardiac arrest.
Acute inflammation of the heart muscle, often following a viral respiratory infection, causing severe ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmias, cardiogenic shock, and potentially sudden cardiac arrest.
symptoms_in_common: Recent upper respiratory illness with conjunctivitis, sore throat, cough, and ear pain
Imaging findings consistent with pulmonary edema and pleural effusions
Apparent absence of obstructive coronary disease on coronary angiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Pregnancy with monochorionic diamniotic twins
Gestational diabetes
Polyhydramnios
Initial focal right-leg pain followed by left-leg tenderness

data.description: Pregnancy-associated systolic heart failure occurring during the last month of pregnancy or in the months after delivery, characterized by reduced left-ventricular function, pulmonary congestion, edema, and arrhythmias.
symptoms_in_common: Cough and wheezing that may reflect pulmonary congestion
Pulmonary edema and pleural effusions on imaging
Ventricular tachycardia and cardiac arrest can occur in severe disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent preceding conjunctivitis with green drainage
Sore throat and ear pain suggesting a viral prodrome
Sudden crushing chest pain is less typical than progressive dyspnea and orthopnea
Initial unilateral leg pain

data.description: Obstruction of pulmonary arterial blood flow by thrombus, commonly arising from deep venous thrombosis. Pregnancy, obesity, and reduced venous flow are major risk factors; massive embolism can cause shock and cardiac arrest.
symptoms_not_in_common: Three-week viral-type prodrome with conjunctivitis, sore throat, and ear pain
Monomorphic ventricular tachycardia, whereas massive pulmonary embolism more often causes pulseless electrical activity
Wheezing is not a classic presenting feature
Imaging findings suggesting cardiogenic pulmonary edema and pleural effusions rather than a pulmonary arterial filling defect

data.diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome due to pregnancy-associated spontaneous coronary artery dissection
data.description: A nonatherosclerotic tear or intramural hematoma of a coronary artery that may occur during late pregnancy or the postpartum period, causing myocardial ischemia, infarction, ventricular arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac arrest.
symptoms_not_in_common: Recent viral respiratory and conjunctival illness
Several days of progressive bilateral edema and cough before the event
Leg pain and tenderness
Normal-appearing coronary angiography would argue against this diagnosis
Pulmonary edema may occur after a large infarction but is not the usual initial presentation

data.description: 73-year-old man with 2 days of worsening weakness, lethargy, chills, diarrhea, decreased oral intake, progressive confusion/irritability, and near-catatonia with reduced responsiveness. He also had recurrent epistaxis and chest/left arm pain. Past history included diabetes mellitus, atrial fibrillation, diastolic heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, prior exudative pericardial effusion that resolved spontaneously, hyperlipidemia, pancytopenia, obstructive sleep apnea, GERD, and headaches. He had epistaxis since childhood, with family history of recurrent epistaxis in his mother and daughter. On exam, he was somnolent but arousable, oriented with waxing and waning attention, had dry mucous membranes, dried blood around the nares, multiple facial/lip/trunk telangiectasias, nonblanching cherry angiomas on the chest, irregularly irregular heart sounds, a liver edge palpable 2 cm below the right costal margin, and chronic venous insufficiency changes in the legs.

An autosomal-dominant vascular malformation disorder characterized by recurrent spontaneous epistaxis, mucocutaneous telangiectasias, and arteriovenous malformations in organs such as the liver, lungs, brain, and gastrointestinal tract.
symptoms_in_common: Family history of recurrent epistaxis in his mother and daughter
Multiple telangiectasias on the face, lips, and trunk
Possible hepatic vascular malformations on Doppler ultrasound and CT
Chronic anemia/pancytopenia history that may be exacerbated by recurrent bleeding
History of pulmonary hypertension and heart failure, which can occur with high-output states from hepatic arteriovenous shunting
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute diarrhea
Chills
Decreased oral intake
Acute waxing-and-waning confusion and near-catatonia
Chest and left arm pain

data.diagnosis: Hepatic arteriovenous malformations due to hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
data.description: Abnormal direct connections between hepatic arteries, portal veins, and/or hepatic veins. In HHT, these can produce enlarged tortuous hepatic vessels, arterioportal shunting, portal hypertension, high-output cardiac failure, and less commonly hepatic encephalopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging findings consistent with abnormal hepatic vascular channels and arteriovenous shunting
Telangiectasias and lifelong epistaxis supporting underlying HHT
symptoms_not_in_common: Diarrhea
Chills
Dry mucous membranes from poor intake
Chest and left arm pain
Acute confusion is possible if severe shunting causes encephalopathy but is not a common initial manifestation

data.diagnosis: Hepatic encephalopathy from portosystemic shunting associated with hepatic vascular malformations
data.description: A neuropsychiatric syndrome caused by impaired detoxification of gut-derived substances, often including ammonia, when blood bypasses functional hepatic metabolism through portosystemic shunts. Hepatic vascular malformations can create such shunting even without classic cirrhosis.
symptoms_in_common: Possible hepatic vascular shunting on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Lifelong recurrent epistaxis
Mucocutaneous telangiectasias
Family history of epistaxis
Chills
Diarrhea
Chest and left arm pain
Dried blood around the nares

data.description: A 7-month-old female infant presented with a 2-month history of brown macules on the back and thighs, without prodromal erythema or trauma. Her birth history was unremarkable, and her growth and development were normal. Family history was unremarkable. Physical examination revealed 7 sharply marginated, irregularly shaped, polymorphic hyperpigmented macules of 10 to 15 mm in diameter, without scales, on the back and thighs. The hyperpigmented macules were of orange hue, with unevenness of the pigmentation. Vital signs were normal. There was no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly. Laboratory test results, including complete blood cell count, liver function tests, and renal function, were normal.
A common pediatric form of mastocytosis caused by increased mast cells in the skin, producing tan, brown, or orange macules that may become red, swollen, or itchy after rubbing (Darier sign).
symptoms_in_common: Multiple sharply demarcated brown-orange hyperpigmented macules
Lesions on the trunk and thighs
Normal blood count, liver tests, and renal tests
Image appearance suggestive of a wheal-and-flare response after friction
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported pruritus
No reported flushing, blistering, diarrhea, or other mast-cell mediator symptoms
No explicitly documented Darier sign

data.description: A benign non-Langerhans-cell histiocytic disorder of infancy and childhood that usually causes solitary or multiple yellow, orange, red-brown papules or nodules.
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesions are flat macules rather than papules or nodules
Lesions are predominantly on the back and thighs rather than the typical head and neck distribution
No yellow papular or nodular appearance
Multiple lesions are less typical than a solitary lesion

data.description: A clonal proliferation of Langerhans cells that can affect the skin alone or occur as part of multisystem disease; skin lesions may be red-brown papules, crusted lesions, or seborrheic dermatitis-like eruptions.
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesions are macules without papules, crusting, erosion, or scaling
No scalp or flexural seborrheic-type eruption
No lymphadenopathy
No hepatosplenomegaly
Normal blood count and liver function tests
Normal growth and development

data.description: Benign, sharply bordered hyperpigmented macules caused by increased melanin; multiple lesions can occur in neurocutaneous syndromes such as neurofibromatosis type 1.
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesions are orange-brown with uneven pigmentation rather than uniformly light-brown
Irregular polymorphic shapes rather than typically smooth-edged oval lesions
New onset over 2 months rather than usually present from birth or early infancy
Image suggests inducible erythema or swelling, which is not typical

data.description: Residual darkening of the skin after inflammation, trauma, insect bites, dermatitis, or other skin injury; pigmentation may persist after the original eruption resolves.
symptoms_in_common: No scale at the time of examination
Normal systemic examination and laboratory results
symptoms_not_in_common: No preceding erythema, rash, trauma, or insect-bite history
Orange hue and apparent wheal response are less typical
Multiple similar lesions developing without a recognized inflammatory trigger

data.description: A 17-year-old girl presented to the emergency department with constipation and bloodless vomiting for 3 weeks. The vomiting worsened after food ingestion. The patient was exhausted and underweight, although she did not suffer abdominal pain. At admission, the patient had unwillingly lost 10 kg over 2 years, resulting in a body mass index of 14. During this period, she started prevention medicine due to a loss of menstruation. The patient had no prior medical or surgical history. Blood tests revealed an increased sed rate (ESR) of 33 (normal range: 2-20) as the only outlier. A contrast-enhanced CT was ordered based on the acute exacerbating of vomiting and constipation, with ileus as the tentative diagnosis.

Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and aorta, usually after marked loss of retroperitoneal fat from severe weight loss. The CT measurements show a markedly narrowed aortomesenteric angle and distance with proximal gastric/duodenal dilatation, supporting this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Severe underweight status with BMI of 14
Imaging evidence of gastric and proximal duodenal dilatation
Narrowed aortomesenteric angle and distance on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of abdominal pain
Mildly elevated ESR

data.diagnosis: Anorexia nervosa or severe restrictive eating disorder
data.description: A psychiatric eating disorder characterized by inadequate caloric intake, low body weight, and endocrine consequences of malnutrition. Severe weight loss can precipitate superior mesenteric artery syndrome by reducing the mesenteric fat cushion.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly low body mass index of 14
Progressive 10 kg weight loss over 2 years
Vomiting may occur in advanced malnutrition or secondary to gastrointestinal dysmotility/obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported fear of weight gain
No reported body-image disturbance
No reported intentional food restriction or compensatory behaviors
Acute postprandial vomiting with CT-confirmed duodenal compression is not explained by an eating disorder alone
Mildly elevated ESR is not typical

data.description: Partial or complete blockage of the upper small bowel causing retained gastric contents, postprandial vomiting, and reduced bowel movements. In this case, the likely mechanical cause is superior mesenteric artery compression of the duodenum.
symptoms_in_common: Marked gastric and proximal duodenal dilatation on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No abdominal pain
No history of abdominal surgery or adhesions
Long-standing severe weight loss and amenorrhea are not typical consequences of an acute bowel obstruction
Mildly elevated ESR is nonspecific

data.description: 41-year-old man with morbid obesity, hyperlipidemia, and prior cholecystectomy, status post Roux-en-Y gastric bypass 8 years earlier. He initially presented with epigastric and left upper quadrant pain worsened by eating, with abdominal tenderness but no rebound or guarding, and normal basic labs. He later developed 4 months of foul-smelling watery diarrhea 6–7 times daily with visible food particles, pale floating stools, increased flatus, and daily feculent eructation. On later emergency presentation, he had progressive weakness, myalgias, muscle cramps, and significant weight loss from 95.3 kg to 72.6 kg, and appeared cachectic with dry mucous membranes, feculent breath, and decreased skin turgor.

data.diagnosis: Gastrocolic fistula involving the Roux-en-Y gastric pouch and transverse colon
data.description: An abnormal communication between the gastric pouch and colon, allowing ingested food to pass directly into the colon. This is a rare late complication of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and can result from marginal ulceration, chronic inflammation, or surgical complications. The contrast study demonstrates a fistulous tract from the gastric pouch to the transverse/descending colon.
symptoms_in_common: Visible undigested food particles in stool
Postprandial epigastric and left upper quadrant abdominal pain
Dehydration signs including dry mucous membranes and decreased skin turgor
Weakness, myalgias, and muscle cramps consistent with malnutrition and electrolyte loss
symptoms_not_in_common: No rebound tenderness or guarding
Normal basic laboratory tests early in the course

data.diagnosis: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass
data.description: Excessive bacterial colonization of the small intestine, often promoted by altered anatomy or intestinal stasis after bariatric surgery. It can cause malabsorption, diarrhea, gas, and nutritional deficiencies.
symptoms_in_common: Weakness and muscle cramps related to malabsorption or nutritional deficiency
History of altered gastrointestinal anatomy after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass
symptoms_not_in_common: Daily feculent eructation
Feculent breath
Visible food particles in stool suggesting rapid gastric-to-colonic transit
Imaging evidence of a direct fistula between the gastric pouch and colon
Severe watery diarrhea occurring 6–7 times daily due to direct colonic exposure to ingested food

data.description: Insufficient pancreatic digestive enzyme secretion causing fat malabsorption, steatorrhea, weight loss, and nutritional deficiencies. It can produce pale, floating, foul-smelling stools but does not explain the demonstrated gastric-colonic connection.
symptoms_in_common: Weakness and muscle cramps that may occur with malnutrition
symptoms_not_in_common: Feculent eructation and feculent breath
Postoperative imaging demonstrating a fistula from the gastric pouch to the transverse colon
Acute or progressive severe watery diarrhea from direct gastric-to-colonic transit
History strongly suggesting a late Roux-en-Y gastric bypass fistula complication
Postprandial left upper quadrant pain specifically associated with the fistulous process

data.description: A 20-year-old woman with a history of asthma presented to the emergency department with shortness of breath and sharp pains in her chest and neck. The pain worsened on deep inspiration. She had a cough producing small amounts of whitish sputum. She had experienced several previous asthma exacerbations and had not been using her inhalers regularly. On examination, her airway was patent with a generalized moderate wheeze in her chest, but no other obvious clinical signs. She could speak in full sentences and had normal oxygen saturations and temperature. She was mildly tachycardic and appeared slightly anxious. Blood tests showed a mild neutrophilia and elevated C reactive protein.

Air leaks into the mediastinum, usually after increased intrathoracic pressure from coughing, wheezing, or an asthma exacerbation. It commonly causes acute pleuritic chest pain with pain radiating to the neck.
symptoms_in_common: Sharp chest pain worsened by deep inspiration
Normal oxygen saturation despite chest pain and dyspnea
Chest radiograph findings suggestive of mediastinal air
symptoms_not_in_common: Whitish sputum production
Mild neutrophilia
Elevated C-reactive protein

data.description: An episode of worsening bronchospasm and airway inflammation causing wheeze, cough, chest tightness, and shortness of breath, often precipitated by poor adherence to inhaled therapy or respiratory infection.
symptoms_in_common: Ability to speak in full sentences and normal oxygen saturation, consistent with a non-severe exacerbation
symptoms_not_in_common: Sharp pleuritic chest pain
Neck pain
Pain worsened by deep inspiration

data.diagnosis: Viral bronchitis or lower respiratory tract infection
data.description: Inflammation of the bronchi, usually viral, causing cough, sputum production, wheeze, and sometimes triggering an asthma exacerbation.
symptoms_in_common: Cough with small amounts of whitish sputum
Possible asthma exacerbation triggered by respiratory infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Sharp chest and neck pain
Marked pleuritic quality of the pain
Normal temperature without systemic infective symptoms

data.description: Obstruction of pulmonary arterial blood flow by a thrombus, typically causing sudden dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, tachycardia, and occasionally cough.
symptoms_in_common: Sharp chest pain worsened by deep inspiration
Normal oxygen saturation can occur in smaller pulmonary emboli
symptoms_not_in_common: Generalized wheeze associated with poorly controlled asthma
Neck pain
Productive whitish sputum cough
No stated thromboembolic risk factors

data.description: Air in the pleural space causing partial or complete lung collapse, often presenting with sudden unilateral pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath. It can occur in patients with underlying lung disease, including asthma.
symptoms_not_in_common: Neck pain is less typical without extensive air leak
Generalized bilateral wheeze rather than reduced breath sounds on one side
Normal chest radiograph without a visible pleural line or lung collapse
Productive cough with whitish sputum

data.description: 47-year-old homeless man with 1 month of intermittent leg pain and pins-and-needles sensation, starting in the toes and gradually spreading to the shins. History includes 33 years of intravenous heroin use (current use), hepatitis C infection, hypertension, 52 pack-year smoking history, and rare alcohol use. No family history of neuropathy. Exam: afebrile, chronically ill-appearing, with elevated blood pressure; normal cardiac, pulmonary, abdominal, skin, and cranial nerve findings; normal strength and reflexes; unsteady gait with limited ambulation due to pain and decreased pinprick, light touch, and temperature sensation in ორივe lower extremities.

A nutritional deficiency syndrome caused by inadequate niacin or tryptophan intake, classically producing photosensitive dermatitis, diarrhea, neuropsychiatric symptoms, and peripheral neuropathy. The images are suggestive of pellagrous dermatitis, including a Casal necklace-like rash on the neck and symmetric acral dermatitis.
symptoms_in_common: Painful distal lower-extremity paresthesias beginning in the toes
Bilateral stocking-distribution loss of pinprick, light-touch, and temperature sensation
Unsteady gait due to painful sensory neuropathy
Symmetric rash involving the forearms/hands and neck in the supplied images
symptoms_not_in_common: No diarrhea reported
No confusion, dementia, depression, or other prominent neuropsychiatric symptoms reported
Normal skin examination in the written examination conflicts with the photographed dermatitis
Normal reflexes and strength are less typical in advanced nutritional neuropathy

data.diagnosis: Hepatitis C-associated mixed cryoglobulinemia with peripheral neuropathy
data.description: An immune-complex vasculitic disorder associated with chronic hepatitis C infection that can cause painful distal sensory neuropathy, purpura, arthralgia, renal disease, and systemic symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Skin lesions on the extremities could potentially represent vasculitic lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: No palpable purpura specifically described
No arthralgias reported
No renal symptoms, hematuria, edema, or hypertension-related renal findings reported
The neck and symmetric sun-exposed dermatitis shown in the images is not typical of cryoglobulinemic vasculitis
No systemic vasculitic symptoms such as fever or fatigue reported

data.diagnosis: Nutritional peripheral neuropathy due to thiamine deficiency (dry beriberi)
data.description: Thiamine deficiency, often related to poor nutrition, can cause a painful symmetric distal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, gait impairment, weakness, and reduced reflexes.
symptoms_in_common: High risk of poor nutritional intake due to homelessness
Symmetric distal leg pain and paresthesias
Distal sensory loss affecting both lower extremities
Gait instability and limited walking due to neuropathic pain
symptoms_not_in_common: No weakness reported
Reflexes are normal rather than reduced
No edema, heart failure, tachycardia, or other wet-beriberi findings
The photographed photosensitive neck and acral dermatitis is not characteristic of isolated thiamine deficiency
Rare alcohol use reduces, but does not eliminate, risk

data.description: Vitamin B6 deficiency can occur with malnutrition and may cause a length-dependent peripheral neuropathy with distal numbness, burning pain, and paresthesias; dermatitis and mucosal changes can also occur.
symptoms_in_common: Risk of malnutrition related to homelessness
Bilateral distal paresthesias and neuropathic pain
Gait difficulty caused by sensory symptoms
Dermatitis in the supplied images could occur with vitamin deficiency
symptoms_not_in_common: No cheilosis, glossitis, stomatitis, anemia, or seizures reported
The neck distribution resembling a Casal necklace is more characteristic of niacin deficiency
No known medication exposure strongly associated with B6 deficiency, such as isoniazid
Normal reflexes and strength are not the usual finding in more significant neuropathy

data.diagnosis: Heroin-associated toxic or nutritional length-dependent peripheral neuropathy
data.description: Chronic heroin use may be associated with peripheral neuropathy through toxic exposure, adulterants, repeated hypoxic injury, infections, or severe nutritional deficiency. It commonly presents with distal symmetric sensory complaints.
symptoms_in_common: Thirty-three-year history of intravenous heroin use with ongoing use
Painful pins-and-needles sensation beginning in the toes
Gradual spread of symptoms proximally toward the shins
Gait impairment due to neuropathic pain
symptoms_not_in_common: No temporal relationship between a specific heroin exposure and symptom onset reported
No altered mental status, weakness, respiratory event, or hypoxic episode reported
The photographed symmetric neck and forearm dermatitis is not directly typical of heroin toxicity
Normal reflexes and preserved strength may be less typical if neuropathy becomes advanced

data.description: 8-month-old male born at term, from a non-consanguineous family, with two prior admissions for bronchitis at 3 and 6 months of age; one episode was associated with severe neutropenia that resolved without treatment. He presented with respiratory distress, fever, and fatigue. Examination showed no palpable lymph nodes or tonsillar tissue, bilateral lung crackles, and diminished breath sounds. Chest X-ray revealed bilateral infiltrates without pleural effusion. Laboratory studies showed low IgG and IgM, very low IgA, and BTK c.494G>A (p.C165Y) mutation detected.

A primary immunodeficiency caused by pathogenic variants in the X-linked BTK gene, resulting in failure of B-cell maturation, markedly reduced immunoglobulins, and susceptibility to recurrent bacterial respiratory infections after maternal antibodies decline.
symptoms_in_common: Male infant with onset of recurrent respiratory infections in early infancy
Current pneumonia-like illness with fever, respiratory distress, crackles, diminished breath sounds, and bilateral pulmonary infiltrates
Absent palpable lymph nodes and tonsillar tissue
Low IgG and IgM with very low IgA
