Transient severe neutropenia, which can occur during infections in XLA

data.description: A group of severe inherited immunodeficiencies characterized by profound T-cell dysfunction, often with impaired B-cell and/or natural killer-cell function, leading to severe and recurrent infections in infancy.
symptoms_in_common: Early-onset recurrent lower respiratory tract infections
Absent or very small lymphoid tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: Confirmed pathogenic BTK mutation strongly supports X-linked agammaglobulinemia instead
No reported opportunistic infections, persistent thrush, chronic diarrhea, or failure to thrive
Transient rather than persistent neutropenia

data.description: A predominantly antibody-deficiency disorder causing low immunoglobulin levels, impaired antibody production, and recurrent sinopulmonary infections; it usually presents later in childhood or adulthood.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent bronchitis and lower respiratory tract infection
Bilateral pulmonary infiltrates compatible with respiratory infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation at 8 months is much earlier than typical for CVID
Absent tonsils and lymph nodes are more characteristic of X-linked agammaglobulinemia
Confirmed BTK mutation supports X-linked agammaglobulinemia rather than CVID
Male sex with an X-linked molecular diagnosis

data.description: A temporary delay in maturation of immunoglobulin production during infancy that may cause low IgG and recurrent respiratory infections but generally improves spontaneously.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked reduction of multiple immunoglobulin classes, including very low IgA and low IgM
Absent tonsillar and lymph node tissue
Confirmed BTK c.494G>A (p.C165Y) mutation
Severe recurrent infections requiring hospitalization
Episode of severe neutropenia

data.description: A 35-year-old patient presented to A&E with complaints of sudden onset pain in scrotum extending to perineum, scrotal swelling, loss of penile erection following sexual intercourse. On examination the patient had scrotal swelling and bruising at the base of the penis and scrotum, but no penile swelling.

data.diagnosis: Penile fracture (rupture of the right corpus cavernosum/tunica albuginea)
data.description: Acute tear of the tunica albuginea surrounding an erect corpus cavernosum, usually during sexual intercourse. The MRI demonstrates a defect in the right corpus cavernosum tunica albuginea near the penile base with associated soft-tissue hematoma extending into the scrotum.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden onset pain during or immediately after sexual intercourse
Bruising at the base of the penis
MRI evidence of a tunica albuginea defect in the right corpus cavernosum
symptoms_not_in_common: No penile shaft swelling; however, this can occur when a proximal tear decompresses into the scrotum or perineum

data.diagnosis: Proximal penile fracture with scrotal/perineal hematoma
data.description: A subtype of penile fracture in which a tear near the root of the penis allows blood to track into the perineum and scrotum, potentially producing marked scrotal bruising with relatively little visible penile shaft swelling.
symptoms_in_common: Pain centered in the scrotum and extending to the perineum
Bruising at the penile base and scrotum
MRI showing a proximal right corpus cavernosum tunica albuginea defect
MRI and ultrasound evidence of hematoma extending into the scrotal sac

data.diagnosis: Rupture of the superficial dorsal penile vein
data.description: Traumatic tearing of the superficial dorsal vein during intercourse can cause penile or scrotal bruising and swelling and may clinically resemble penile fracture, although the tunica albuginea remains intact.
symptoms_not_in_common: Immediate loss of erection is less typical
MRI evidence of a tunica albuginea defect in the corpus cavernosum is not expected
Pain extending prominently into the perineum is less characteristic

data.diagnosis: Testicular rupture or traumatic testicular hematoma
data.description: Testicular trauma may produce acute scrotal pain, swelling, and hematoma, often after blunt trauma. It is an important emergency differential diagnosis in patients with an acute swollen bruised scrotum.
symptoms_not_in_common: Symptoms began during sexual intercourse rather than direct scrotal blunt trauma
Immediate loss of penile erection is not typical
Bruising concentrated at the penile base is less typical
MRI demonstrates a corpus cavernosum tunica albuginea tear rather than disruption of the testicular tunica albuginea

data.description: 8-year-5-month-old male with severe global developmental delay and intellectual disability: full-term birth by vaginal delivery to consanguineous parents, birth weight 2.5 kg. He never achieved head control or independent sitting, learned to roll at age 5, and has never developed speech or communication. Examination showed a myopathic face, high-arched palate, nystagmus, generalized muscle weakness, marked hypotonia, absent deep tendon reflexes, knee and ankle contractures, and positive right Babinski sign with probable left Babinski sign. Serum CK was 1514 U/L.

An autosomal-recessive congenital muscular dystrophy caused by abnormal alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation. It combines severe hypotonia and muscle weakness with elevated CK, major developmental impairment, structural brain abnormalities, and ocular involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Severe congenital-onset global developmental delay and intellectual disability
Never achieved independent sitting or speech
Generalized muscle weakness and marked hypotonia
Contractures of the knees and ankles
Brain imaging abnormalities including ventriculomegaly/hydrocephalus and abnormal cerebral development
symptoms_not_in_common: Positive Babinski signs are less characteristic than the peripheral hypotonia and hyporeflexia, although they can occur with associated brain malformations
High-arched palate is not a defining feature

data.description: A severe congenital muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy characterized by profound developmental delay, congenital muscle weakness, markedly abnormal brain development such as cobblestone lissencephaly and hydrocephalus, and eye abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Likely autosomal-recessive setting with parental consanguinity
Severe motor impairment with inability to sit independently
Ventriculomegaly/hydrocephalus and severe structural brain abnormalities on imaging
Possible upper motor neuron signs such as Babinski responses due to cerebral malformation
symptoms_not_in_common: Survival to 8 years is less typical because classic Walker-Warburg syndrome often causes death in infancy or early childhood

The reported ocular findings are limited to nystagmus; Walker-Warburg syndrome often has more severe structural eye abnormalities such as microphthalmia, retinal dysplasia, cataracts, or congenital glaucoma
High-arched palate is not a core diagnostic feature

data.description: An alpha-dystroglycanopathy causing congenital muscular dystrophy with hypotonia, elevated CK, severe intellectual disability, brain malformations, and sometimes ocular abnormalities. Severity varies, with some affected children surviving into later childhood.
symptoms_in_common: Congenital or early-infantile severe muscle weakness and hypotonia
Marked global developmental delay and severe intellectual disability
Failure to achieve independent sitting and absent speech development
Brain structural abnormalities with ventricular enlargement and abnormal white matter/cortical development
Babinski signs may occur in association with central nervous system involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy is most frequently reported in individuals of Japanese ancestry, although it can rarely occur in other populations
Profound inability to obtain head control by age 8 is often more severe than the usual Fukuyama phenotype
High-arched palate is not typical

data.description: A 69-year-old male patient presented with lower abdominal pain. Physical examination revealed a flat abdomen without varicose veins, soft abdomen, with a palpable 3 cm×4 cm hard mass in the left lower abdomen, positive lower abdominal tenderness without rebound tenderness. Bowel sounds were normal at 4 times per minute. The patient had a history of cataracts for over one year, denied history of coronary heart disease, diabetes, hypertension, hepatitis, tuberculosis, or other acute or chronic infectious diseases. He denied food or drug allergies, trauma, blood transfusion history, or other surgical history.
A rare gland-forming malignancy arising from urachal remnants, usually located at the bladder dome or midline anterior pelvis and often presenting late as a lower abdominal or suprapubic mass.
symptoms_in_common: Pelvic mass near the superior/anterior aspect of the bladder on CT
Histology showing malignant gland-forming epithelial cells consistent with adenocarcinoma
symptoms_not_in_common: No hematuria was reported
No urinary frequency, urgency, dysuria, or other urinary symptoms were reported
Cataracts are not related to urachal adenocarcinoma

data.description: An uncommon bladder cancer composed of malignant glandular epithelial cells, usually arising from the bladder mucosa and potentially forming an invasive pelvic mass.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging evidence of a pelvic mass involving or adjacent to the bladder
symptoms_not_in_common: Gross or microscopic hematuria was not reported
No irritative urinary symptoms such as dysuria, frequency, or urgency were reported
Cataracts are not typical manifestations

data.diagnosis: Colorectal adenocarcinoma with pelvic extension or metastasis
data.description: A malignant glandular tumor of the colon or rectum that can present as a lower abdominal mass and may invade adjacent pelvic structures, including the bladder.
symptoms_in_common: Age is typical for colorectal cancer
Hard palpable mass in the left lower abdomen
Gland-forming adenocarcinoma morphology on tissue examination
symptoms_not_in_common: No change in bowel habits was reported
No rectal bleeding or melena was reported
No weight loss or anorexia was reported
Bowel sounds were normal
Cataracts are not related to colorectal adenocarcinoma

diagnoses.name: Bladder invasion
diagnoses.title: Mucinous cystic neoplasm with associated invasive carcinoma of other or unspecified parts of biliary tract[Gallbladder]

data.description: 32-year-old woman with a history of dissociative and depressive disorders, treated as an outpatient with multiple psychiatric medications, admitted to the emergency department for somnolence after a presumed suicide attempt. On arrival she was hemodynamically stable, afebrile, with normal oxygen saturation and respiratory rate, and had somnolence without other abnormal physical findings. Glasgow Coma Scale was 11/15. Laboratory studies showed severe metabolic acidosis with marked lactic acidosis and elevated anion and osmolal gaps.

Toxic alcohol ingestion, often intentional, that causes high anion-gap metabolic acidosis, increased osmolal gap early after ingestion, lactic-acidosis-like laboratory findings, and central nervous system depression.
symptoms_in_common: Somnolence with reduced Glasgow Coma Scale
Marked lactic acidosis or apparent lactic acidosis
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported acute kidney injury
No reported hypocalcemia
No reported calcium oxalate crystals in urine
No reported flank pain or renal symptoms

data.description: Toxic alcohol ingestion that produces an elevated osmolal gap followed by severe high anion-gap metabolic acidosis and neurologic depression; visual toxicity is a characteristic later finding.
symptoms_in_common: Severe metabolic acidosis with elevated anion gap
Initially normal oxygen saturation and respiratory rate can occur early
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported visual disturbance, blurred vision, photophobia, or blindness
No reported headache
No reported abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting
Marked lactic acidosis is less characteristic than formic acid-mediated acidosis

data.description: Propylene glycol is a solvent in some medications, particularly intravenous sedatives and certain liquid formulations. Accumulation or overdose can cause somnolence, increased osmolal gap, high anion-gap metabolic acidosis, and lactic acidosis.
symptoms_in_common: Somnolence and reduced level of consciousness
Exposure risk from multiple psychiatric medications or possible overdose
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported recent high-dose intravenous lorazepam, diazepam, phenobarbital, or other propylene-glycol-containing infusion
No reported renal dysfunction
No reported hypotension or arrhythmia

data.diagnosis: Metformin-associated lactic acidosis due to metformin overdose
data.description: Metformin overdose can cause profound lactic acidosis, altered mental status, and gastrointestinal symptoms, particularly after intentional ingestion or in the presence of renal impairment. An elevated osmolal gap is not usually a primary feature.
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated osmolal gap is not typical
No reported metformin use or diabetes history
No reported nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or abdominal pain
No reported renal failure

data.description: Isopropyl alcohol ingestion causes central nervous system depression and an elevated osmolal gap, often with ketosis. Unlike other toxic alcohols, it generally does not cause severe high anion-gap metabolic acidosis.
symptoms_in_common: Initially stable vital signs may be present
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe high anion-gap metabolic acidosis is not typical
Marked lactic acidosis is not typical
No reported ketosis or acetone odor
No reported abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, or hemorrhagic gastritis

data.description: 15-year-old girl with 6 weeks of lower abdominal pain that began midline, was sharp/crampy, worsened with movement, improved when lying down, and shifted to the right within 24 hours. Initial exam showed mild bilateral lower abdominal tenderness, greater on the right, with a soft, nondistended abdomen and no rebound or guarding; labs showed leukocytosis, anemia, and elevated C-reactive protein. Six weeks later, she returned with recurrent similar pain causing school absence, progressive abdominal enlargement over 2 weeks, and difficulty fitting into pants. She denied fever, gastrointestinal, urinary, or vaginal symptoms. She had no significant medical history, took no medications, and had normal growth and development; menarche had not occurred. Exam then showed a firm, distended right lower abdomen with mild tenderness and Tanner stage 4 pubertal development. Repeat labs showed worsening leukocytosis, anemia, and markedly elevated C-reactive protein.

data.diagnosis: Ovarian yolk sac tumor (endodermal sinus tumor)
data.description: A highly malignant ovarian germ-cell tumor that typically occurs in children and adolescents and can grow rapidly, often producing a large unilateral pelvic mass with hemorrhage and necrosis. Histology commonly shows reticular/microcystic patterns, Schiller-Duval bodies, and hyaline globules; serum alpha-fetoprotein is usually markedly elevated.
symptoms_in_common: Large right-sided pelvic or lower abdominal mass on examination and imaging
Imaging appearance of a large heterogeneous mass with hemorrhagic or necrotic components
symptoms_not_in_common: Six weeks of recurrent crampy pain before marked enlargement
Initial pain migrating from the midline to the right lower quadrant
No reported constitutional symptoms
No reported elevation of alpha-fetoprotein

data.diagnosis: Ovarian torsion associated with a large ovarian neoplasm
data.description: Twisting of the ovarian vascular pedicle causes venous congestion, edema, hemorrhage, infarction, and abdominal pain. Torsion frequently occurs in an enlarged ovary, including one enlarged by a benign or malignant ovarian tumor.
symptoms_in_common: Acute sharp crampy lower abdominal pain
Pain worse with movement and improved by lying down
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive abdominal enlargement over two weeks is more suggestive of an underlying mass than torsion alone
Pain recurring over six weeks is less typical than sudden severe persistent pain
Absence of nausea and vomiting
No fever
Anemia is not typical in uncomplicated torsion

data.description: A malignant ovarian germ-cell tumor composed of primitive germ cells, most often affecting adolescents and young women. It usually presents as a unilateral solid pelvic mass with abdominal pain or distension and may be associated with elevated lactate dehydrogenase.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked hemorrhagic and necrotic appearance is less typical than for yolk sac tumor
Markedly elevated C-reactive protein is not a characteristic presentation
Recurrent acute crampy pain suggests torsion or hemorrhage rather than dysgerminoma alone
No reported elevated lactate dehydrogenase
No reported constitutional symptoms

data.diagnosis: Juvenile granulosa cell tumor of the ovary
data.description: A sex cord-stromal ovarian tumor that occurs predominantly in children and adolescents. It may become large and can cause abdominal pain, distension, torsion, or hemorrhage; many tumors secrete estrogen and cause precocious puberty or abnormal uterine bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Large unilateral ovarian or pelvic mass
Possible hemorrhagic component within a large ovarian mass
symptoms_not_in_common: No menarche despite Tanner stage 4 development
No vaginal bleeding or other estrogen-excess manifestations
Marked leukocytosis and C-reactive protein elevation are not typical
Rapid aggressive enlargement with extensive necrosis is more suggestive of a malignant germ-cell tumor
No reported hormonal abnormalities

data.description: A malignant germ-cell tumor containing immature embryonal tissue, most commonly diagnosed in the first two decades of life. It may present with a rapidly enlarging unilateral adnexal mass, abdominal pain, torsion, rupture, or abdominal distension.
symptoms_not_in_common: No described fat, calcification, or tooth-like elements on imaging
Marked inflammatory-marker elevation is not typical
Leukocytosis is not a typical primary finding
Pathologic appearance is more suggestive of a yolk sac tumor than immature teratoma
No reported serum germ-cell tumor markers

diagnoses.name: Juvenile granulosa-cell tumor
diagnoses.title: Juvenile granulosa cell tumour unknown behaviour of unspecified site

data.description: 32-month-old Korean boy presented with irritability and fever. Born at 40 weeks gestation with 2.9kg birth weight via normal vaginal delivery to a healthy 28-year-old G3P2 mother. Had flexion deformity of both middle fingers at birth. Showed mild general hypotonia in early infancy with weak cry and poor sucking. History of epileptic seizures 6 times since age 15 months. Developmental delay: raised head at 7 months, sat at 26 months, not yet standing. Physical exam showed prognathism, low-set ears, small crashed nose, widely spaced incisors, round back. Demonstrated repeated stereotyped behavior like hitting chin with palm. Neurologic exam showed decreased muscle tone (grade IV/IV bilaterally) but normal deep tendon reflexes, no spasticity or pathologic reflexes, normal sensory function, and no meningeal signs.

data.diagnosis: Alpha-thalassemia X-linked intellectual disability syndrome (ATR-X syndrome)
data.description: A rare X-linked neurodevelopmental disorder caused by pathogenic variants in ATRX. It is characterized by severe developmental delay/intellectual disability, infantile hypotonia, distinctive facial appearance, skeletal or digital abnormalities, seizures in some patients, and alpha-thalassemia with hemoglobin H inclusions on supravital blood smear.
symptoms_in_common: Male child with severe global developmental delay
Early infantile hypotonia, weak cry, and poor sucking
Delayed head control and markedly delayed sitting/standing
Facial dysmorphism including low-set ears, depressed/small nasal bridge, prognathism, and widely spaced incisors
Congenital flexion deformities of the middle fingers
Blood-smear inclusions compatible with hemoglobin H inclusion bodies
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute fever
Irritability as the presenting acute complaint

data.diagnosis: ATR-16 syndrome (alpha-thalassemia intellectual disability syndrome due to 16p13.3 deletion)
data.description: A contiguous-gene deletion syndrome involving the alpha-globin gene cluster on chromosome 16p13.3. It causes alpha-thalassemia, developmental delay/intellectual disability, hypotonia, and variable craniofacial dysmorphism.
symptoms_in_common: Possible congenital limb or finger abnormalities
Blood-smear findings compatible with alpha-thalassemia/hemoglobin H inclusions
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe stereotyped chin-hitting behavior
Repeated epileptic seizures are less characteristic
Markedly severe motor delay may be more pronounced than typical
Acute fever
Irritability

data.diagnosis: Hemoglobin H disease (alpha-thalassemia with three affected alpha-globin genes)
data.description: A form of alpha-thalassemia caused by loss or inactivation of three alpha-globin genes. It produces excess beta-globin tetramers (hemoglobin H), which can appear as multiple punctate inclusions in red cells with supravital staining, often called golf-ball inclusions.
symptoms_in_common: Peripheral blood smear findings compatible with hemoglobin H inclusion bodies
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe global developmental delay
Infantile hypotonia
Weak cry and poor sucking
Epileptic seizures
Congenital flexion deformities of both middle fingers
Facial dysmorphism
Stereotyped chin-hitting behavior
Acute fever
Irritability

data.description: A neurodevelopmental disorder usually caused by a deletion of chromosome 17p11.2 or pathogenic variants in RAI1. It features developmental delay, hypotonia, distinctive facial features, behavioral dysregulation, repetitive behaviors, and self-injurious behavior.
symptoms_in_common: Stereotyped and potentially self-injurious behavior such as striking the chin
Seizures can occur in some affected children
symptoms_not_in_common: Hemoglobin H-like red-cell inclusions are not typical
Alpha-thalassemia is not typical
Congenital flexion deformity of both middle fingers is not a characteristic finding
Acute fever
Irritability

diagnoses.name: X-linked alpha-thalassemia/mental retardation syndrome
diagnoses.title: X-linked alpha thalassaemia with mental retardation

data.description: A previously healthy 58-year-old male presented with two weeks of lumbar pain and fever, accompanied by asthenia, anorexia, and recent weight loss of 3kg. He was a non-smoker with no drug abuse, recent travel, or animal contact history. On examination, he had a fever of 39.3°C with hemodynamic stability, bilateral painless swollen legs, and respiratory crackles on the right side. Laboratory tests showed hemoglobin 116 g/l, leukocyte count 33.3*109 cells/l, C-reactive protein 114.6mg/l, creatinine 56 μmol/l, elevated liver enzymes (AST 174 U/l, ALT 209 U/l, ALP 406 U/l, GGT 517 U/l), total bilirubin 76 μmol/l, conjugated bilirubin 66 μmol/l, and INR 1.38. Serology for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV were negative. Urinary sediment was unremarkable.

A bacterial infection causing pus collection within the iliopsoas muscle, often presenting with fever, back or flank pain, and marked inflammatory laboratory abnormalities. CT appearance is compatible with inflammatory enlargement/collection involving the left psoas region.
symptoms_in_common: CT findings suggestive of an iliopsoas inflammatory collection
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked conjugated hyperbilirubinemia
Prominent cholestatic liver-enzyme elevation
Bilateral painless leg swelling
Right-sided respiratory crackles

data.diagnosis: Pyogenic spondylodiscitis with secondary psoas abscess
data.description: Bacterial infection of an intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebral endplates that can extend into the psoas muscle and form an abscess. Staphylococcus aureus is a common cause.
symptoms_in_common: Constitutional symptoms including fatigue, anorexia, and weight loss
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported focal neurologic deficit
No reported radicular pain
No reported vertebral tenderness
Cholestatic jaundice and elevated liver enzymes are not typical primary features
Bilateral painless leg edema is not a typical presenting feature

data.diagnosis: Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia with metastatic infection
data.description: Bloodstream infection with Staphylococcus aureus can seed distant sites, causing vertebral osteomyelitis, psoas abscess, septic thrombophlebitis, pneumonia, or other deep abscesses.
symptoms_in_common: Lumbar pain suggesting a metastatic musculoskeletal focus
Right-sided respiratory crackles that could reflect pulmonary involvement
Systemic symptoms including asthenia, anorexia, and weight loss
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported skin or soft-tissue source of infection
No reported intravenous drug use
No reported cardiac murmur or embolic skin lesions
Severe cholestatic liver test abnormalities are not classic primary manifestations

data.diagnosis: Septic pelvic thrombophlebitis or iliac vein thrombosis secondary to psoas infection
data.description: Inflammation and thrombosis of pelvic or iliac veins can occur adjacent to an iliopsoas abscess or other deep pelvic infection. It may cause bilateral lower-extremity edema and persistent fever.
symptoms_in_common: Possible adjacent psoas/pelvic infection on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Anorexia and weight loss are nonspecific rather than typical thrombotic symptoms
Marked cholestatic hepatitis is not typical
Right-sided respiratory crackles are not typical unless there is pulmonary embolic or infectious involvement

data.diagnosis: Tuberculous spondylodiscitis (Pott disease) with psoas abscess
data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the spine can cause chronic back pain, constitutional symptoms, vertebral destruction, and cold psoas abscesses. It is generally more indolent than pyogenic infection.
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt high fever of 39.3°C is less typical
Extreme leukocytosis is less typical
Markedly elevated C-reactive protein is more suggestive of acute pyogenic infection
Only a two-week history is shorter than the usual subacute or chronic course
No stated tuberculosis exposure, travel history, or immunosuppression

data.description: A 67-year-old man with advanced alcoholic cirrhosis presented with progressive dyspnea. Physical examination after thoracentesis revealed right lung crackles, and the patient developed coughing, tachypnea, and tachycardia. His oxygen saturation was 82% while breathing ambient air.
Acute noncardiogenic pulmonary edema that can occur after rapid drainage of a large pleural effusion or pneumothorax, causing edema in the re-expanded lung.
symptoms_in_common: Severe hypoxemia with oxygen saturation of 82% on room air
New predominantly right-sided pulmonary infiltrates/consolidation on imaging after drainage of a large right pleural effusion
symptoms_not_in_common: No symptoms clearly inconsistent with this diagnosis

data.description: A typically right-sided transudative pleural effusion caused by passage of ascitic fluid through diaphragmatic defects in patients with advanced cirrhosis.
symptoms_in_common: Large right-sided pleural effusion/opacification on chest imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute coughing and worsening hypoxemia immediately after thoracentesis
Right lung crackles after fluid drainage
New right-lung air-space opacities after thoracentesis

data.description: Acute chemical lung injury caused by aspiration of gastric or oropharyngeal contents, often producing cough, hypoxemia, and dependent pulmonary infiltrates.
symptoms_not_in_common: Symptoms began in direct temporal association with thoracentesis rather than a reported aspiration event
No vomiting, impaired consciousness, or witnessed aspiration is described
The imaging pattern follows re-expansion of a previously compressed right lung

data.description: Pulmonary fluid accumulation due to elevated cardiac filling pressures, usually causing dyspnea, crackles, hypoxemia, and bilateral perihilar or diffuse infiltrates.
symptoms_not_in_common: Infiltrates are predominantly unilateral in the right lung
Abrupt onset after thoracentesis is more characteristic of re-expansion pulmonary edema
No history of heart failure, elevated jugular venous pressure, or peripheral edema is provided

data.description: Infection of the lung parenchyma that can cause cough, dyspnea, hypoxemia, crackles, and focal or multifocal pulmonary consolidation.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, purulent sputum, leukocytosis, or infectious prodrome is described
The abrupt deterioration immediately after thoracentesis is atypical for pneumonia
The rapid post-procedural imaging change favors re-expansion edema rather than infection

data.description: 52-year-old woman with exertional right buttock and thigh pain that resolves within 2 minutes of rest. Exercise tolerance worsened over past year, now limited to several blocks. Previously able to run 5-6 miles per day. Recently diagnosed hypertension controlled with lisinopril (5 mg daily). No other cardiovascular risk factors. Physical exam shows blood pressure 124/76 mm Hg bilaterally, high-pitched systolic bruit over right subcostal region and umbilicus, normal peripheral pulses. Ankle brachial index (ABI) at rest borderline normal (0.91) on right and normal (1.03) on left. Remainder of examination normal.

data.diagnosis: Multivessel fibromuscular dysplasia involving the renal and right iliac arteries
data.description: Fibromuscular dysplasia is a nonatherosclerotic, noninflammatory arterial disease, most often affecting middle-aged women. It can produce a characteristic alternating stenosis and dilation ('string-of-beads') appearance and may involve renal, carotid, and less commonly iliac arteries.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional right buttock and thigh claudication
Rapid relief of pain with rest
Normal peripheral pulses despite proximal arterial disease
Angiographic appearance consistent with multifocal arterial stenoses/dilatations
symptoms_not_in_common: No headache, pulsatile tinnitus, or neurologic symptoms suggestive of carotid/vertebral involvement
No renal dysfunction or flash pulmonary edema reported

data.description: External iliac artery endofibrosis is a nonatherosclerotic narrowing of the external iliac artery, classically occurring in highly active endurance athletes. It causes exercise-induced buttock, hip, or thigh claudication with normal or near-normal resting pulses and ABI.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional unilateral right buttock and thigh pain
Pain resolves rapidly after stopping exercise
Resting ABI is only borderline abnormal, which can occur because disease may be more evident during exertion
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypertension is not a typical consequence of isolated iliac endofibrosis
Right subcostal/umbilical abdominal bruit suggests possible renal or more proximal arterial involvement
Multifocal beaded arterial imaging is more suggestive of fibromuscular dysplasia than isolated endofibrosis

data.description: Atherosclerotic peripheral artery disease can cause stenosis of the aortoiliac arteries, producing buttock or thigh claudication that is reproducibly triggered by exertion and relieved by rest.
symptoms_not_in_common: Relatively young age for significant atherosclerotic aortoiliac disease
Female sex with few reported atherosclerotic risk factors other than hypertension
Prior high-level endurance exercise
Normal peripheral pulses
Imaging pattern of multifocal stenosis/dilatation is not typical of focal atherosclerotic plaque disease

diagnoses.name: External iliac artery dissection
diagnoses.title: Aneurysm or dissection of iliac artery[External iliac artery]

data.description: A 66-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with episodes of palpitations, dizziness, and near fainting that had lasted for a few hours. Her medical history included removal of a left atrial myxoma 15 years ago, after which she experienced recurrent atrial tachycardia managed with modified release verapamil 240 mg once daily. She had recently started sotalol 120 mg twice daily in addition to verapamil and underwent direct current cardioversion for persistent atrial tachycardia one week prior to presentation. Initial workup showed normal urea and electrolytes including magnesium. An echocardiogram revealed normal left ventricular systolic function with no recurrence of left atrial myxoma.

A form of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia associated with QT-interval prolongation, often caused by QT-prolonging medications such as sotalol. It can cause transient episodes of hemodynamic instability and may deteriorate into ventricular fibrillation.
symptoms_in_common: Acute episodic onset over several hours
ECG appearance consistent with polymorphic wide-complex tachycardia
symptoms_not_in_common: History of left atrial myxoma removal
Recurrent atrial tachycardia
Normal urea, electrolytes, and magnesium
Normal left ventricular systolic function

data.diagnosis: Acquired long QT syndrome due to sotalol
data.description: QT-interval prolongation caused by medication exposure, particularly class III antiarrhythmic drugs such as sotalol. Acquired long QT syndrome predisposes to torsades de pointes and syncope.
symptoms_in_common: Recent commencement of sotalol 120 mg twice daily
Ventricular arrhythmia compatible with QT-related proarrhythmia
symptoms_not_in_common: Previous left atrial myxoma
Persistent atrial tachycardia requiring cardioversion
Normal electrolyte and magnesium levels
No evidence of structural left ventricular dysfunction

data.diagnosis: Drug-induced proarrhythmia from combined antiarrhythmic therapy
data.description: A clinically significant new or worsened arrhythmia caused by antiarrhythmic medication. Sotalol can prolong repolarization and provoke polymorphic ventricular tachycardia; concomitant verapamil may contribute to bradycardia or conduction effects that increase susceptibility to QT-related arrhythmia.
symptoms_in_common: Symptoms began after addition of sotalol to chronic verapamil therapy
ECG evidence of a dangerous ventricular tachyarrhythmia
symptoms_not_in_common: Remote history of atrial myxoma excision
Normal echocardiographic left ventricular systolic function
No electrolyte or magnesium abnormality

data.description: A rapid ventricular rhythm with changing QRS morphology. When associated with prolonged QT interval it is termed torsades de pointes; it commonly presents with palpitations, presyncope, syncope, or sudden cardiac arrest.
symptoms_in_common: ECG showing a rapid polymorphic wide-complex tachycardia
Recent exposure to a QT-prolonging antiarrhythmic drug
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic recurrent atrial tachycardia
Prior left atrial myxoma surgery
Normal electrolyte studies
Normal left ventricular systolic function

data.description: 18-year-old pregnant woman. Healthy with no history of smoking, drug abuse, or family history of chromosomal disease or encephalodysplasia. Experienced mild flu-like symptoms during first month of pregnancy that resolved after three days without medication.

30-year-old male with 6 weeks of low-grade fever, fatigue, and progressive polyarthritis of large joints in the upper and lower limbs, without small joint involvement. Exam showed fever (38.9°C), multiple tender dull red nodules on the forehead, left cheek, and sternum, a firm 1×1 cm right cervical lymph node, bilateral arthritis of the knees, hips, and elbows, and palpable hepatomegaly 4 cm below the right costal margin. No relevant past history; TB contact and high-risk sexual behavior were denied. Laboratory studies showed normal blood count, low ESR (6 mm/h), elevated CRP (131 mg/L), negative ANA, rheumatoid factor, ANCA, ASO, and anti-DNase B, sterile blood cultures, negative tests for gonococci and syphilis, and normal calcium and ACE.

data.diagnosis: Sarcoidosis (acute sarcoid arthritis with cutaneous sarcoidosis)
data.description: A systemic granulomatous inflammatory disease characterized by noncaseating granulomas, commonly involving intrathoracic lymph nodes, lungs, skin, joints, liver, and lymph nodes. Acute presentations can include fever, erythematous skin lesions, and inflammatory arthritis.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive inflammatory polyarthritis involving large joints
Tender dull red cutaneous nodules on the face and sternum
Bilateral hilar/intrathoracic lymphadenopathy on chest radiograph
Negative rheumatoid factor, ANA, and ANCA
Granulomatous inflammation with giant cells on skin histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal serum ACE level
Normal serum calcium level
Very low ESR despite substantial systemic inflammation
Predominant knee, hip, and elbow arthritis rather than the more typical ankle-predominant arthritis of acute sarcoidosis

data.diagnosis: Tuberculosis with Poncet disease (tuberculosis-associated reactive polyarthritis)
data.description: Poncet disease is a sterile reactive polyarthritis occurring in association with active tuberculosis elsewhere in the body. Tuberculosis may also produce lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly, skin lesions, and hilar or mediastinal lymph node enlargement.
symptoms_in_common: Granulomatous inflammation with giant cells on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: No known tuberculosis contact
No described pulmonary symptoms such as chronic cough, hemoptysis, or weight loss
No microbiologic confirmation of tuberculosis provided
Normal ESR is less typical in active disseminated tuberculosis
Facial and sternal red nodules are less typical than erythema nodosum of the lower legs

data.description: Hodgkin lymphoma can cause prolonged fever, lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly, elevated inflammatory markers, and mediastinal or hilar lymph node enlargement. Paraneoplastic inflammatory manifestations, including arthritis and skin eruptions, can occur but are uncommon.
symptoms_in_common: Possible mediastinal/hilar lymphadenopathy on chest radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal blood count
No reported weight loss, drenching night sweats, or pruritus
Prominent bilateral inflammatory large-joint arthritis is not typical
Tender red skin nodules are not a usual presentation
Granulomatous skin pathology would favor sarcoidosis or infection over lymphoma

data.diagnosis: Disseminated fungal infection, such as histoplasmosis
data.description: Disseminated histoplasmosis is a systemic fungal infection that can involve lymph nodes, liver, lungs, skin, and bone marrow. It may produce fever, hepatomegaly, lymphadenopathy, inflammatory markers, and granulomatous histology.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported immunosuppression or relevant exposure history
Normal blood count, whereas disseminated disease often causes cytopenias
No reported pulmonary, gastrointestinal, or mucosal symptoms
Symmetric inflammatory polyarthritis is not a classic dominant manifestation
No fungal organisms or cultures reported

data.diagnosis: Seronegative rheumatoid arthritis with rheumatoid nodules
data.description: Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune arthritis that usually affects small joints symmetrically but can occasionally present atypically. Rheumatoid nodules are firm subcutaneous lesions with palisading granulomatous inflammation and central fibrinoid necrosis.
symptoms_in_common: Possible granulomatous/palisading features on skin nodule histology
symptoms_not_in_common: No small-joint involvement
Negative rheumatoid factor
Fever, cervical lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly, and hilar lymphadenopathy are unusual for uncomplicated rheumatoid arthritis
Rheumatoid nodules are more typical in established seropositive disease
Facial nodules are less typical than extensor-surface nodules

data.description: 13-year-old girl with a multiply recurrent hypothalamic/chiasmatic pilocytic astrocytoma with ventricular metastases. Had never received steroids or bisphosphonates. After 16 courses of treatment, complained of wrist pain. Physical examination revealed tenderness to palpation of the left dorsal wrist with decreased range of motion.

data.diagnosis: Osteonecrosis (avascular necrosis) of the distal radial epiphysis, likely treatment-associated
data.description: Ischemic death of bone marrow and trabecular bone caused by impaired blood supply. The MRI appearance of a subchondral/epiphyseal low-signal band in the distal radius is concerning for osteonecrosis. Antineoplastic therapy, including antiangiogenic agents, can rarely contribute even without corticosteroid exposure.
symptoms_in_common: MRI abnormality centered in the distal radial epiphysis
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypothalamic-chiasmatic pilocytic astrocytoma with ventricular metastases

data.diagnosis: Stress injury or insufficiency fracture of the distal radius
data.description: A stress or insufficiency fracture is a small fracture caused by repetitive loading or weakened bone rather than a major traumatic event. It can cause focal pain and may appear as a linear low-signal band on MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Linear low-signal abnormality in the distal radius on MRI
Cancer treatment that may affect bone health
symptoms_not_in_common: No acute trauma is reported
The imaging appearance is more suggestive of osteonecrosis than a typical fracture line
Hypothalamic-chiasmatic pilocytic astrocytoma with ventricular metastases

data.description: Kienböck disease is avascular necrosis of the lunate carpal bone, causing progressive dorsal wrist pain, stiffness, and impaired wrist motion. It is a consideration for dorsal wrist pain but is less consistent with an abnormality centered in the distal radius.
symptoms_not_in_common: MRI abnormality appears to involve the distal radial epiphysis rather than the lunate
Young age is less typical
History of recurrent intracranial tumor and repeated chemotherapy is not a typical cause

data.description: 10-month-old male admitted with fever. Born at 38 weeks gestation after unremarkable pregnancy, birth weight 2,960g. History of cephalhematoma over parietooccipital region at birth, bilateral inguinal hernia repair at 2 months, recurrent pneumonia and urinary tract infection. Growth parameters below 3rd percentile (weight: 7,500g, length: 73.7cm). Physical exam showed pale skin, sparse/light/curly hair with pili torti on microscopy. Neurologic exam revealed diffuse hypotonia with poor head/trunk support, no visual fixing/following, hyperreflexic deep tendon reflexes bilaterally with ankle clonus, bilateral Babinski extension. Lab results: serum copper 27 μg/dL (normal 70-130), ceruloplasmin 9.07 μg/dL (normal 20-60).

An X-linked ATP7A-related disorder of copper transport causing systemic copper deficiency, low ceruloplasmin, neurodegeneration, characteristic sparse kinky hair (pili torti), connective-tissue abnormalities, and tortuous cerebral arteries.
symptoms_in_common: Failure to thrive with weight and length below the 3rd percentile
Diffuse hypotonia and poor head/trunk control
Hyperreflexia, ankle clonus, and bilateral Babinski signs
Brain MRI diffusion-restricted white-matter lesions consistent with ischemic injury
Marked tortuosity of intracranial/cervical arteries on MR angiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever at admission

data.description: A milder allelic ATP7A-related copper transport disorder characterized primarily by connective-tissue abnormalities, bladder diverticula, hernias, joint laxity, and occipital bone exostoses; neurologic impairment is generally less severe than in classic Menkes disease.
symptoms_in_common: History of cephalhematoma suggesting connective-tissue fragility
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe early neurodevelopmental impairment with poor head control
No visual fixation
Marked hyperreflexia, ankle clonus, and bilateral Babinski signs
Sparse kinky hair with prominent pili torti
Severe failure to thrive
Acute bilateral white-matter ischemic lesions
Recurrent pneumonia and urinary tract infection
Fever at admission

data.description: Copper deficiency due to inadequate intake, malabsorption, excessive zinc exposure, or prolonged parenteral nutrition can cause low serum copper and ceruloplasmin, anemia, poor growth, hypotonia, and neurologic dysfunction.
symptoms_not_in_common: Pili torti and sparse light curly hair
History of cephalhematoma and bilateral inguinal hernias
Marked tortuosity of cerebral and cervical arteries
Bilateral ischemic white-matter lesions in infancy
Hyperreflexia with ankle clonus and bilateral Babinski signs
Absent visual fixation
Recurrent pneumonia and urinary tract infection
Fever at admission

data.diagnosis: Mitochondrial encephalopathy with stroke-like or ischemic brain lesions
data.description: Mitochondrial disorders can present in infancy with failure to thrive, hypotonia, developmental delay, recurrent illness, and multifocal brain lesions, although they do not usually cause profound copper deficiency or pili torti.
symptoms_in_common: Severe developmental impairment with poor head control
Hyperreflexia and upper motor neuron signs
Bilateral brain white-matter lesions with diffusion restriction
symptoms_not_in_common: Very low serum copper
Low ceruloplasmin
Sparse kinky hair with pili torti
Cephalhematoma and inguinal hernias suggesting connective-tissue disease
Marked tortuosity of intracranial and cervical arteries

data.description: 47-year-old female with an incidentally discovered right adrenal mass noted 3 years ago, initially 2.2 × 3.1 cm and untreated, now enlarged on CT 10 days ago to 5.8 × 4.7 cm. She has remained asymptomatic throughout. Past history is unremarkable for hypertension, diabetes, cardiac, pulmonary, or cerebrovascular disease; she denies smoking and alcohol use and reports reduced menstrual flow. Physical examination was normal, including stable vital signs, normal cardiopulmonary findings, and a soft, non-tender abdomen without palpable mass or renal tenderness.
A rare, usually benign adrenal cortical tumor composed of large eosinophilic oncocytic cells. It is commonly nonfunctioning and discovered incidentally, but may enlarge substantially.
symptoms_in_common: No hypertension or diabetes suggesting hormone excess
Progressive enlargement of a unilateral adrenal mass
Normal abdominal examination despite a sizable lesion
Imaging appearance of a well-defined right adrenal mass
symptoms_not_in_common: Reduced menstrual flow is not a typical feature of a nonfunctioning adrenal oncocytoma

data.description: A common benign tumor of the adrenal cortex. Many adenomas are nonfunctioning and found incidentally, although some produce cortisol or aldosterone.
symptoms_in_common: No diabetes or overt Cushingoid features
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked growth from approximately 3 cm to nearly 6 cm over 3 years is less typical for a benign adrenal adenoma
Reduced menstrual flow is not typical unless there is significant hormonal secretion

data.description: A rare malignant tumor of the adrenal cortex that often presents as a large enlarging adrenal mass and may be hormonally functional or nonfunctioning.
symptoms_in_common: Large unilateral adrenal mass greater than 4 cm
Possible absence of symptoms in a nonfunctioning tumor
Normal blood pressure and lack of overt endocrine syndrome can occur in nonfunctioning disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No abdominal pain, palpable mass, weight loss, or constitutional symptoms
No signs of cortisol, androgen, or aldosterone excess
Slow asymptomatic course over 3 years is less characteristic of an aggressive carcinoma

data.description: A catecholamine-producing tumor of the adrenal medulla that may be discovered incidentally; some lesions are clinically silent or minimally functional.
symptoms_not_in_common: No hypertension
No episodic headache
No palpitations
No diaphoresis
No tremor or anxiety episodes
No cardiovascular symptoms
Reduced menstrual flow is not typical

data.description: A rare benign vascular lesion of the adrenal gland that is often nonfunctioning, asymptomatic, and detected incidentally; it can enlarge and become heterogeneous because of hemorrhage, thrombosis, or calcification.
symptoms_in_common: Normal vital signs and normal abdominal examination
Nonfunctioning clinical presentation without hypertension or diabetes
symptoms_not_in_common: Reduced menstrual flow is not a typical feature
No abdominal or flank discomfort despite lesion enlargement, although larger hemangiomas can cause pain

data.description: 34-year-old white male presented with an indurated plaque on the forehead that extended onto the scalp over approximately 1 year. Initial laboratory findings showed positive antinuclear antibodies (1:200) and slightly increased C3d complement; other laboratory tests were normal.

data.diagnosis: Linear morphea (linear scleroderma) of the forehead/scalp, "en coup de sabre"
data.description: A localized autoimmune sclerosing disorder causing a linear band of induration, atrophy, pigment change, and sometimes scarring alopecia on the forehead and scalp. The "en coup de sabre" subtype resembles a saber-cut depression and commonly affects the frontoparietal scalp.
symptoms_in_common: Slowly progressive indurated plaque over approximately 1 year
Linear forehead lesion extending onto the scalp
Visible scalp atrophy and hair loss within the lesion
Positive antinuclear antibodies can occur in localized scleroderma
Histology compatible with dermal/subcutaneous sclerosis and inflammatory infiltrates
symptoms_not_in_common: No systemic sclerosis manifestations were reported, such as Raynaud phenomenon, sclerodactyly, dysphagia, or pulmonary involvement

data.description: A deeper variant of localized scleroderma involving the deep dermis, subcutaneous fat, fascia, and sometimes muscle, producing marked induration and tethering of the skin.
symptoms_in_common: Sclerotic changes extending into deeper tissue on histology
symptoms_not_in_common: The sharply linear forehead-to-scalp distribution is more characteristic of linear morphea en coup de sabre than generalized deep morphea
No limb contractures, restricted mobility, or widespread deep plaques were reported

data.description: A form of cutaneous lupus in which inflammation of subcutaneous fat causes firm plaques followed by lipoatrophy and sometimes scarring alopecia when the scalp is involved.
symptoms_in_common: Scalp hair loss/atrophy in the affected area
Inflammation involving subcutaneous tissue on histology
symptoms_not_in_common: The linear saber-like forehead and scalp distribution is not typical
No photosensitivity, malar rash, oral ulcers, arthritis, or other lupus manifestations were reported
No classic lupus histologic features, such as interface dermatitis, prominent dermal mucin, or hyaline fat necrosis, were described

data.description: A chronic cutaneous lupus variant that produces well-demarcated inflammatory plaques with scale, dyspigmentation, scarring, and permanent alopecia on the scalp.
symptoms_in_common: Positive antinuclear antibodies may be present
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion is described as deeply indurated and linear rather than a scaly discoid plaque
Extension from forehead to scalp in an en coup de sabre pattern is atypical
No adherent scale, follicular plugging, dyspigmentation, or photosensitivity was reported

data.description: A lymphocytic cicatricial alopecia in which inflammation around hair follicles causes progressive permanent scalp hair loss, often with perifollicular erythema and scale.
symptoms_in_common: Inflammatory infiltrate may be seen around follicular structures
symptoms_not_in_common: A broad indurated forehead plaque extending onto the scalp is not typical
No perifollicular scale, pruritus, burning, or follicular papules were reported
Dermal and subcutaneous sclerosis is not characteristic of lichen planopilaris
Positive antinuclear antibodies are not a typical defining finding

data.description: A 14-year-old girl with no prior medical history presented to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain for 2 days, accompanied by non-bilious vomiting. Physical examination revealed pallor, diffuse abdominal tenderness with guarding, and sluggish bowel sounds but no rigidity. Her recent history included two episodes of multiple oral ulcers that had resolved spontaneously. Laboratory findings showed hemoglobin 88 g/L, total leucocyte count 3.6 × 10⁹/L, platelets 96 × 10⁹/L, and ESR 54 mm/h. Urinalysis was normal, and blood and urine cultures were sterile. Initial ANA testing by indirect immunofluorescence with HEp-2 cell substrate was negative. Subsequent repeat ANA testing at a different laboratory remained negative, but dsDNA and anti-Ro antibodies were strongly positive with low concentrations of C3 and C4. Echocardiography showed a mild pericardial effusion.

data.diagnosis: ANA-negative systemic lupus erythematosus with lupus enteritis (mesenteric vasculitis)
data.description: Systemic lupus erythematosus can rarely occur despite repeatedly negative ANA testing. Immune-complex vasculitis of mesenteric vessels may cause bowel-wall edema, intestinal pseudo-obstruction or ileus, severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and CT features such as bowel-wall thickening/target appearance and mesenteric vascular engorgement.
symptoms_in_common: Severe diffuse abdominal pain with guarding
Sluggish bowel sounds and dilated bowel loops consistent with ileus or intestinal pseudo-obstruction
Low C3 and C4 complement levels
Mild pericardial effusion consistent with serositis
CT appearance compatible with bowel-wall edema and mesenteric vasculitis
symptoms_not_in_common: Repeated negative ANA by HEp-2 immunofluorescence, which is unusual although possible in rare ANA-negative lupus
Normal urinalysis despite serologic evidence of active lupus

data.description: A gastrointestinal manifestation of active SLE caused by inflammation of small mesenteric vessels, producing bowel ischemia, submucosal edema, ascites, bowel dilation, and potentially perforation if untreated.
symptoms_in_common: CT findings suggestive of bowel-wall thickening/edema and mesenteric inflammatory vascular changes
symptoms_not_in_common: Oral ulcers are not a defining feature of isolated mesenteric vasculitis
Mild pericardial effusion reflects systemic lupus activity rather than bowel vasculitis itself
Negative ANA is atypical in the usual lupus-associated form

data.description: Behçet disease is a multisystem inflammatory vasculitis classically characterized by recurrent oral and genital ulcers, eye inflammation, skin lesions, and sometimes gastrointestinal ulceration or vascular involvement causing abdominal pain.
symptoms_not_in_common: No genital ulcers reported
No uveitis or other eye inflammation reported
No typical skin lesions reported
Marked leukopenia and thrombocytopenia are not typical core findings
Strong anti-dsDNA and anti-Ro positivity is not characteristic
Low C3 and C4 complement levels are not typical
Pericardial effusion is less characteristic
The overall serologic pattern strongly favors lupus rather than Behçet disease

data.diagnosis: Polyarteritis nodosa or another systemic medium-vessel vasculitis
data.description: Medium-vessel vasculitides can involve mesenteric arteries and cause acute abdominal pain, bowel ischemia, vomiting, and renal vascular abnormalities. Polyarteritis nodosa generally does not cause glomerulonephritis.
symptoms_in_common: Severe abdominal pain that could reflect mesenteric ischemia
Possible radiologic evidence of vascular or ischemic abdominal involvement
Normal urinalysis can occur in polyarteritis nodosa
symptoms_not_in_common: Recurrent oral ulcers are not typical
Leukopenia and thrombocytopenia are not typical primary features
Strong anti-dsDNA antibodies are not characteristic
Anti-Ro antibodies are not characteristic
Low complement levels are less typical
Pericardial effusion is less typical
The combination of cytopenias, hypocomplementemia, and lupus-specific antibodies favors SLE

data.description: 41-year-old woman with chest pain. One year earlier, she had transient left-sided chest and shoulder tightness. Five days before presentation, she developed acute substernal chest pain radiating to the jaw and shoulders with dyspnea while packing for a flight; it lasted 1 hour and resolved spontaneously. The day before presentation, similar pain recurred after walking, with light-headedness and dyspnea. History includes laparoscopy for an ovarian cyst and miscarriage 1 month prior. She exercises regularly, does not smoke, and drinks alcohol socially. Family history is notable for hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome in multiple first-degree relatives and a maternal cousin who died of a cerebral aneurysm at 51. On examination, she was diaphoretic; vital signs were temperature 36.6°C, heart rate 68/min, blood pressure 143/87 mmHg bilaterally, respiratory rate 18/min, and oxygen saturation 100%, with no cardiac murmurs, rubs, or gallops.

A nonatherosclerotic tear or intramural hematoma within a coronary artery wall that narrows the true lumen and causes acute coronary syndrome. The angiogram is consistent with dissection involving the left anterior descending coronary artery.
symptoms_in_common: Pain radiating to the jaw and shoulders
Young woman with few conventional atherosclerotic risk factors
Recent miscarriage, a hormonal and physiologic context associated with SCAD
symptoms_not_in_common: No symptoms are strongly atypical; the presentation is highly compatible with SCAD

data.description: A noninflammatory, nonatherosclerotic arterial disease causing stenosis, aneurysm, dissection, or a characteristic beaded appearance of medium-sized arteries. It is strongly associated with SCAD; the renal artery imaging appears consistent with multifocal FMD.
symptoms_in_common: Possible arterial tortuosity or multifocal vascular abnormalities on imaging
Family history suggestive of connective-tissue or arterial fragility
symptoms_not_in_common: No flank pain
No reported headaches or pulsatile tinnitus
No documented renal dysfunction
No reported prior transient ischemic attack or stroke symptoms

data.diagnosis: Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) secondary to SCAD
data.description: Myocardial infarction without persistent ST-segment elevation, caused here by reduced coronary blood flow from spontaneous coronary artery dissection rather than plaque rupture.
symptoms_in_common: Prolonged substernal chest pain lasting approximately 1 hour
Coronary angiographic abnormality producing impaired coronary flow
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported persistent ST-segment elevation
No known diabetes, smoking history, or hyperlipidemia
Age and overall low traditional atherosclerotic risk profile are less typical for conventional myocardial infarction

data.description: A heritable connective-tissue disorder, usually caused by pathogenic COL3A1 variants, characterized by arterial dissection or rupture, organ fragility, and pregnancy-related complications. It is an important consideration in patients with spontaneous arterial dissections and a relevant family history.
symptoms_in_common: Possible renal or other arterial abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported thin translucent skin
No reported easy bruising
No reported characteristic facial features
No reported history of bowel, uterine, or major arterial rupture
Family history is specifically described as hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome rather than confirmed vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome

data.description: Myocardial ischemia caused by atherosclerotic plaque rupture or erosion with coronary thrombosis. This is a common cause of acute chest pain but is less favored than SCAD because of the angiographic appearance and absence of traditional cardiovascular risk factors.
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 41 years
Female sex with low conventional cardiovascular risk
Regular exercise
No smoking history
No reported diabetes, hyperlipidemia, or established vascular disease
Angiographic findings favor coronary dissection rather than plaque-mediated obstruction

data.description: Patient is a 2 month-old male, full-term infant, with severe malnutrition and failure to thrive, admitted to the intensive care unit, with long term feeding difficulties. The study was performed initially to rule out malrotation.

data.diagnosis: Congenital duodenal stenosis or duodenal web
data.description: Partial congenital obstruction of the duodenum caused by narrowing or an intraluminal mucosal web. Unlike complete duodenal atresia, it may present later with chronic feeding intolerance and poor growth.
symptoms_not_in_common: No bilious vomiting is described
No abdominal distension is described
No jaundice is described

data.diagnosis: Intestinal malrotation with intermittent midgut volvulus
data.description: Abnormal embryologic positioning of the bowel that can predispose to twisting of the mesentery and intermittent or acute obstruction. An upper gastrointestinal contrast study is commonly performed to evaluate this condition.
symptoms_in_common: Upper gastrointestinal contrast study performed to rule out malrotation
symptoms_not_in_common: No bilious emesis is described
No acute abdominal pain or irritability is described
No abdominal distension is described
No bloody stools are described
No hemodynamic instability attributable to bowel ischemia is described

data.description: Progressive hypertrophy of the pyloric muscle causing gastric outlet obstruction, typically in young male infants between 2 and 8 weeks of age.
symptoms_not_in_common: No projectile non-bilious vomiting is described
No persistent post-feeding emesis is described
No palpable olive-shaped abdominal mass is described
No dehydration or hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis is described

data.diagnosis: Annular pancreas causing partial duodenal obstruction
data.description: A congenital pancreatic anomaly in which pancreatic tissue encircles the duodenum, producing variable narrowing and delayed gastric emptying. Partial obstruction may present with chronic feeding intolerance and poor weight gain.
symptoms_not_in_common: No bilious vomiting is described
No abdominal distension is described
No classic double-bubble radiographic description is provided
No associated congenital anomalies are described

data.description:
47-year-old man with hypertension presented with 3 days of left periorbital swelling, throat tightness, hoarseness, and dysphagia to solids. He had no pruritus, visual symptoms, pain, dyspnea, wheezing, fever, or recent illness. Exam showed periorbital edema with faint erythema, mildly enlarged tongue, hoarse muffled voice, and no stridor; vital signs were stable.

Two weeks later, he developed worsening dysphonia, increased throat swelling sensation, nasal regurgitation of liquids, shoulder and hip pain, and reduced ability to jump. Exam then showed anterior/lateral neck tenderness, subcutaneous edema of both upper arms, normal arm strength, reduced hip strength, and difficulty rising from a seated position. Labs showed markedly elevated CK, elevated AST/ALT, mildly elevated ESR/CRP, normal TSH, positive ANA (1:160), and negative myositis-specific antibodies. Left deltoid biopsy showed mild fiber size variability, perivascular inflammatory infiltrate, and MHC class I positivity on nonnecrotic fibers.

data.diagnosis: Dermatomyositis with prominent facial and upper-airway edema
data.description: An idiopathic inflammatory myopathy characterized by proximal muscle weakness, elevated muscle enzymes, characteristic cutaneous findings, and possible dysphagia from pharyngeal muscle involvement. Severe periorbital, facial, subcutaneous, and pharyngeal edema can rarely be a presenting manifestation.
symptoms_in_common: Periorbital edema with faint erythema consistent with a heliotrope-type eruption
Progressive dysphonia and hoarse muffled voice
Dysphagia and nasal regurgitation of liquids suggesting pharyngeal muscle involvement
Proximal lower-extremity weakness with difficulty rising from a seated position and reduced ability to jump
Subcutaneous edema of the upper arms
Markedly elevated CK and elevated AST/ALT
Muscle biopsy with perivascular inflammation and MHC class I expression on nonnecrotic fibers
MRI evidence of edema in facial, tongue, soft-palate, pharyngeal, and cervical muscles
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of clearly described classic Gottron papules or Gottron sign
No clearly described photosensitive shawl sign, V-sign, or poikilodermatous rash
Initial presentation resembling isolated angioedema before overt muscle weakness

data.description: An autoimmune inflammatory myopathy causing symmetric proximal muscle weakness, muscle pain, elevated CK, and possible dysphagia due to involvement of bulbar and pharyngeal muscles. Unlike dermatomyositis, it does not produce characteristic skin findings.
symptoms_in_common: Difficulty rising from a seated position
Dysphonia and hoarseness due to possible pharyngeal muscle involvement
Elevated AST and ALT from muscle injury
MHC class I positivity on nonnecrotic muscle fibers
symptoms_not_in_common: Periorbital edema with erythema suggestive of heliotrope rash
Prominent facial, tongue, upper-airway, and subcutaneous edema
MRI showing extensive edema of facial and pharyngeal muscles with cervical subcutaneous edema
Perivascular inflammatory infiltrate, which is more supportive of dermatomyositis than classic polymyositis

data.description: A severe autoimmune myopathy characterized by marked CK elevation and rapidly progressive proximal weakness. It may be associated with statin exposure, anti-HMGCR antibodies, anti-SRP antibodies, malignancy, or other autoimmune disease.
symptoms_in_common: Difficulty standing from a seated position
Negative myositis-specific antibody panel can occur in some cases
symptoms_not_in_common: Periorbital erythema and edema suggestive of dermatomyositis
Prominent facial, upper-airway, and subcutaneous edema
Perivascular inflammatory infiltrates on muscle biopsy
MHC class I expression with inflammatory pathology rather than predominantly muscle fiber necrosis and regeneration
No reported statin exposure or anti-HMGCR/anti-SRP antibody positivity

data.diagnosis: Bradykinin-mediated angioedema, including ACE inhibitor-associated angioedema
data.description: Angioedema is localized swelling of subcutaneous and submucosal tissues, often involving the lips, tongue, face, and upper airway. Bradykinin-mediated forms typically lack urticaria and pruritus and can be associated with ACE inhibitor use.
symptoms_in_common: Stable vital signs and no initial respiratory distress
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive proximal muscle weakness
Shoulder and hip pain
Difficulty rising from a seated position
Reduced ability to jump
Marked CK elevation
Elevated AST and ALT from muscle inflammation
Perivascular inflammatory infiltrates and MHC class I positivity on muscle biopsy
Persistent diffuse edema involving skeletal muscles of the face, pharynx, and neck on MRI

data.description: 11-year-old boy who received his first black henna tattoo while on holiday in Portugal in August 2013. One week after getting the tattoo, the area became hot, red, raised and itchy. Physical exam showed bullae with clear yellow-orange discharge and golden crusting on a background of erythematous plaque.

data.diagnosis: Allergic contact dermatitis to para-phenylenediamine (PPD) in black henna tattoo
data.description: A delayed type IV hypersensitivity reaction caused by PPD, a common additive in black henna tattoos. It often produces an intensely itchy, eczematous or blistering rash precisely following the tattoo pattern several days after exposure.
symptoms_in_common: Rash began about one week after application of a black henna tattoo
Erythematous plaque matching the tattoo distribution
symptoms_not_in_common: Golden crusting may indicate secondary bacterial infection rather than uncomplicated allergic dermatitis

data.description: Allergic contact dermatitis complicated by superficial bacterial infection, usually Staphylococcus aureus and/or Streptococcus pyogenes. Damaged, scratched eczematous skin can develop honey-colored or golden crusts and drainage.
symptoms_in_common: Delayed itchy, erythematous blistering eruption after black henna exposure
Rash localized to the tattooed area
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, malaise, or spreading systemic symptoms were reported
The sharply tattoo-patterned eruption is more characteristic of the underlying allergic contact reaction than infection alone

data.description: A superficial Staphylococcus aureus skin infection characterized by fragile blisters, erosions, yellow drainage, and crusting. It may occur secondarily on disrupted skin such as dermatitis or a tattoo reaction.
symptoms_not_in_common: Intense itch is more suggestive of allergic dermatitis than primary bullous impetigo
Onset after black henna tattoo exposure
Lesion closely follows the tattoo design
No reported fever or generalized illness

data.diagnosis: Irritant contact dermatitis from henna tattoo chemicals
data.description: An inflammatory skin reaction caused by direct chemical injury from tattoo ingredients or solvents. It can cause redness, burning, blistering, and weeping at sites of exposure, though it usually occurs sooner than allergic dermatitis.
symptoms_in_common: Red, hot, raised skin at the exposure site
Localized distribution corresponding to the tattoo
symptoms_not_in_common: Symptoms began one week after exposure, which is more typical of delayed allergic contact dermatitis
Marked itch favors allergic contact dermatitis
Golden crusting suggests possible secondary infection

data.description: 59-year-old man with multiple nodules on his joints. Patient had history of gouty arthritis (confirmed by visualization of negative birefringent crystals in joint aspirate), hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Physical examination showed multiple gouty nodules in the auricle, knee, ankle, and toe joints, with severe loss of flexion and extension in hands. Laboratory findings showed elevated creatine (137 μmol/L; normal range 62–115 μmol/L) and uric acid (725 μmol/L; normal range 208–428 μmol/L).
Advanced gout caused by longstanding deposition of monosodium urate crystals in joints and soft tissues, producing large tophi, erosive arthritis, and joint deformity.
symptoms_in_common: History of gouty arthritis confirmed by negatively birefringent crystals in joint aspirate
Multiple large nodules consistent with tophi on the hands, auricle, knees, ankles, and toes
Severe hand deformity with loss of flexion and extension
Involvement of typical gout sites including toe, ankle, knee, and auricle
Mildly elevated creatinine, which may accompany gout-associated kidney disease

data.description: A chronic autoimmune inflammatory polyarthritis that can cause symmetric hand deformities and firm subcutaneous rheumatoid nodules, usually over pressure points.
symptoms_in_common: Severe loss of hand flexion and extension
symptoms_not_in_common: Negatively birefringent crystals in joint aspirate
Marked hyperuricemia
Tophi involving the auricles
Known history of crystal-proven gout
Typical gout distribution involving toes, ankles, and knees

data.description: Deposition of calcium salts in skin and periarticular soft tissues, causing firm calcified nodules near large joints and sometimes restricting joint movement.
symptoms_in_common: Nodules involving knees, ankles, and hands
Restricted hand movement due to bulky soft-tissue masses
symptoms_not_in_common: Negatively birefringent monosodium urate crystals in aspirated joint fluid
Markedly elevated uric acid level
Auricular tophi
Established history of gouty arthritis
Typical podagra-related toe involvement

data.description: A 25-year-old man was referred to the oncology unit with a three-week history of a progressively enlarging neck lump and atypical lymphoid cells found on fine needle aspiration cytology. He reported mild exertional dyspnea and drenching night sweats, but denied weight loss, occupational exposure to harmful substances, recent travel, or high-risk sexual behavior. He had a smoking history since age 16. On physical examination, a palpable right supraclavicular lymph node measuring 3 cm in diameter was found. Chest radiography revealed a widened mediastinum but no lung lesions. Core biopsy of the lymph node showed partial effacement of nodal architecture by scattered large cells in a background of reactive lymphocytes, eosinophils, and plasma cells with some collagen fibrosis. These large cells stained positive for CD15 and CD30 and negative for CD45.

data.diagnosis: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma, nodular sclerosis subtype
data.description: A subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma characterized by Reed-Sternberg cells in an inflammatory background, often with collagen fibrosis and frequent mediastinal involvement in young adults. Tumor cells are typically CD15-positive, CD30-positive, and CD45-negative.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively enlarging right supraclavicular lymph node
Mild exertional dyspnea from mediastinal disease
Large atypical lymphoid cells on cytology/biopsy
Large cells positive for CD15 and CD30
Reactive background containing lymphocytes, eosinophils, and plasma cells
Collagen fibrosis in the lymph node biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss
No recent travel
No high-risk sexual behavior

data.description: An aggressive B-cell lymphoma that commonly arises as a bulky anterior mediastinal mass in young adults and can cause dyspnea and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy. It usually expresses B-cell markers such as CD20, PAX5, and CD45 rather than the classic Hodgkin immunophenotype.
symptoms_in_common: Widened mediastinum consistent with a mediastinal mass
symptoms_not_in_common: Large atypical cells are CD15-positive
Large atypical cells are CD30-positive in a classic Hodgkin-like pattern
Large atypical cells are CD45-negative
Prominent eosinophil-rich reactive background
Collagen fibrosis with nodular sclerosis-type morphology
No reported B-cell marker expression

data.description: A rare lymphoma with overlapping clinical, morphologic, and immunophenotypic features of classical Hodgkin lymphoma and primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma. It often presents with a mediastinal mass in young adults.
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy pattern is strongly characteristic of nodular sclerosis classical Hodgkin lymphoma
Large cells are CD45-negative, favoring classical Hodgkin lymphoma
No reported expression of B-cell markers such as CD20, CD79a, OCT2, or PAX5
Eosinophil-rich inflammatory background and fibrosis are more typical of nodular sclerosis Hodgkin lymphoma

data.description: A CD30-positive T-cell lymphoma that can present with systemic symptoms and lymphadenopathy. Depending on subtype, it may express ALK and usually retains CD45 and expresses T-cell-associated markers.
symptoms_not_in_common: CD15 positivity is less typical
CD45 negativity is less typical
No reported T-cell marker expression
No reported ALK expression
Reactive eosinophils, plasma cells, and collagen fibrosis favor classical Hodgkin lymphoma
Mediastinal presentation with nodular sclerosis-type histology is more typical of Hodgkin lymphoma

data.description: A 45-year-old man presented with dry cough and breathlessness. During the investigation, he was found to be infected with HIV. Physical examination and other baseline clinical details were not specifically described in this brief case report.

An opportunistic fungal pneumonia in people with advanced HIV infection, typically causing subacute hypoxemic respiratory illness with bilateral diffuse or perihilar interstitial/ground-glass pulmonary infiltrates.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral diffuse/perihilar pulmonary infiltrates on chest radiograph

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the lungs, which is more frequent in people with HIV and may produce atypical diffuse, lower-zone, or miliary radiographic infiltrates in immunosuppressed patients.
symptoms_not_in_common: Dry cough is less typical than persistent productive cough
No fever, night sweats, weight loss, hemoptysis, or known tuberculosis exposure was described

data.description: An opportunistic viral pneumonia occurring mainly in severely immunocompromised patients with HIV, causing dyspnea, cough, hypoxemia, and diffuse bilateral interstitial or ground-glass infiltrates.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever was reported
No other evidence of disseminated cytomegalovirus disease, such as visual or gastrointestinal symptoms, was described

data.description: Acute bacterial infection of the lung, commonly due to Streptococcus pneumoniae or other bacteria, which occurs more often and may be more severe in people with HIV.
symptoms_not_in_common: Dry cough is less typical than productive cough
No fever, pleuritic chest pain, purulent sputum, or focal lobar consolidation was described

data.diagnosis: HIV-associated non-Hodgkin lymphoma with pulmonary involvement
data.description: Aggressive lymphoma can occur in advanced HIV infection and may involve the lungs, producing diffuse infiltrates, nodules, lymphadenopathy, cough, and dyspnea.
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss, persistent fever, night sweats, lymph node enlargement, or discrete lung masses were described

data.description: A 65-year-old man with a 40 pack-year smoking history presented with a one-month history of worsening breathlessness and chest discomfort on walking. He came to hospital following a collapse that occurred after self-administering sublingual glyceryl trinitrate to relieve his symptoms. He reported no history of cough or coryza, had not lost weight, and experienced no haemoptysis. Laboratory testing revealed a raised serum D-dimer level.

data.diagnosis: Pulmonary lymphangitic carcinomatosis from bronchogenic carcinoma
data.description: Tumour spread through pulmonary lymphatic vessels, commonly from lung adenocarcinoma or another malignancy, causing interlobular septal thickening and asymmetric interstitial lung abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively worsening breathlessness over one month
Asymmetric right-sided interstitial/septal thickening on imaging
Small right pleural effusion on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss
No haemoptysis
No cough

data.description: Obstruction of pulmonary arterial vessels by thrombus, typically causing acute or subacute breathlessness, chest pain, syncope, and an elevated D-dimer level. Pulmonary embolism may occasionally be associated with unilateral pulmonary oedema or pleural effusion.
symptoms_not_in_common: Symptoms progressed over a month rather than having a clearly abrupt onset
No haemoptysis
Marked unilateral interlobular septal thickening is not a typical primary imaging finding of uncomplicated pulmonary embolism

data.diagnosis: Unilateral pulmonary oedema due to pulmonary venous obstruction
data.description: Pulmonary oedema confined predominantly to one lung can occur when pulmonary venous drainage is obstructed, for example by a hilar malignancy, pulmonary vein thrombosis, or severe asymmetric mitral regurgitation. CT may show smooth septal thickening, ground-glass opacity, and pleural effusion.
symptoms_in_common: Predominantly right-sided interstitial/septal thickening on imaging
Absence of infective upper respiratory symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported orthopnoea or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea
No known history of heart failure or valvular heart disease
Collapse after glyceryl trinitrate is not specific for pulmonary oedema

data.diagnosis: Primary lung cancer with right hilar/mediastinal vascular or lymphatic involvement
