data.description: A central bronchogenic malignancy may cause progressive dyspnoea and chest discomfort by obstructing bronchi, pulmonary vessels, or lymphatic drainage. Smoking is a major risk factor, and secondary lymphatic congestion can produce unilateral interstitial abnormalities and pleural fluid.
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss
No haemoptysis
No cough

data.description: Infectious or inflammatory pneumonitis can cause breathlessness and unilateral interstitial or ground-glass pulmonary opacities, sometimes with a small pleural effusion.
symptoms_in_common: Right-sided pulmonary interstitial opacity on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No cough
No coryza or other upper respiratory symptoms
No reported fever
Chest discomfort on exertion and collapse are less typical
Raised D-dimer is nonspecific and does not particularly support pneumonia

data.description: A 56-year-old woman presented with a 1-week history of shortness of breath and sore throat. Her medical history included smoking, obesity, type 2 diabetes On examination, her oxygen saturation was 81% on room air, dropping to 71% with exertion. She was afebrile with a normal white blood cell count. Chest examination revealed soft heart sounds, decreased air entry, wheeze, and aegophony at the lung bases bilaterally. Abdominal examination was normal except for obesity.

Loss of right diaphragmatic motor function causing elevation of the right hemidiaphragm, reduced lung expansion, and basal compressive atelectasis. It can cause marked dyspnea and hypoxemia, particularly in people with obesity or underlying lung disease.
symptoms_in_common: Severe hypoxemia at rest and with exertion
Decreased air entry at the lung bases
Elevated right hemidiaphragm on chest radiograph
Basal compressive atelectatic change on CT
Obesity, which can worsen ventilatory impairment
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat
Wheeze
Bilateral aegophony
Smoking history is not a direct feature of diaphragmatic paralysis

data.description: A congenital or acquired abnormal elevation of an intact but thinned or weakened diaphragm. It may compress the adjacent lung and cause dyspnea, recurrent basal atelectasis, and reduced oxygenation.
symptoms_in_common: Marked elevation of the right hemidiaphragm on imaging
Compression of the right lung base on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat
Wheeze
Bilateral aegophony
Acute 1-week onset is less typical if eventration is longstanding

data.diagnosis: Right lower-lobe and/or middle-lobe compressive atelectasis secondary to elevated right hemidiaphragm
data.description: Partial collapse of lung tissue caused by external compression and reduced ventilation from a markedly elevated diaphragm. Atelectasis can produce basal reduced breath sounds, aegophony, dyspnea, and impaired oxygenation.
symptoms_in_common: Decreased air entry at the bases
Basal lung compression/collapse visible on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat
Wheeze is not a typical primary manifestation
Bilateral findings are less well explained by isolated right-sided atelectasis
Afebrile state and normal white blood cell count do not suggest an infectious cause of atelectasis

data.description: An acute worsening of airflow limitation in a smoker, often presenting with dyspnea, wheeze, and hypoxemia. COPD may coexist with diaphragmatic dysfunction and make respiratory compromise more severe.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked unilateral elevation of the right hemidiaphragm
Basal compressive lung collapse on CT
Aegophony is not typical of uncomplicated COPD
Sore throat is nonspecific
No documented chronic cough, sputum production, or prior COPD diagnosis

data.description: 67-year-old female patient presented with chief complaint of swelling in right cheek. History of unhealed tooth extraction sockets from right upper posterior tooth extraction performed approximately one month previously. Past medical history significant for colorectal cancer treatment. Intraoral examination revealed localized, well-defined swelling measuring 4 cm × 5 cm obliterating buccal and palatal vestibules in region of unhealed extraction sockets of teeth 14, 15, and 16. Laboratory examination showed abnormal GTP level and slightly elevated serum CRP level.

data.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) of the maxilla/oral cavity
data.description: An aggressive non-Hodgkin B-cell lymphoma that may arise at extranodal sites such as the maxilla, gingiva, palate, or extraction sockets. It can present as a rapidly enlarging oral mass with bone destruction and delayed healing after dental extraction.
symptoms_in_common: Localized rapidly apparent right cheek swelling
Obliteration of buccal and palatal vestibules
Imaging appearance of a soft-tissue mass involving the right maxillary alveolar region
History of prior cancer treatment, which may be associated with immune dysregulation
symptoms_not_in_common: Abnormal GTP level is not a typical presenting feature of oral DLBCL
No constitutional B symptoms such as fever, night sweats, or weight loss were reported

data.diagnosis: Epstein-Barr virus-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
data.description: A subtype of aggressive B-cell lymphoma often occurring in older adults or people with impaired immunity. It can involve extranodal sites, including the oral cavity, and may present as a destructive mass or nonhealing extraction wound.
symptoms_in_common: Previous colorectal cancer treatment with possible treatment-related immune impairment
Localized destructive-appearing maxillary lesion on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Abnormal GTP level is not characteristic
No documented EBV testing result was provided
No fever, weight loss, or night sweats were reported

data.description: A highly aggressive lymphoma with plasmablastic cell morphology, most often affecting the oral cavity in immunocompromised individuals. It can cause rapidly enlarging oral soft-tissue masses, ulceration, bone involvement, and delayed healing after extraction.
symptoms_in_common: Large localized cheek and intraoral swelling
Possible immunocompromised state related to prior cancer treatment
Soft-tissue mass with maxillary alveolar involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Plasmablastic lymphoma is more classically associated with HIV infection or marked immunosuppression, neither of which was reported
No oral ulceration was specifically described
Abnormal GTP level is not typical

data.diagnosis: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw with secondary infection
data.description: Jawbone necrosis associated with antiresorptive or antiangiogenic cancer therapies, often triggered by tooth extraction. It commonly presents with nonhealing extraction wounds, exposed necrotic bone, swelling, pain, and secondary inflammation or infection.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent nonhealing extraction sockets after dental extraction
symptoms_not_in_common: A large well-defined 4 cm × 5 cm mass is less typical than exposed necrotic bone and sequestration
No exposed bone, purulent drainage, or severe pain was reported
The described cytologic and immunohistochemical findings favor a lymphoid neoplasm rather than osteonecrosis
No history of bisphosphonate, denosumab, or antiangiogenic therapy was provided

data.description: A bacterial infection of the maxillary alveolar bone and surrounding tissues, often following dental extraction. It may produce swelling, pain, delayed socket healing, inflammatory laboratory abnormalities, and bone destruction.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, purulent discharge, severe dental pain, or leukocytosis was reported
The lesion is described as a large well-defined mass rather than diffuse inflammatory swelling
Histologic/cytologic features and lymphoma-associated immunostains are not typical of a routine odontogenic infection
Prior cancer treatment and the apparent neoplastic imaging pattern raise concern for malignancy rather than simple infection

diagnoses.name: Primary oral diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
diagnoses.title: Diffuse large B-cell lymphomas

data.description: 24-year-old man presents with severely itchy rash that spread over two months. Had previously used an over-the-counter cream containing clobetasol, ofloxacin, terbinafine, and ornidazole which helped initially.

data.diagnosis: Tinea corporis and tinea cruris (steroid-modified tinea incognito)
data.description: A dermatophyte fungal infection of the body and groin producing annular, enlarging, scaly plaques. Prior potent topical corticosteroid use can suppress classic scale and inflammation while allowing extensive spread, termed tinea incognito.
symptoms_in_common: Large annular and polycyclic erythematous plaques with peripheral scale
Involvement of the groin and inner thighs
Partial initial improvement with a cream containing terbinafine and clobetasol
Extensive, atypical appearance after use of potent topical clobetasol

data.description: A reactive inflammatory eruption characterized by slowly expanding annular plaques, often with trailing scale inside the advancing border. It may be triggered by infections, medications, or other systemic factors.
symptoms_in_common: Rash spreading over weeks to months
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked groin-predominant involvement
Very severe itch
Initial improvement with a terbinafine-containing antifungal combination cream
Broad, markedly inflamed plaques resembling dermatophyte infection

data.description: A variant of psoriasis in which red, scaly plaques develop ring-like or polycyclic borders. It may involve the groin and other body sites but usually has a chronic relapsing course.
symptoms_in_common: Temporary improvement with potent topical clobetasol
symptoms_not_in_common: Rapid centrifugal spread over two months
Prominent ring-shaped advancing borders with central clearing
Marked worsening or atypical extension after steroid-containing combination cream
Distribution strongly centered on groin and inner thighs without described classic extensor plaques

data.description: An eczematous dermatitis causing pruritic coin-shaped erythematous, scaly plaques, commonly on the limbs. Lesions can become widespread but are usually not truly annular with an active raised edge.
symptoms_in_common: May improve temporarily with topical corticosteroids
symptoms_not_in_common: Large annular and polycyclic lesions with central clearing
Prominent active peripheral borders
Groin and inner-thigh predominance
Progressive centrifugal expansion suggestive of fungal infection

data.description: 72-year-old man with GERD previously controlled on daily omeprazole developed recurrent heartburn 11 months before admission, followed by postprandial nausea and early satiety. Symptoms gradually worsened over 9 months, progressing from solid foods to soft solids, then blended foods, and finally liquids over the 2 weeks before admission, when he became unable to tolerate liquids and presented to the emergency department. Two months before admission, EGD was limited by large retained gastric food despite 24-hour fasting; no intraluminal mass was seen. On presentation, he was thin, had a nasogastric tube, and had mild epigastric tenderness without distension.

data.diagnosis: Diffuse-type gastric adenocarcinoma (linitis plastica, including signet-ring cell carcinoma)
data.description: An infiltrative gastric cancer that spreads diffusely through the stomach wall, often sparing the mucosal surface early and causing rigid wall thickening, gastric outlet obstruction, and marked gastric dilatation.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive intolerance of solids, then soft foods, blended foods, and liquids
No obvious intraluminal mass on initial endoscopy
Imaging appearance of markedly dilated stomach with distal gastric/antral wall thickening
symptoms_not_in_common: Long history of GERD previously controlled with omeprazole

data.diagnosis: Gastric outlet obstruction from pancreatic adenocarcinoma
data.description: Cancer of the pancreatic head or adjacent pancreas can externally compress or invade the duodenum or distal stomach, producing progressive gastric outlet obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive inability to tolerate solids and liquids
symptoms_not_in_common: No pancreatic mass is described on imaging
No jaundice is reported
No dark urine or pale stools are reported
No prominent back pain is reported
Endoscopic appearance suggests intrinsic gastric wall disease rather than solely extrinsic compression

data.diagnosis: Peptic-ulcer-related benign pyloric or duodenal stricture
data.description: Chronic acid-peptic ulcer disease can scar and narrow the pylorus or proximal duodenum, causing mechanical gastric outlet obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive vomiting or inability to tolerate oral intake
Retained food in the stomach after prolonged fasting
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive infiltrative gastric wall thickening is less typical of a simple benign peptic stricture
No active peptic ulcer or scarred pyloric channel was reported on prior endoscopy
Thin appearance and prolonged progressive course raise concern for malignancy rather than uncomplicated benign stricture

data.description: A mesenchymal tumor arising from the gastric wall that may grow intramurally or exophytically and cause obstruction when located near the antrum or pylorus.
symptoms_in_common: A submucosal or intramural lesion can be missed on routine mucosal endoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: No discrete gastric mass is described
Diffuse circumferential gastric wall infiltration is less typical than a focal mass
No gastrointestinal bleeding, melena, or anemia is reported

data.description: Primary gastric lymphoma can infiltrate and thicken the gastric wall, occasionally causing outlet obstruction and systemic nutritional decline.
symptoms_in_common: Potential for obstructive symptoms if the antrum or pylorus is involved
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe progressive mechanical obstruction to liquids is less common than with infiltrative gastric adenocarcinoma
No fever, night sweats, or lymphadenopathy are reported
No discrete ulcerated gastric mass or enlarged regional lymph nodes are described

data.description: A male full-term neonate was admitted to the hospital 4 hours after birth for ecchymosis and petechiae. The infant was delivered by cesarean section at 40+5 weeks gestation due to failed induction, with birth weight 4000g and Apgar scores of 10. Physical examination revealed stable vital signs, weight 3850g, length 52cm, head circumference 35cm. The infant was alert and responsive with no special facial features. Skin examination showed large areas of ecchymosis on the chest, back, and upper limbs, with ecchymosis at the hepatitis B vaccine and vitamin K1 injection sites, and scattered pinpoint hemorrhages on the buttocks and lower limbs. The umbilical cord ligation site showed no bleeding, and cardiac, pulmonary, abdominal, and neurological examinations were normal.

An X-linked disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the WAS gene, classically characterized by thrombocytopenia with bleeding manifestations, eczema, and immune dysfunction. In neonates, bruising and petechiae from thrombocytopenia may be the first finding; the maternal carrier pattern in the sequencing image supports an X-linked inherited disorder.
symptoms_in_common: Bruising at vitamin K1 and hepatitis B injection sites
Bleeding manifestations beginning shortly after birth
Maternal sequence variant with unaffected father, compatible with X-linked inheritance
symptoms_not_in_common: No eczema reported
No recurrent or severe infections reported
No diarrhea, autoimmune manifestations, or lymphadenopathy reported

data.description: A milder phenotypic form of WAS gene-related disease characterized predominantly by congenital thrombocytopenia and mucocutaneous bleeding, often without the severe eczema and immunodeficiency of classic Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Maternal carrier-type sequencing pattern with unaffected father
symptoms_not_in_common: No other atypical symptoms are reported
No mucosal bleeding, gastrointestinal bleeding, or intracranial hemorrhage reported

data.description: A condition in which maternal antibodies against fetal platelet antigens cross the placenta and destroy fetal or neonatal platelets, causing severe thrombocytopenia, petechiae, bruising, and risk of intracranial hemorrhage in an otherwise well newborn.
symptoms_in_common: Clinically well-appearing neonate with stable vital signs
No hepatosplenomegaly or other systemic abnormalities described
symptoms_not_in_common: Sequencing findings suggesting an inherited maternal variant are not typical for an alloimmune platelet-antibody disorder
No history of a previously affected sibling or maternal platelet-antibody testing is provided

data.diagnosis: Inherited thrombocytopenia due to a platelet-production or platelet-function disorder
data.description: Inherited platelet disorders can cause congenital or neonatal thrombocytopenia and impaired primary hemostasis, producing petechiae, purpura, ecchymoses, and disproportionate bleeding after minor trauma or injections.
symptoms_in_common: Neonatal onset of petechiae and ecchymoses
Normal general examination apart from skin bleeding manifestations
symptoms_not_in_common: No platelet count, platelet size, peripheral smear findings, or platelet aggregation results are provided
No family history of thrombocytopenia or bleeding is reported

data.description: X-linked deficiencies of factor VIII or factor IX that cause impaired secondary coagulation and bleeding in male infants, particularly after trauma, procedures, or injections. Severe disease may present in the neonatal period.
symptoms_not_in_common: Petechiae are not typical of hemophilia and more strongly suggest thrombocytopenia or a platelet disorder
No prolonged bleeding from circumcision, heel sticks, umbilical stump, or other procedures is reported
No deep muscle hematoma, hemarthrosis, or intracranial bleeding is reported

data.description: 50-year-old man presented with 2-week history of constant worsening headache affecting the whole head. No history of head trauma, but reported headbanging at a Motörhead concert 4 weeks prior to presentation. Medical history was unremarkable and patient denied substance misuse. Neurological examination and laboratory studies, including coagulation screening, were normal.

data.diagnosis: Acute subdural hematoma due to headbanging
data.description: Bleeding between the dura mater and arachnoid membrane, typically caused by tearing of bridging veins after acceleration-deceleration head movement. CT commonly shows a crescent-shaped extra-axial collection with mass effect.
symptoms_in_common: Recent repetitive vigorous head movement during headbanging
Symptoms developing over days to weeks after the inciting event
CT appearance of a crescentic extra-axial collection with mass effect
symptoms_not_in_common: No recognized direct head trauma
Normal neurological examination
No coagulation abnormality

data.description: A slowly accumulating subdural blood collection that may occur after minor or unrecognized trauma and can present primarily with headache, cognitive change, or focal neurological deficits weeks later.
symptoms_in_common: Possible minor repetitive head trauma from headbanging
Delayed presentation after a provoking event
Normal laboratory coagulation screening can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: The imaging appearance may be relatively hyperdense, which is more suggestive of acute blood than a fully chronic hematoma
No cognitive decline, gait disturbance, weakness, or confusion
No focal neurological deficits

data.description: A focal bruise of brain tissue caused by traumatic acceleration-deceleration forces, most often involving the frontal or temporal lobes and potentially associated with headache and cerebral edema.
symptoms_not_in_common: No direct head impact or conventional traumatic injury reported
Normal neurological examination
No altered consciousness, seizure, vomiting, or focal neurological deficit
The dominant CT finding is more consistent with an extra-axial subdural collection than an intraparenchymal contusion

data.description: A 35-year-old woman presented to the emergency room with a clinically incarcerated umbilical hernia. Fourteen days after the initial hernia repair surgery, she developed strong pain in the right lower abdomen and complained of umbilical secretion. Physical examination revealed the patient was afebrile. Blood analysis showed a slight elevation in leukocyte count at 11.05 × 10^9/L, while other parameters were unexceptional. Ultrasound of the abdominal wall detected a semisolid infraumbilical mass with a diameter of 5.5 cm. Initial histologic examination of the resected omental fat from the hernia repair revealed malignant cells with neuroendocrine differentiation. Immunohistochemical analysis was positive for synaptophysin and protein gene product 9.5. Fluorescent in situ hybridization revealed a rearrangement of the EWSR1 gene.

data.diagnosis: Extraskeletal Ewing sarcoma / peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor (pPNET) of the omentum
data.description: A malignant small round-cell sarcoma occurring in soft tissue rather than bone. It commonly harbors an EWSR1 gene rearrangement and may show neural/neuroendocrine differentiation with synaptophysin and PGP9.5 positivity.
symptoms_not_in_common: Umbilical secretion shortly after hernia surgery
Mild leukocytosis
Presentation as a clinically incarcerated umbilical hernia

data.description: An aggressive small round-cell sarcoma that usually arises in the peritoneal cavity and may present as an abdominal or omental mass. It often carries an EWSR1-WT1 fusion, although its typical immunophenotype includes desmin and cytokeratin expression rather than predominantly neural markers.
symptoms_not_in_common: Female sex is less typical, as DSRCT more commonly affects young males
Strong neuroendocrine differentiation with synaptophysin and PGP9.5 positivity is not the classic immunophenotype
Umbilical secretion after surgery
Afebrile presentation with only mild leukocytosis

data.description: A high-grade malignant epithelial tumor with neuroendocrine differentiation, often positive for synaptophysin and other neuroendocrine markers. It can arise in or metastasize to the abdomen and peritoneum.
symptoms_not_in_common: EWSR1 rearrangement is not typical
Young age is less typical for poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma
Omental soft-tissue origin without an identified visceral primary is less typical
Umbilical secretion after hernia surgery

data.description: A malignant tumor of primitive sympathetic nervous system cells that can express synaptophysin and other neural markers. It is predominantly a childhood malignancy and is uncommon as a primary omental tumor in adults.
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 35 years is highly atypical
EWSR1 rearrangement is not characteristic
Primary omental presentation is unusual
Umbilical secretion after surgery
Minimal systemic symptoms and only slight leukocytosis

data.description: 60-year-old Japanese woman presented with a black nodule on the right postauricular area. Initial staging after radical resection and sentinel node biopsy was pT3aN0M0 stage IIA. At 19 months post-surgery, imaging detected right jugular lymph node and lung metastases. Seven courses of pembrolizumab treatment later, evaluation showed further lung metastasis and new liver metastasis. Tumor harbored BRAF V600E mutation. Thirteen days after starting dabrafenib/trametinib, patient developed fever and hepatosplenomegaly. Laboratory findings showed pancytopenia, hyperferritinemia, increased liver enzyme levels, and coagulation abnormalities.

data.diagnosis: Drug-induced hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) caused by dabrafenib plus trametinib
data.description: A life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome characterized by uncontrolled activation of macrophages and T cells, often causing fever, cytopenias, liver dysfunction, coagulopathy, hyperferritinemia, and hemophagocytosis in bone marrow. In this case it is temporally associated with initiation of BRAF/MEK inhibitor therapy.
symptoms_in_common: High fever developing 13 days after starting dabrafenib plus trametinib
Bone marrow image consistent with hemophagocytosis
Skin eruption compatible with a drug-associated inflammatory reaction
symptoms_not_in_common: Metastatic melanoma involving lung, liver, and jugular lymph node
BRAF V600E-mutated tumor

data.description: HLH can rarely occur as an immune-related adverse event from immune checkpoint inhibitors such as pembrolizumab, due to excessive immune activation. It may occur during therapy or, less commonly, after treatment exposure.
symptoms_not_in_common: The syndrome began shortly after dabrafenib plus trametinib initiation rather than during pembrolizumab treatment
No reported onset immediately following a pembrolizumab infusion
Metastatic melanoma progression despite pembrolizumab

data.diagnosis: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) due to dabrafenib/trametinib
data.description: DRESS is a severe delayed drug hypersensitivity reaction that can cause fever, rash, hepatitis, lymphadenopathy, hematologic abnormalities, and internal-organ involvement. BRAF/MEK inhibitors can cause significant drug eruptions and systemic inflammatory toxicity.
symptoms_in_common: Fever after starting a new medication
Cutaneous eruption suggested by the arm image
Systemic illness with possible liver involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Pancytopenia is less typical than eosinophilia or atypical lymphocytosis
Hyperferritinemia is more characteristic of HLH
Hepatosplenomegaly is more characteristic of HLH
Coagulation abnormalities are more suggestive of severe HLH or disseminated intravascular coagulation
No eosinophilia, facial edema, lymphadenopathy, or prolonged drug-latency period is reported

data.description: 14-year-old boy presented to trauma unit with gunshot wound to left eye. Alert and hemodynamically stable, blind in left eye, no CSF rhinorrhea. Pubertal status: Tanner stage S3, height: 1.7m (75th percentile). Laboratory findings: 8am serum cortisol 28 nmol/L (normal 171-536), thyroid-stimulating hormone 0.63 mIU/L (normal 0.27-4.20), free thyroxine 13.5 pmol/L (normal 13.6-23.2), luteinising hormone 0.7 IU/L (normal 1.3-9.8), insulin-like growth factor 1 19.4 nmol/L (normal 28.8-127.3), prolactin 13.04 pmol/L (normal 174-660.9), testosterone undetectable <0.1 nmol/L (normal 1-38.5).

data.diagnosis: Traumatic panhypopituitarism due to penetrating sellar/pituitary injury
data.description: Loss of multiple anterior pituitary hormone functions following direct traumatic injury to the pituitary gland or hypothalamic-pituitary region. The imaging suggests a retained projectile in the sellar region, making direct pituitary destruction highly likely.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly low 8am cortisol, consistent with central adrenal insufficiency
Low free thyroxine with an inappropriately non-elevated TSH, consistent with central hypothyroidism
Low luteinising hormone and undetectable testosterone, consistent with central hypogonadism
Low insulin-like growth factor 1, consistent with growth hormone deficiency
Very low prolactin, supporting pituitary tissue or stalk injury
Delayed/incomplete pubertal development for age (Tanner stage S3 at age 14)
Projectile trajectory/retained metallic fragment involving the sellar region
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute left-eye blindness from the gunshot injury
Gunshot wound to the left eye
No cerebrospinal-fluid rhinorrhea
Hemodynamic stability and alert mental status

data.diagnosis: Traumatic pituitary stalk injury or hypothalamic-pituitary disconnection
data.description: Damage to the pituitary stalk or hypothalamus can interrupt hypothalamic releasing hormones and reduce anterior pituitary hormone secretion. In a complete stalk injury, prolactin is often elevated because dopamine inhibition is lost; however, direct pituitary damage can instead cause low prolactin.
symptoms_in_common: Low cortisol suggesting impaired ACTH stimulation
Low free thyroxine with non-elevated TSH
Pubertal delay or impaired pubertal progression
Penetrating trauma near the sellar and suprasellar region
symptoms_not_in_common: Low prolactin is less typical of isolated pituitary stalk transection, which often produces elevated prolactin
No reported polyuria, polydipsia, or hypernatremia to suggest associated central diabetes insipidus
Acute unilateral blindness is more directly explained by ocular trauma
No cerebrospinal-fluid rhinorrhea

data.diagnosis: Central adrenal insufficiency secondary to traumatic ACTH deficiency
data.description: Central adrenal insufficiency occurs when inadequate ACTH secretion from the pituitary or hypothalamus causes deficient cortisol production. It can be life-threatening during acute illness or trauma despite initially stable vital signs.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple additional anterior pituitary hormone deficiencies supporting central rather than primary adrenal disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported hypotension
No reported hypoglycemia
No reported vomiting, abdominal pain, weakness, or collapse
No hyperpigmentation, which would be more consistent with primary adrenal insufficiency
Left-eye blindness is not a typical feature

data.diagnosis: Central hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with delayed puberty
data.description: Reduced hypothalamic GnRH or pituitary gonadotropin secretion leads to low LH/FSH and low testosterone, resulting in delayed or arrested pubertal development. In this case it is likely part of broader traumatic hypopituitarism.
symptoms_in_common: Tanner stage S3 at age 14, suggesting delayed or incomplete pubertal progression
Low IGF-1 and other pituitary hormone abnormalities indicating hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute left-eye blindness is not typical
Gunshot wound is not a usual presentation of isolated hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
Markedly low cortisol and central hypothyroidism indicate disease beyond isolated gonadotropin deficiency
No reported chronic symptoms such as reduced libido, absent secondary sexual characteristics, or infertility

data.description: 14-month-old girl with 3 months of recurrent episodic vomiting, starting at 11 months of age, with four episodes lasting 3–5 days and associated with lethargy, decreased oral intake, and intermittent diarrhea. Over the same period, she had developmental regression, no longer attempting to walk and instead crawling unsteadily with occasional falls. Parents reported brief morning shaking episodes with symmetric movements lasting seconds over about 10 minutes, without loss of consciousness. Born full-term without complications. On examination, she was alert and interactive but had frontal bossing, a full fontanelle with visible pulsations when supine, head circumference 51.5 cm, decreased leg tone, brisk 3+ patellar reflexes, and flexor plantar responses. Eye movements were normal, with reactive pupils and no nystagmus or gaze limitation.

data.diagnosis: Congenital aqueductal stenosis causing obstructive hydrocephalus
data.description: Narrowing or obstruction of the cerebral aqueduct blocks cerebrospinal fluid flow from the third to fourth ventricle, producing marked enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles with a relatively normal fourth ventricle. It may present in infancy with progressive macrocephaly and signs of raised intracranial pressure.
symptoms_in_common: Loss of walking ability and unsteady crawling
MRI appearance of severe obstructive ventriculomegaly involving the lateral and third ventricles
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent diarrhea
Brief symmetric morning shaking episodes without loss of consciousness

data.diagnosis: Obstructive hydrocephalus due to a tectal glioma
data.description: A low-grade tumor of the tectal plate can compress the cerebral aqueduct and cause progressive obstructive hydrocephalus. Children may initially present primarily with symptoms of elevated intracranial pressure rather than focal neurologic signs.
symptoms_in_common: Obstructive pattern of hydrocephalus on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported tectal mass on the provided imaging
Normal eye movements without vertical gaze limitation
Intermittent diarrhea
Brief shaking episodes are not a typical primary manifestation

data.diagnosis: Hydrocephalus due to an intraventricular cyst or aqueductal web
data.description: A congenital membrane, web, or cyst near the cerebral aqueduct can intermittently or progressively obstruct cerebrospinal fluid flow, leading to triventricular hydrocephalus and raised intracranial pressure.
symptoms_in_common: MRI findings compatible with obstruction at the aqueductal level
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent diarrhea
Brief symmetric shaking episodes without impaired consciousness

data.description: A choroid plexus papilloma is a benign intraventricular tumor that can cause hydrocephalus through cerebrospinal fluid overproduction, obstruction, or both. It often presents in young children with macrocephaly and increased intracranial pressure.
symptoms_not_in_common: No intraventricular enhancing mass is described on the imaging
The imaging pattern appears more consistent with aqueduct-level obstruction than diffuse cerebrospinal fluid overproduction
Intermittent diarrhea
Brief shaking episodes without loss of consciousness

data.diagnosis: Dandy-Walker malformation or other posterior fossa cerebrospinal fluid-flow malformation
data.description: Dandy-Walker spectrum disorders involve abnormal development of the cerebellar vermis and fourth ventricle and may lead to hydrocephalus, developmental delay, and progressive macrocephaly in infancy.
symptoms_in_common: Vomiting suggestive of raised intracranial pressure
symptoms_not_in_common: Imaging does not describe an enlarged fourth ventricle or posterior fossa cyst
No cerebellar vermian hypoplasia is described
Brisk patellar reflexes are less characteristic than cerebellar hypotonia or ataxia
Intermittent diarrhea
Brief shaking episodes without loss of consciousness

diagnoses.name: Aqueductal stenosis
diagnoses.title: Stenosis of the aqueduct of Sylvius

data.description: 31-year-old man with sleep apnea and a 6-month history of lethargy and intermittent headaches, referred for newly diagnosed hypertension. Blood pressure was repeatedly elevated (170/128, 164/110, 173/110 mm Hg). He was an ex-smoker with a 20 pack-year history. On examination, heart rate was 106 bpm and BMI 34; no cushingoid features, hyperpigmentation, renal or carotid bruits, or tremor were noted. Full blood count, urea, electrolytes, and renal artery Doppler were normal. Laboratory tests showed elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio (157) with normal serum aldosterone and low plasma renin, and mildly elevated 24-hour urinary cortisol with suppressed post-dexamethasone cortisol and low ACTH.
A cause of secondary hypertension due to inappropriate aldosterone activity, usually from an adrenal adenoma or bilateral adrenal hyperplasia, producing sodium retention and suppression of renin.
symptoms_in_common: Severe persistent hypertension at a young age
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal serum aldosterone
Normal electrolytes, with no reported hypokalemia
Mildly elevated urinary cortisol

data.diagnosis: Low-renin essential hypertension associated with obesity and obstructive sleep apnea
data.description: Primary hypertension can be associated with obesity and obstructive sleep apnea; these conditions increase sympathetic activity and may suppress renin through relative volume expansion.
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio
Mildly elevated 24-hour urinary cortisol

data.description: Cushing syndrome is chronic excess cortisol production, which can cause hypertension, obesity, fatigue, glucose intolerance, and characteristic physical changes.
symptoms_not_in_common: Suppressed cortisol after dexamethasone, arguing against autonomous cortisol excess
Low ACTH without persistent nonsuppressible cortisol elevation
No cushingoid physical features
No reported diabetes, proximal muscle weakness, easy bruising, or purple striae
Elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio with low renin

data.diagnosis: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess or another low-renin mineralocorticoid hypertension syndrome
data.description: These disorders cause hypertension through mineralocorticoid receptor activation independent of aldosterone, leading to low renin and often low or normal aldosterone. Causes include inherited enzyme defects, licorice ingestion, or other mineralocorticoid-like states.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported hypokalemia or metabolic alkalosis
No history provided of licorice use, chewing tobacco, or causative medication exposure
Elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio may be misleading but is not the classic biochemical pattern
Obstructive sleep apnea and obesity provide an alternative explanation for hypertension

data.description: 46-year-old woman who experienced chest pain before having an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Pre-arrest rhythm strip showed sinus tachycardia. Initial troponin I was 5.9 μg/L (normal: 0-0.04 μg/L). Medical history included similar chest pain episode one year prior after taking sumatriptan for migraine, with transient inferior and lateral ST elevation on ECG but negative troponin at that time. Previous coronary angiography showed normal left coronary system and dominant right coronary artery with minor ostial spasm and slow flow. Negative bubble study for right to left shunting. Current medications: oral diltiazem, nicorandil, lansoprazole, and beclometasone inhaler. Patient was a former smoker.

data.diagnosis: Vasospastic angina (Prinzmetal angina) with coronary artery spasm
data.description: Transient constriction of an epicardial coronary artery causing myocardial ischemia, often with transient ST-segment elevation and potentially malignant ventricular arrhythmias or cardiac arrest.
symptoms_in_common: Transient inferior and lateral ST-segment elevation during a prior episode
Minor ostial right coronary artery spasm on previous angiography
Slow coronary flow despite no obstructive coronary disease
Chest pain temporally associated with sumatriptan use
Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest following chest pain
Markedly elevated troponin during the current event
Use of diltiazem and nicorandil, medications commonly used for coronary vasospasm
symptoms_not_in_common: No major symptoms are clearly atypical; sinus tachycardia before arrest is nonspecific

data.diagnosis: Acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction due to coronary vasospasm
data.description: Acute myocardial infarction caused by prolonged coronary vasospasm leading to sustained ischemia and myocardial necrosis, even in the absence of fixed obstructive coronary artery disease.
symptoms_in_common: Acute chest pain preceding cardiac arrest
Marked troponin I elevation to 5.9 μg/L
ECG appearance consistent with acute anterior ST-segment elevation/acute transmural ischemia
Prior angiography without significant fixed coronary obstruction, supporting a non-atherosclerotic mechanism such as spasm
Cardiac arrest as a complication of severe acute ischemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Previous episode had negative troponin despite ST elevation, which is more consistent with transient ischemia without infarction
No documented persistent obstructive coronary lesion is described

data.diagnosis: Sumatriptan-induced coronary vasospasm and myocardial ischemia
data.description: A medication-associated coronary vasospasm syndrome in which triptan-induced serotonergic vasoconstriction triggers myocardial ischemia, ST-segment elevation, infarction, or rarely cardiac arrest.
symptoms_in_common: A similar prior chest-pain event occurred after taking sumatriptan
Prior transient inferior and lateral ST-segment elevation after sumatriptan exposure
Previously normal coronary angiography apart from minor spasm and slow flow
Current presentation is compatible with recurrent severe coronary vasospasm
Cardiac arrest and elevated troponin can occur in severe medication-associated coronary spasm
symptoms_not_in_common: Current sumatriptan exposure immediately before the cardiac arrest is not explicitly reported
The patient is taking diltiazem and nicorandil, which would generally be expected to reduce spasm risk

data.diagnosis: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA)
data.description: Myocardial infarction meeting biomarker and clinical criteria for acute ischemia without obstructive coronary artery disease on angiography; possible mechanisms include coronary vasospasm, microvascular dysfunction, embolism, spontaneous coronary artery dissection, and plaque disruption.
symptoms_in_common: Previous angiography showing no significant obstructive coronary artery disease
Female sex and relatively young age for conventional obstructive coronary disease
Potential vasospasm mechanism demonstrated on prior angiography
symptoms_not_in_common: The current coronary angiographic findings are not provided, so non-obstructive coronary arteries during the current infarction are not confirmed
Prior documented coronary spasm provides a more specific explanation than MINOCA as a broad syndrome

data.description: A 44-year-old woman with cerebral palsy and multiple sclerosis (diagnosed at age 16) presented to the emergency department with four days of acute constipation and vomiting. She had a history of chronic constipation due to neurogenic bowel dysfunction secondary to her underlying conditions, initially managed with laxatives. Her constipation had become severe enough to warrant insertion of a sacral anterior root stimulator in the last year. On examination, her abdomen was markedly distended, diffusely tender, with absent bowel sounds. There was no guarding, rigidity, or previous incisions, and all hernia orifices were intact. Vital signs showed tachycardia (140 beats/min), tachypnea, normal blood pressure (130/60 mmHg), and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. Laboratory findings revealed normal pH of 7.36, hypocapnea (PCO2 29mmHg), hyperlactataemia (20 mg/dL), normal PO2 (), white blood cell count of 10,500 cells/mm3 (73% neutrophils), and elevated C-reactive protein of 3.25 mg/dL.

data.diagnosis: Sigmoid volvulus with acute large-bowel obstruction
data.description: Twisting of the sigmoid colon around its mesentery, causing a closed-loop large-bowel obstruction. It is strongly associated with chronic constipation, neurologic disease, and institutionalized or immobile patients. The imaging appearance is consistent with a markedly dilated, obstructed colon.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic constipation and neurogenic bowel dysfunction
Neurologic disease with impaired bowel motility
Dilated large-bowel loops and air-fluid levels on abdominal imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No prior episodes of volvulus are reported
No peritoneal guarding or rigidity
No hypotension

data.description: Functional obstruction with massive colonic dilatation in the absence of a fixed mechanical blockage. It commonly occurs in patients with severe neurologic disease, immobility, metabolic illness, or medications affecting intestinal motility.
symptoms_in_common: Underlying cerebral palsy and multiple sclerosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Four days of complete acute obstruction may be more suggestive of a mechanical obstruction such as volvulus
Air-fluid levels and a possible closed-loop configuration favor mechanical obstruction
Elevated lactate raises concern for bowel ischemia rather than uncomplicated pseudo-obstruction

data.description: Inflammation and pressure injury of the colon caused by impacted stool, usually in patients with severe chronic constipation, neurologic impairment, dehydration, or limited mobility. It can progress to ischemia, ulceration, perforation, and sepsis.
symptoms_in_common: Fecal loading/impaction visible on CT imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported fever
No guarding, rigidity, or clear peritonitis
The degree of gaseous colonic dilatation may be more typical of volvulus or pseudo-obstruction than isolated fecal impaction

data.diagnosis: Ischemic colitis or impending colonic ischemia secondary to obstructive megacolon
data.description: Compromised blood flow to the colon due to severe distension or a closed-loop obstruction, such as volvulus. This can cause bowel-wall ischemia, pneumatosis, necrosis, perforation, and systemic deterioration.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported bloody diarrhea or rectal bleeding
No hypotension
No guarding or rigidity despite concern for advanced ischemia
Normal arterial pH

data.description: 64-year-old man with 5 months of cough with thin yellow sputum, exertional dyspnea, chest tightness, and wheezing. Ten days before presentation he developed lethargy, myalgias, chills, headaches, anorexia, and night sweats. On presentation he had fever, tachycardia, dyspnea, bitemporal bandlike headaches, neck stiffness, and photophobia. Exam showed neck stiffness, inspiratory crackles bilaterally, and mild synovial thickening in the hands consistent with chronic arthritic changes. Past history included fibromyalgia, L5 radiculopathy with foot drop, carpal tunnel syndrome, knee and neck osteoarthritis, cervical spondylosis, sleep apnea, and peptic ulcer disease. He worked in a healthcare facility and had recent travel to Florida and Europe/Caribbean.

Opportunistic fungal pneumonia, usually in patients with impaired cellular immunity such as undiagnosed HIV infection, hematologic malignancy, or immunosuppressive therapy. CT commonly shows diffuse ground-glass opacities and may show small nodules; direct fluorescent staining of respiratory specimens can demonstrate characteristic cysts.
symptoms_not_in_common: Thin yellow sputum, since PJP cough is often nonproductive
Wheezing
Neck stiffness
Photophobia
Bitemporal bandlike headache
Meningeal symptoms

data.diagnosis: Disseminated cryptococcosis with cryptococcal meningitis and pulmonary cryptococcosis
data.description: Infection caused by Cryptococcus neoformans or Cryptococcus gattii, often affecting immunocompromised individuals. It may cause subacute pulmonary disease with nodules or infiltrates and can disseminate to the central nervous system, producing subacute meningitis with headache, fever, and neck stiffness.
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent wheezing
Thin yellow sputum
Acute onset of severe constitutional symptoms over only 10 days, although this can occur
Chronic hand synovial thickening

data.diagnosis: Tuberculosis with pulmonary and tuberculous meningitis involvement
data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection can cause chronic cough, constitutional symptoms, pulmonary nodules or tree-in-bud opacities, and subacute meningitis. Healthcare exposure and travel may increase exposure risk.
symptoms_not_in_common: Wheezing
Chest tightness
Acute respiratory worsening over a short period
No reported weight loss
No reported hemoptysis

data.description: Legionella pneumophila causes an atypical pneumonia associated with fever, cough, dyspnea, headache, myalgias, and gastrointestinal or neurologic manifestations. Exposure to contaminated water systems, including those in healthcare facilities or hotels during travel, is a risk factor.
symptoms_not_in_common: Five-month duration of cough before systemic illness
Neck stiffness and photophobia suggesting true meningitis
Night sweats over a chronic course
Diffuse small pulmonary nodules rather than typical focal or multilobar consolidation
Chronic wheezing

data.diagnosis: Disseminated histoplasmosis with central nervous system involvement
data.description: Histoplasma capsulatum infection is acquired by inhalation and can produce pulmonary nodules, diffuse infiltrates, constitutional symptoms, and, especially in immunocompromised patients, disseminated infection including chronic meningitis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Wheezing
Chest tightness
Thin yellow sputum
Rapid development of meningeal symptoms
No reported bird, bat, cave, or heavy soil exposure

data.description: 47-year-old woman admitted with left lumbar pain and macroscopic hematuria. Past medical history unremarkable. Physical examination showed pale skin, no peripheral edema, blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, and diuresis of 1000 mL/day. Laboratory studies showed moderate normocytic anemia, elevated creatinine, heavy proteinuria, hematuria, and hypoalbuminemia. ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-Ro, anti-La, anti-Sm, anti-RNP, anti-β2-glycoprotein 1, antiphospholipid, cANCA, pANCA, anti-GBM antibodies, cryoglobulins, rheumatoid factor, hepatitis B/C, HIV, and serum protein electrophoresis were negative.

A kidney vascular injury pattern caused by endothelial damage and microvascular thrombosis, producing glomerular ischemia, arteriolar intimal thickening, and renal dysfunction. The biopsy appearance is compatible with TMA.
symptoms_in_common: Reduced urine output relative to normal daily diuresis
symptoms_not_in_common: Left lumbar pain
Absence of hypertension
No peripheral edema

data.diagnosis: Complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome)
data.description: A form of thrombotic microangiopathy caused by dysregulation of the alternative complement pathway. It may be kidney-predominant and can occur without diarrhea or severe hypertension.
symptoms_in_common: Acute kidney dysfunction with elevated creatinine
Renal biopsy features suggestive of thrombotic microangiopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Macroscopic hematuria is less typical than microscopic hematuria
Left lumbar pain is not a typical presenting feature
No documented thrombocytopenia
No documented laboratory evidence of hemolysis

data.description: A kidney-predominant form of thrombotic microangiopathy in which biopsy shows TMA lesions but systemic manifestations such as thrombocytopenia and overt hemolytic anemia may be absent or mild.
symptoms_in_common: Negative autoimmune, ANCA, anti-GBM, antiphospholipid, viral, and monoclonal-protein testing
symptoms_not_in_common: Left lumbar pain is not characteristic
Macroscopic hematuria is less common than microscopic hematuria
No peripheral edema despite hypoalbuminemia

data.description: Severe hypertension can damage renal arterioles and glomerular capillaries, causing a thrombotic microangiopathy pattern with renal failure, hematuria, proteinuria, and anemia.
symptoms_in_common: Biopsy pattern compatible with thrombotic microangiopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, which does not support malignant hypertension
No history of hypertension
Left lumbar pain is not typical
No peripheral edema

data.description: A 31-year-old female, G3P2, came in with 5-day history of severe menorrhagia. She was treated medically and discharged. She was readmitted 2 days later with menorrhagia and anaemia (haemoglobin of 77). The patient had suffered a spontaneous miscarriage a few months earlier.

An abnormal high-flow connection between uterine arteries and veins, often acquired after pregnancy-related events such as miscarriage, curettage, or uterine trauma. It can cause sudden, recurrent, life-threatening uterine bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Marked blood-loss anaemia with haemoglobin of 77
Recurrent bleeding despite initial medical treatment

data.description: Persistence of placental or fetal tissue within the uterus after miscarriage or pregnancy termination, causing continued or delayed vaginal bleeding and sometimes infection.
symptoms_in_common: History of spontaneous miscarriage a few months earlier
symptoms_not_in_common: Bleeding occurring several months after the miscarriage is less typical than bleeding soon after pregnancy loss
No fever, pelvic pain, uterine tenderness, or foul-smelling discharge is reported

data.diagnosis: Gestational trophoblastic disease (persistent gestational trophoblastic neoplasia)
data.description: Abnormal persistent proliferation of pregnancy-related trophoblastic tissue after a pregnancy event, including miscarriage; it may produce irregular or heavy uterine bleeding and can be highly vascular.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent or recurrent abnormal uterine bleeding
symptoms_not_in_common: No information is provided about persistently elevated beta-hCG
No symptoms of metastatic disease are reported
No uterine enlargement or pregnancy-related systemic symptoms are reported

data.description: A benign smooth-muscle tumour of the uterus. Fibroids projecting into the uterine cavity commonly cause heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding and iron-deficiency anaemia.
symptoms_in_common: Age within the common reproductive-age range for fibroids
symptoms_not_in_common: The close temporal association with a recent miscarriage favors a pregnancy-related vascular or retained-tissue cause
No chronic history of heavy periods, pelvic pressure, enlarged uterus, or bulk-related symptoms is reported

data.description: 28-year-old man with abdominal pain and 10–12 watery stools/day after completing azithromycin for pneumonia. Six weeks later, after symptoms resolved and bowel habits returned to baseline, he developed 3 weeks of abdominal discomfort relieved by bowel movements with increased stool frequency to 4–5 stools/day. At the second presentation, vital signs and physical examination were unremarkable. Clostridium difficile PCR was positive; white blood cell count and other listed labs were within normal limits.

C. difficile infection is antibiotic-associated colitis caused by toxin-producing C. difficile, often presenting with watery diarrhea and abdominal cramping. Recurrence can occur weeks after apparent resolution of an initial episode.
symptoms_in_common: Recent azithromycin exposure before initial onset
Recurrent increased stool frequency after a symptom-free interval
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
Normal white blood cell count
Normal vital signs and unremarkable abdominal examination

data.description: Post-infectious irritable bowel syndrome is a functional bowel disorder that can develop after an episode of infectious or antibiotic-associated diarrhea, causing persistent or recurrent abdominal discomfort with altered bowel habits.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal discomfort relieved by bowel movements
Symptoms developing after a prior diarrheal illness
Normal vital signs and physical examination
symptoms_not_in_common: Initial severe watery diarrhea of 10–12 stools/day
Positive Clostridium difficile PCR
Symptoms beginning immediately after antibiotic therapy

data.description: Antibiotic-associated diarrhea is diarrhea occurring during or shortly after antibiotic use due to disruption of the normal intestinal microbiota. It may be mild and noninfectious or may reflect C. difficile infection.
symptoms_not_in_common: Recurrent bowel symptoms six weeks after complete resolution
Positive Clostridium difficile PCR, which suggests a specific C. difficile-related process rather than uncomplicated antibiotic-associated diarrhea

data.diagnosis: Clostridioides difficile colonization with another cause of diarrhea
data.description: C. difficile colonization refers to detection of C. difficile by PCR without active toxin-mediated disease. PCR can remain positive after prior infection or identify asymptomatic carriage, while diarrhea may be due to another condition such as post-infectious bowel dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: Normal vital signs and unremarkable physical examination
Milder recurrent symptoms at the second presentation compared with the initial illness
Abdominal discomfort relieved by bowel movements
symptoms_not_in_common: Frequent watery diarrhea after antibiotic exposure is more suggestive of active C. difficile infection than asymptomatic colonization
Initial stool frequency of 10–12 watery stools/day

diagnoses.name: Clostridioides difficile colonization
diagnoses.title: Intestinal infections due to Clostridioides difficile

data.description: 29-year-old man with 6 weeks of unintentional 10 kg weight loss, severe upper abdominal pain radiating to the throat and worsened by eating, followed 3 weeks later by nausea, intermittent vomiting, decreased oral intake, one episode of hematemesis, sore throat, and fever. Past history included a respiratory illness 2 years earlier and chronic macular hyperpigmentation of the feet and legs for 10 years. On exam he was cachectic, tachycardic, and febrile, with low BMI, white exudate on the underside of the tongue, coarse breath sounds with fine rales at both lung bases, and multiple nontender mobile submandibular, submental, and cervical lymph nodes (1–2 cm). Labs showed anemia, lymphopenia with marked CD4 depletion, elevated HIV-1 RNA, and positive HIV serology.
Systemic infection with Histoplasma capsulatum, often occurring in advanced HIV/AIDS; it can involve the lungs, reticuloendothelial system, lymph nodes, gastrointestinal tract, and bone marrow.
symptoms_in_common: Advanced HIV infection with marked CD4 depletion
Severe unintentional weight loss and cachexia
Diffuse small pulmonary nodules/interstitial infiltrates on chest imaging
Abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and poor oral intake
Possible gastrointestinal bleeding manifested by hematemesis
symptoms_not_in_common: White oral/tongue exudate is more suggestive of oral candidiasis
Chronic macular hyperpigmentation of the feet and legs for 10 years is not a typical manifestation
Pain radiating specifically to the throat is not characteristic

data.diagnosis: Disseminated tuberculosis with miliary pulmonary tuberculosis
data.description: Hematogenous dissemination of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, particularly likely in severe immunosuppression, producing diffuse tiny pulmonary nodules and potentially involving lymph nodes and the gastrointestinal tract.
symptoms_in_common: Advanced HIV infection with severe CD4 depletion
Diffuse micronodular pulmonary pattern compatible with miliary spread
Coarse breath sounds and bibasilar fine rales
Abdominal pain, anorexia, nausea, and vomiting
History of a prior respiratory illness
symptoms_not_in_common: White oral/tongue exudate is not typical of tuberculosis
Hematemesis is possible with gastrointestinal involvement but is not a common presentation
Severe upper abdominal pain radiating to the throat is not typical
Longstanding macular hyperpigmentation is not typical of tuberculosis

data.description: Opportunistic disseminated infection caused by nontuberculous mycobacteria, usually occurring in patients with advanced AIDS and very low CD4 counts; it commonly causes constitutional, hematologic, lymph node, liver, spleen, and gastrointestinal manifestations.
symptoms_in_common: Possible diffuse pulmonary nodular abnormalities in immunocompromised patients
symptoms_not_in_common: Pulmonary findings are less prominent in disseminated MAC than in miliary tuberculosis or histoplasmosis
One episode of hematemesis is not a typical feature
White oral/tongue exudate suggests concomitant candidiasis rather than MAC
Chronic leg and foot hyperpigmentation is not typical

data.description: An opportunistic fungal pneumonia in advanced HIV/AIDS, classically causing subacute fever, dyspnea, dry cough, hypoxemia, and diffuse bilateral ground-glass pulmonary opacities.
symptoms_in_common: Advanced HIV infection with marked CD4 depletion
symptoms_not_in_common: No dyspnea is reported
No dry cough is reported
Micronodular pulmonary pattern is less typical than diffuse ground-glass opacity
Prominent cervical lymphadenopathy is not typical
Severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and hematemesis are not typical
White oral/tongue exudate is not caused by Pneumocystis
Chronic skin hyperpigmentation is not typical

data.description: Aggressive B-cell lymphoma associated with advanced HIV infection that may involve lymph nodes, lungs, gastrointestinal tract, and bone marrow, causing systemic symptoms and gastrointestinal bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple cervical, submandibular, and submental lymph nodes
Nausea, vomiting, and reduced oral intake
Pulmonary nodules or infiltrates can occur with extranodal disease
symptoms_not_in_common: The lymph nodes are described as small, mobile, and nontender rather than large or progressively enlarging
Diffuse miliary-type pulmonary micronodules more strongly suggest disseminated infection
White oral/tongue exudate is more suggestive of candidiasis
Longstanding lower-extremity hyperpigmentation is not typical

data.description: 65-year-old Haitian man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, hypertension, bicuspid aortic valve with ascending/aortic-root aneurysm, prior treated secondary syphilis, positive tuberculin skin test with negative chest radiograph, and recent HTLV-1 positivity. He had 12 kg unintentional weight loss over 2 years and presented with a leg injury and diffuse pruritic rash. Examination showed bilateral wrinkled axillary plaques, multiple thin brown macules and patches with collarette scale on the palms and some soles, and bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy.

data.diagnosis: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL) with cutaneous involvement
data.description: An aggressive mature T-cell neoplasm caused by HTLV-1 infection, often occurring in people from HTLV-1-endemic regions. It may present with pruritic, polymorphic skin lesions, lymphadenopathy, constitutional symptoms, blood involvement, hypercalcemia, and systemic organ disease.
symptoms_in_common: Haitian origin from an HTLV-1-endemic population
Thin brown macules and patches with scale
Skin biopsy appearance consistent with epidermotropic atypical lymphoid infiltration
symptoms_not_in_common: Leg injury as the presenting reason for evaluation
End-stage renal disease on hemodialysis
Bicuspid aortic valve with ascending aortic-root aneurysm

data.description: Mycosis fungoides is the most common primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and typically causes slowly progressive, pruritic patches, plaques, or tumors with epidermotropic atypical T lymphocytes on biopsy.
symptoms_in_common: Weight loss and lymphadenopathy can occur in advanced disease
symptoms_not_in_common: HTLV-1 positivity, which strongly favors ATLL rather than classic mycosis fungoides
Prominent palmar and plantar collarette scaling
Bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy at presentation
Haitian epidemiologic background specifically associated with HTLV-1-related ATLL

data.description: Secondary syphilis is a disseminated stage of Treponema pallidum infection that can cause a generalized papulosquamous eruption, classically involving the palms and soles, along with generalized lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Brown macules and patches with collarette scale
symptoms_not_in_common: Previously treated secondary syphilis
Wrinkled axillary plaques are not a classic secondary-syphilis finding
HTLV-1 positivity
Skin histology suggestive of epidermotropic atypical lymphoid cells rather than the plasma-cell-rich infiltrate typical of syphilis
Longstanding progressive weight loss over 2 years

data.description: Scabies is an infestation by Sarcoptes scabiei that causes intense pruritus and papules, excoriations, burrows, or eczematous plaques, often affecting finger webs, wrists, axillae, genital areas, and sometimes palms and soles.
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy
Marked unintentional weight loss
Thin brown macules and patches with collarette scale rather than burrows or excoriated papules
HTLV-1 positivity
Histologic epidermotropic atypical lymphoid infiltrate

data.description: 52-year-old man with a 2-week history of exertional central chest fullness and dyspnea, absent at rest, without light-headedness or syncope. Past history includes type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea on CPAP, and family history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Prior screening echocardiogram 3 years earlier showed mild left ventricular hypertrophy with otherwise normal structure and function. Exam: afebrile, BP 146/70 mmHg, HR 70/min, RR 14/min, BMI 36.2; normal JVP, regular rhythm without murmurs/rubs/gallops, normal lung and abdominal exams, no leg edema, symmetric pulses. Labs notable for creatinine 1.6 mg/dL (baseline 1.0), potassium 5.4 mmol/L, WBC 10,900/mm³; troponin I, INR, and TSH were normal.

A rare, rapidly progressive inflammatory myocarditis characterized histologically by myocardial inflammation, necrosis, and multinucleated giant cells. It commonly causes ventricular arrhythmias, conduction disease, heart failure, and sudden cardiac death.
symptoms_in_common: Sustained wide-complex ventricular tachycardia on ECG
Myocardial biopsy image showing inflammatory infiltrates with multinucleated giant cells
Previously only mild left ventricular hypertrophy with subsequently acute cardiac symptoms
Normal troponin does not exclude myocarditis
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No resting dyspnea
No syncope or light-headedness
No clinical signs of overt heart failure such as elevated JVP, pulmonary crackles, or peripheral edema

data.description: Granulomatous inflammation involving the myocardium that can produce ventricular arrhythmias, atrioventricular block, heart failure, and scar-related cardiomyopathy. Histology usually demonstrates noncaseating granulomas, sometimes with giant cells.
symptoms_in_common: Inflammatory myocardial pathology containing giant cells
Possible progressive myocardial involvement despite a previously largely normal echocardiogram
symptoms_not_in_common: No known pulmonary sarcoidosis
No reported hilar adenopathy, cough, skin lesions, uveitis, or other extracardiac sarcoidosis manifestations
No documented atrioventricular block
No syncope
Histology appears more consistent with diffuse giant-cell myocarditis than well-formed noncaseating granulomas

data.description: An inherited myocardial disorder characterized by unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy, myocyte disarray, fibrosis, exertional symptoms, and increased risk of ventricular arrhythmias or sudden cardiac death.
symptoms_in_common: Prior echocardiogram showing mild left ventricular hypertrophy
Ventricular tachycardia can occur in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: No murmur suggestive of dynamic left ventricular outflow obstruction
No syncope or presyncope
No documented marked asymmetric septal hypertrophy or systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve
Myocardial biopsy with prominent inflammation and multinucleated giant cells is not typical of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
The acute 2-week presentation is less typical than the chronic course of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

data.diagnosis: Coronary artery disease with exertional angina
data.description: Atherosclerotic narrowing of coronary arteries causes myocardial oxygen supply-demand mismatch, typically producing exertional chest pressure and dyspnea. It may also predispose to ventricular arrhythmias when ischemia or scar is present.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional central chest fullness relieved by rest
Ventricular arrhythmia may occur with significant ischemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal troponin I
No ischemic ST-segment elevation described on the ECGs
No known prior myocardial infarction
Myocardial biopsy showing giant-cell inflammatory myocarditis is not typical of coronary artery disease
No resting chest pain

data.description: 32-year-old woman, pregnant at 31 weeks and 4 days, with history of CIN II treated by loop excision 2 years earlier and prior bilateral breast reduction. During pregnancy she was diagnosed with chronic hypertension at 18 weeks. She presented with 2 weeks of flu-like symptoms, headache, and sore throat followed by lower abdominal pain and fever. Exam showed temperature 38.3°C, uterine contractions, fundal height at 29 weeks, and a cervix 1 cm dilated and fully effaced with intact membranes. Ultrasound showed fetal growth at the 5th percentile with oligohydramnios, and fetal monitoring showed tachycardia with late decelerations. Labs revealed marked leukocytosis with neutrophilia and elevated C-reactive protein. After cesarean delivery, she developed persistent fever, rising inflammatory markers, and a non-healing surgical wound despite antibiotics and standard wound care.
A rare neutrophilic inflammatory dermatosis causing rapidly progressive, painful ulceration after trauma or surgery (pathergy). Surgical debridement can worsen the wound.
symptoms_in_common: Non-healing cesarean surgical wound despite antibiotics and standard wound care
Ulcerated postoperative wound with purulent-appearing yellow material
Violaceous or dusky undermined wound borders visible in the image
Persistent fever and rising inflammatory markers
symptoms_not_in_common: Two weeks of flu-like symptoms and sore throat before delivery
Preterm contractions and cervical effacement
Oligohydramnios
Fetal growth restriction
Fetal tachycardia with late decelerations

data.diagnosis: Postpartum wound infection / cesarean surgical-site infection
data.description: A bacterial infection involving the cesarean incision, ranging from superficial cellulitis to deep incisional infection, often causing fever, leukocytosis, wound drainage, and delayed healing.
symptoms_in_common: Open wound with yellow exudate and surrounding erythema
symptoms_not_in_common: Failure to improve despite antibiotics and standard wound care
Violaceous undermined-appearing wound edges, which are more suggestive of pyoderma gangrenosum
Flu-like prodrome and sore throat before labor
Fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios

data.description: A rapidly progressive, life-threatening bacterial infection of fascia and soft tissue that may occur after surgery and causes systemic toxicity, severe pain, tissue necrosis, and wound breakdown.
symptoms_in_common: Rapid postoperative wound deterioration and failure to heal
Wound with necrotic-appearing tissue and exudate
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported severe pain out of proportion to examination
No reported crepitus, bullae, skin anesthesia, or rapidly spreading black necrosis
Persistence despite antibiotics without mention of hemodynamic collapse may be less typical
Violaceous ulcer edges and apparent pathergic postoperative worsening favor pyoderma gangrenosum

data.description: An infection and inflammation of the amniotic fluid, placenta, membranes, or uterus, usually presenting during labor with maternal fever, leukocytosis, uterine tenderness, contractions, and fetal tachycardia.
symptoms_in_common: Lower abdominal pain and uterine contractions
Preterm labor with cervical dilation and complete effacement
symptoms_not_in_common: Intact membranes, although chorioamnionitis can still occur with intact membranes
Persistent non-healing cesarean wound after delivery
Violaceous ulcerative wound borders
Failure of wound healing despite antibiotics

data.diagnosis: Sweet syndrome (acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis), including postoperative pathergy
data.description: A neutrophilic inflammatory disorder characterized by fever, neutrophilia, elevated inflammatory markers, and painful erythematous plaques or pseudovesicular lesions; trauma or surgery may trigger lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Postoperative inflammatory skin/wound complication that may not respond to antibiotics
symptoms_not_in_common: Large deep ulceration of the cesarean incision is less typical than for pyoderma gangrenosum
No described tender erythematous plaques, papules, or nodules at other skin sites
Preterm labor, oligohydramnios, and fetal growth restriction are not typical manifestations
The wound's undermined violaceous ulcer margins are more characteristic of pyoderma gangrenosum

data.description: An 87-year-old man presented with a one-year history of difficulty swallowing, with episodes of choking and aspiration that progressively increased in frequency. Laryngeal examination revealed extraluminal obstruction from behind. The patient had multiple comorbidities as mentioned in the case.

data.diagnosis: Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH) with large anterior cervical osteophytes
data.description: A disorder characterized by flowing calcification and ossification along spinal ligaments, often producing large anterior cervical osteophytes that can mechanically compress the pharynx or esophagus.
symptoms_in_common: Extraluminal obstruction from behind on laryngeal examination
Imaging appearance of prominent anterior cervical bony/ossified changes
symptoms_not_in_common: No symptoms clearly atypical for this diagnosis are described

data.diagnosis: Cervical spondylosis with anterior cervical osteophyte-related dysphagia
data.description: Degenerative disease of the cervical spine that can form anterior osteophytes; when large, these bony spurs may compress the hypopharynx or cervical esophagus and cause dysphagia and aspiration.
symptoms_in_common: Posterior extraluminal compression of the laryngeal/pharyngeal region
Degenerative-appearing cervical spine changes on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Neck pain or reduced neck mobility is not reported
Neurologic symptoms of cervical myelopathy or radiculopathy are not reported

data.description: A benign or malignant mass arising in the retropharyngeal space, hypopharynx, thyroid region, cervical esophagus, or adjacent tissues can externally compress the swallowing passage and lead to progressive dysphagia and aspiration.
symptoms_in_common: Extraluminal obstruction seen from behind during laryngeal examination
symptoms_not_in_common: No neck mass is described
No weight loss is reported
No throat pain or odynophagia is reported
No hoarseness is reported
Imaging appears more suggestive of bony cervical-spine prominence than a soft-tissue mass

data.description: A pharyngoesophageal pouch that can retain food and secretions, producing dysphagia, regurgitation, coughing, choking, and aspiration, particularly in older adults.
symptoms_not_in_common: Regurgitation of undigested food is not reported
Halitosis is not reported
Gurgling in the neck is not reported
The laryngeal examination suggests external posterior compression rather than an intraluminal pharyngoesophageal pouch
Imaging suggests cervical bony abnormalities rather than a contrast-filled diverticulum

data.description: A 22-year-old African American/Asian college-age woman presented with a 3-month history of mild exertional dyspnea that progressively worsened despite treatment with inhalers for suspected reactive airway disease. She reported shortness of breath with mild exertion, nonproductive cough for several weeks, and a 5-lb weight loss. She denied fever, chills, headaches, syncope, dizziness, bone pain, nausea, or vomiting. Physical examination was unremarkable except for decreased breath sounds and slight dullness to percussion on the left. Routine laboratory work-up was unremarkable. Initially, chest x-ray showed mediastinal widening, which led to further imaging and biopsy. An open mediastinal biopsy was performed after CT-guided biopsy failed, revealing a poorly differentiated carcinoma initially thought to be thymic carcinoma. Flow cytometry from tissue showed T cells and polyclonal B cells with no immunophenotypic evidence of malignancy.

data.diagnosis: NUT carcinoma (NUT midline carcinoma) of the mediastinum
data.description: A rare, highly aggressive poorly differentiated carcinoma driven by NUTM1 gene rearrangement, often arising in the midline thorax/mediastinum of children and young adults and frequently initially misdiagnosed as thymic carcinoma.
symptoms_in_common: Poorly differentiated carcinoma on mediastinal biopsy
Initial pathologic impression of thymic carcinoma
No evidence of lymphoma by flow cytometry
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or chills
No chest pain reported
Mild symptoms despite a large mediastinal process

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor arising from the thymus, typically presenting as an anterior mediastinal mass and capable of causing respiratory symptoms through compression of adjacent lung or airways.
symptoms_in_common: Decreased left-sided breath sounds and dullness to percussion, possibly from pleural involvement or effusion
symptoms_not_in_common: Very young age; thymic carcinoma is more common in middle-aged adults
No chest pain
No superior vena cava syndrome symptoms such as facial swelling or prominent neck veins
No constitutional fever

data.description: An aggressive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma that commonly affects young women and presents with a bulky anterior mediastinal mass causing cough, dyspnea, pleural effusion, or compression of mediastinal structures.
symptoms_in_common: Decreased breath sounds and dullness to percussion on the left, compatible with pleural effusion or mass effect
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy was interpreted as poorly differentiated carcinoma rather than lymphoma
Flow cytometry showed polyclonal B cells and no immunophenotypic evidence of B-cell malignancy
No fever, night sweats, or other prominent B symptoms reported
No superior vena cava syndrome symptoms reported

data.diagnosis: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma, nodular sclerosis subtype
data.description: A lymphoma frequently affecting adolescents and young adults, especially women, that commonly causes mediastinal lymph-node enlargement and respiratory symptoms from a bulky mediastinal mass.
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy described a poorly differentiated carcinoma rather than Hodgkin lymphoma
No fever, drenching night sweats, or pruritus
Flow cytometry did not demonstrate a malignant lymphoid population
No peripheral lymphadenopathy described

data.description: A germ cell neoplasm arising in the mediastinum, usually presenting as a large anterior mediastinal mass with cough, dyspnea, chest discomfort, or pleural effusion. Teratoma, seminoma, and nonseminomatous tumors are major subtypes.
symptoms_in_common: Possible left pleural fluid or mass effect suggested by decreased breath sounds and dullness
symptoms_not_in_common: Mediastinal germ cell tumors are less common in women than men
Biopsy was interpreted as poorly differentiated carcinoma rather than a germ cell tumor
No tumor-marker information such as alpha-fetoprotein or beta-hCG elevation
No chest pain reported

data.description: 71-year-old woman with hematuria. Past history notable for nephrolithiasis at age 41, long-standing easy skin bruising that worsened at age 66, and osteoporosis (left femoral neck T-score -2.6). Physical examination showed bruising on the lower extremities. Serial evaluation at a tertiary center showed elevated late-night serum cortisol (70 ng/mL) and a Dex-CRH test with cortisol 1.8 µg/dL at 0 minutes and 2 µg/dL at 15 minutes.

A cause of ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome in which both adrenal glands become enlarged and nodular, producing excess cortisol. It often presents later in adulthood with subtle or gradual hypercortisolism.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated late-night serum cortisol indicating loss of normal cortisol circadian rhythm
Abnormal dexamethasone-CRH testing consistent with endogenous hypercortisolism
History of nephrolithiasis, which can occur with cortisol-related hypercalciuria
Bilateral adrenal abnormalities/enlargement suggested by the CT image
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria is not a typical direct manifestation of PBMAH
No reported hypertension, diabetes, central obesity, proximal muscle weakness, or hirsutism

data.diagnosis: Cushing syndrome due to adrenal cortisol excess
data.description: Cushing syndrome is chronic exposure to excessive cortisol. When due to an adrenal source, cortisol production is relatively autonomous and ACTH is usually suppressed; causes include adrenal adenoma, bilateral adrenal hyperplasia, or rarely adrenal carcinoma.
