symptoms_in_common: Failure of appropriate cortisol suppression on dexamethasone-CRH testing
Progressive easy bruising due to cortisol-induced skin thinning
Prior nephrolithiasis, potentially related to hypercalciuria associated with cortisol excess
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria is not a classic feature of Cushing syndrome
No documented truncal obesity, facial rounding, dorsocervical fat pad, purple striae, hypertension, hyperglycemia, or muscle weakness

data.description: A rare ACTH-independent cause of Cushing syndrome caused by multiple small cortisol-producing adrenal nodules. It may occur alone or as part of Carney complex and can produce mild or cyclic hypercortisolism.
symptoms_in_common: Biochemical evidence of endogenous cortisol excess
History of kidney stones potentially related to cortisol-associated calcium loss
symptoms_not_in_common: PPNAD more commonly affects younger patients than this 71-year-old woman
The imaging appearance of enlarged or macronodular adrenal glands would be less typical than for PBMAH
Hematuria is not typical
No reported Carney complex findings such as lentigines, myxomas, or endocrine tumors

data.description: 40-year-old woman with 10 months of progressive lower-extremity edema, starting as episodic pain and swelling in the feet and ankles in the evenings after prolonged standing and progressing to the lower legs and thighs, with abdominal distention and pain. Five months before evaluation, she developed left back and flank pain. Past history includes hypothyroidism, latent tuberculosis, hysterectomy for fibroid uterus, appendectomy, ectopic pregnancy, and two prior vaginal deliveries. On examination, she had 2+ edema of the lower and upper legs, jugular venous pressure of 8 cm H2O, and a distended, mildly tender abdomen with healed surgical scars.

data.diagnosis: Chronic inferior vena cava thrombosis (inferior vena cava syndrome)
data.description: Obstruction of the inferior vena cava by thrombus causes impaired venous return from the legs and pelvis, often producing bilateral leg edema, abdominal wall collateral veins, and flank or abdominal pain.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive bilateral lower-extremity edema extending from the ankles to the thighs
Painful swelling of the feet and ankles
Abdominal distention and mild abdominal pain
Imaging appearance consistent with obstruction of the inferior vena cava and extensive collateral venous channels
symptoms_not_in_common: Upper-leg edema is common, but isolated or predominant upper-leg involvement would be less typical than diffuse bilateral leg edema
Jugular venous pressure of 8 cm H2O is not a defining feature

data.diagnosis: Congenital absence or atresia of the inferior vena cava
data.description: A developmental abnormality in which part or all of the inferior vena cava is absent or severely narrowed. Venous blood is redirected through collateral abdominal, pelvic, paravertebral, and superficial veins; symptoms may develop in adulthood due to venous insufficiency or thrombosis.
symptoms_in_common: Lower-extremity pain and swelling after prolonged standing
Imaging findings suggestive of absent or chronically occluded inferior vena cava with collateral drainage
symptoms_not_in_common: Abdominal distention is not always present
Mild abdominal tenderness is not a classic primary feature
Symptoms first appearing at age 40 are less typical than presentation in younger patients, although delayed presentation can occur

data.diagnosis: Retroperitoneal fibrosis causing inferior vena cava and iliac venous obstruction
data.description: Retroperitoneal fibrosis is inflammatory fibrous tissue in the retroperitoneum that can encase the aorta, inferior vena cava, iliac vessels, and ureters, leading to venous obstruction, leg edema, and abdominal or flank pain.
symptoms_in_common: Possible venous obstruction with collateral circulation on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported urinary obstruction, hydronephrosis, or reduced urine output
No constitutional inflammatory symptoms such as fever, weight loss, or malaise
The initial episodic foot and ankle swelling after standing is more suggestive of venous insufficiency than classic retroperitoneal fibrosis

data.description: Thrombosis involving the iliac veins and/or inferior vena cava causes severe obstruction of venous drainage from both lower limbs and may produce pelvic, abdominal, and flank collateral veins.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging findings compatible with iliocaval obstruction and collateral venous pathways
symptoms_not_in_common: A 10-month slowly progressive course is less typical of an acute deep venous thrombosis, though it can occur with chronic thrombosis
No reported acute unilateral leg swelling, erythema, or warmth
Abdominal distention is not typical unless venous obstruction is extensive

data.diagnosis: Chronic venous insufficiency due to central venous outflow obstruction
data.description: Chronic impairment of venous return causes dependent leg edema, aching, and swelling that worsens after prolonged standing. In this case, central obstruction of the iliac veins or inferior vena cava would explain the severity and bilateral extent.
symptoms_in_common: Foot and ankle swelling worse in the evening after prolonged standing
Progression of edema from the ankles to the legs and thighs
symptoms_not_in_common: Abdominal distention and abdominal pain are not typical of uncomplicated peripheral venous insufficiency
Flank and back pain are not typical
Extensive abdominal or pelvic collateral venous findings on imaging suggest a central venous obstruction rather than isolated superficial venous insufficiency

diagnoses.name: Membranous nephropathy
diagnoses.title: Glomerular disease associated with thin basement membrane nephropathy

data.description: A 22 year old man presented to the emergency department with abdominal pain, jaundice, itching, and fever. His urine was dark and stools pale. Physical examination revealed temperature of 38.7°C, icterus, abdominal tenderness worst in the right upper quadrant with negative Murphy's sign, impalpable gall bladder, inflamed oropharynx with cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy. Laboratory tests showed liver function abnormalities with alkaline phosphatase 327, aspartate aminotransferase 358, and bilirubin 109 suggesting cholestasis. White cell count was elevated at 20.8, C reactive protein was raised at 17, and platelets were low at 168. Monospot test was positive for Epstein Barr virus, confirmed by positive Epstein Barr virus serology. Hepatitis A, B, and C serology were negative.

Acute inflammation of the gallbladder without gallstones, occurring as an uncommon complication of primary Epstein-Barr virus infection. Imaging may show gallbladder wall thickening, edema, and pericholecystic fluid without calculi.
symptoms_in_common: Right upper quadrant abdominal pain and tenderness
Elevated bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, and AST
Ultrasound/MRI findings compatible with gallbladder wall edema/inflammation without gallstones
Positive Monospot test and Epstein-Barr virus serology
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative Murphy's sign
Impalpable gallbladder
Inflamed oropharynx with cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy, which reflect the associated EBV infection rather than cholecystitis itself

data.diagnosis: Acute infectious mononucleosis with cholestatic hepatitis due to Epstein-Barr virus
data.description: Primary Epstein-Barr virus infection commonly causes fever, pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy, and mild hepatitis. In rare cases, it causes marked cholestasis with jaundice, pruritus, dark urine, and pale stools.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated AST and cholestatic liver tests
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent right upper quadrant tenderness
Gallbladder wall edema/inflammatory imaging findings
Marked leukocytosis and elevated inflammatory markers, which may suggest an associated gallbladder inflammatory process

data.description: Bacterial infection of the biliary tree, usually caused by obstruction such as a common bile duct stone. It classically presents with fever, jaundice, and right upper quadrant pain, often with cholestatic liver abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Right upper quadrant abdominal pain and tenderness
symptoms_not_in_common: Positive Epstein-Barr virus serology and Monospot test
Pharyngitis with cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy
No reported bile duct stone or definite biliary duct dilatation on imaging
Gallbladder inflammation without stones is more suggestive of acalculous cholecystitis

data.description: 41-year-old man with sudden, severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the right groin and flank, with nausea and one episode of nonbloody, nonbilious vomiting. Two weeks earlier, he had a similar but milder left lower quadrant pain radiating to the left flank that resolved spontaneously. He also reported several months of fatigue, without fever, weight loss, chest pain, diarrhea, or urinary symptoms. Exam showed diffuse abdominal tenderness without guarding or rebound and bilateral costovertebral angle tenderness, worse on the right. Vitals: T 37.4°C, pulse 78 bpm, BP 188/116 mmHg, RR 18/min, O2 sat 96% on room air. Labs showed leukocytosis with neutrophilia, mild anemia, creatinine 1.5 mg/dL, elevated LDH, elevated ESR and CRP, and bland urinalysis with 1+ protein. He had no known medical conditions or medications, smoked one pack per day for 26 years, and drank alcohol socially.

data.diagnosis: Polyarteritis nodosa (PAN) with renal artery involvement and bilateral renal infarction
data.description: A necrotizing medium-vessel vasculitis that causes segmental arterial stenoses, microaneurysms, thrombosis, and organ ischemia. Renal involvement commonly causes severe hypertension, renal infarcts, impaired kidney function, and elevated inflammatory markers. The imaging appearance of multifocal renal arterial abnormalities with bilateral wedge-shaped renal infarcts is highly suggestive.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden severe flank and lower abdominal pain
Prior transient contralateral flank and abdominal pain
Elevated LDH consistent with tissue infarction
Mild proteinuria with otherwise bland urinalysis
Renal arterial aneurysmal or stenotic abnormalities on angiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Nausea and a single episode of vomiting are nonspecific and are more likely due to acute renal infarction pain than to PAN itself
No fever
No weight loss
No skin lesions such as livedo reticularis or purpura
No peripheral neuropathy or muscle pain
No gastrointestinal bleeding or diarrhea

data.diagnosis: Renal artery fibromuscular dysplasia with renal infarction
data.description: Fibromuscular dysplasia is a nonatherosclerotic, noninflammatory arterial disorder that can produce alternating renal artery stenoses and aneurysmal dilatations, often described as a 'string-of-beads' appearance. It can cause renovascular hypertension, renal artery dissection, thrombosis, or renal infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Flank and abdominal pain due to possible renal ischemia or infarction
Renal arterial multifocal stenotic or aneurysmal imaging abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated ESR and CRP are not typical because fibromuscular dysplasia is not an inflammatory vasculitis
Leukocytosis with neutrophilia is not typical
Months of fatigue are not a classic feature
Elevated LDH suggests acute infarction but is not intrinsic to fibromuscular dysplasia
The patient is male, whereas renal fibromuscular dysplasia is much more common in women

data.diagnosis: Acute renal infarction due to renal arterial thromboembolism or in-situ thrombosis
data.description: Renal infarction results from abrupt interruption of renal arterial blood flow, commonly from cardiac emboli, renal artery thrombosis, arterial dissection, or hypercoagulable states. It produces acute flank or abdominal pain, elevated LDH, hypertension, and kidney dysfunction, often with a relatively bland urinalysis.
symptoms_in_common: Abrupt severe right-sided flank and lower abdominal pain
Wedge-shaped bilateral renal perfusion defects consistent with renal infarcts
Previous transient left-sided pain that could represent an earlier renal ischemic event
symptoms_not_in_common: Several months of fatigue are not specific for an isolated acute embolic renal infarction
Elevated ESR and CRP may occur with infarction but substantial inflammatory-marker elevation raises concern for vasculitis
Multifocal renal arterial microaneurysms or beading would be atypical for a simple embolic event
No known atrial fibrillation, valvular disease, recent myocardial infarction, or other identified embolic source

data.description: Segmental arterial mediolysis is a rare noninflammatory arteriopathy involving medium-sized visceral arteries. It can cause arterial dissections, aneurysms, stenoses, thrombosis, and renal or abdominal organ infarction. Its angiographic appearance can resemble polyarteritis nodosa.
symptoms_in_common: Acute severe abdominal and flank pain
Possible recurrent episodes of pain from sequential vascular events
Renal arterial aneurysmal, stenotic, or dissecting abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated ESR and CRP are less typical because SAM is generally noninflammatory
Months of fatigue are less typical
Leukocytosis may occur with tissue injury but is not a defining feature
Bilateral renal involvement is possible but less characteristic than vasculitic renal artery disease
The combination of constitutional symptoms and inflammatory markers favors polyarteritis nodosa over SAM

data.description: 80-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus, peripheral arterial disease, hypertension, coronary arteriosclerosis, congestive heart failure, hyperlipidemia, and gout, admitted for anorexia, weight loss, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. He had a remote history of emigration from Southeast Asia 22 years earlier. On examination, he was thin and chronically ill-appearing, with mild abdominal tenderness, posterior lower lung crackles, and leg edema; vital signs showed tachycardia with otherwise stable temperature, blood pressure, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation.

data.diagnosis: Disseminated tuberculosis with intestinal tuberculosis and tuberculous aortitis
data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection involving multiple sites, potentially including the ileocecal bowel, lungs, lymph nodes, and aorta. Tuberculous aortitis can cause a mycotic aortic aneurysm or pseudoaneurysm.
symptoms_in_common: Remote residence in Southeast Asia, a region with higher tuberculosis prevalence
Pulmonary crackles and a pulmonary lesion on imaging
Ileocecal or right-colonic ulcerative lesion on imaging/endoscopy
Abdominal aortic aneurysmal or inflammatory vascular abnormality on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported fever
No reported night sweats
No reported cough, hemoptysis, or other prominent respiratory tuberculosis symptoms

data.description: Tuberculosis affecting the gastrointestinal tract, most commonly the ileocecal region, producing ulceration, bowel-wall thickening, abdominal pain, diarrhea, anorexia, and weight loss.
symptoms_in_common: Ileocecal or right lower abdominal lesion with ulceration on imaging/endoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Posterior lower lung crackles are not a primary intestinal tuberculosis manifestation
Aortic aneurysm is not typical of isolated intestinal tuberculosis
Leg edema is not typical of intestinal tuberculosis

data.diagnosis: Mycotic abdominal aortic aneurysm due to Salmonella infection
data.description: An infected aortic aneurysm caused by bacteremia, frequently due to nontyphoidal Salmonella in older adults with diabetes and severe atherosclerotic vascular disease. It may cause abdominal pain and constitutional symptoms and can enlarge rapidly.
symptoms_in_common: Peripheral arterial disease and extensive atherosclerosis
Abdominal aortic aneurysmal abnormality on CT imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Diarrhea is not a typical dominant symptom unless there is concurrent enteritis
Pulmonary lesion or crackles are not typical
Ileocecal ulcerative lesion is not typical
No reported fever, chills, or bacteremia

data.diagnosis: Ileocecal adenocarcinoma with possible metastatic disease
data.description: Colorectal adenocarcinoma involving the cecum or terminal ileum can cause progressive weight loss, anorexia, abdominal discomfort, altered bowel habits, and an ulcerated mass lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Right lower abdominal or ileocecal lesion with ulceration on imaging/endoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Remote Southeast Asian exposure history does not specifically support colorectal cancer
Pulmonary crackles and a small lung lesion are nonspecific and not necessarily metastatic
Aortic aneurysm is unrelated to typical colorectal cancer presentation
No reported gastrointestinal bleeding or iron-deficiency anemia

data.description: A 62-year-old man with chronic hepatitis C virus infection and alcohol-induced cirrhosis presented with 10 days of epigastric pain and vomiting. Laboratory findings revealed an elevated serum lipase level of 6715 U per liter (reference range 0 to 160). On hospital day five, the patient developed nodules measuring 1 cm by 1 cm that became increasingly tender over the following days.

data.diagnosis: Pancreatic panniculitis secondary to acute pancreatitis
data.description: A rare form of lobular panniculitis caused by release of pancreatic enzymes into the circulation during pancreatic disease, producing enzymatic fat necrosis. Histology characteristically shows necrotic adipocytes ('ghost cells') with inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging findings consistent with acute pancreatic inflammation
New tender subcutaneous nodules on the thighs
Skin nodules developing several days after onset of pancreatitis
Biopsy appearance of lobular fat necrosis compatible with pancreatic enzyme-mediated panniculitis
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic hepatitis C infection
Alcohol-induced cirrhosis

data.description: Acute inflammation of the pancreas, commonly associated with alcohol use, gallstones, medications, hypertriglyceridemia, or other pancreatic injury. Severe disease can cause pancreatic necrosis and systemic complications, including pancreatic panniculitis.
symptoms_in_common: Ten days of epigastric abdominal pain
Abdominal CT findings consistent with pancreatic inflammation and possible necrotic change
symptoms_not_in_common: Tender 1-cm subcutaneous nodules on the thighs are not a usual direct feature of uncomplicated acute pancreatitis
Chronic hepatitis C infection is not a typical symptom of acute pancreatitis

data.description: An inflammatory septal panniculitis that produces tender erythematous subcutaneous nodules, most often on the anterior lower legs. It may occur with infections, inflammatory bowel disease, sarcoidosis, medications, or systemic inflammatory conditions.
symptoms_in_common: Acute onset of painful skin lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe epigastric pain
Vomiting
Markedly elevated serum lipase level
CT evidence of pancreatic inflammation
Histology showing enzymatic fat necrosis with ghost adipocytes rather than typical septal panniculitis
Timing of nodules during acute pancreatitis strongly favors pancreatic panniculitis

data.description: A 50-year-old man presented with a 3-week history of back pain and a skull mass that had been growing slowly for 7 months. Physical examination revealed a smooth, firm, and non-tender mass on his skull that gave him the appearance of having a high domed forehead. Laboratory investigations showed renal impairment, hypercalcaemia, anaemia, and immunoparesis. Lambda light chains were detected in both urine and serum. Bone marrow aspirate showed a low level infiltration of plasma cells, though the patient could not tolerate a bone marrow biopsy. A biopsy of the thoracic lesion revealed a monomorphic population of plasma cells that were strongly positive for CD138 and lambda light chain restricted.

data.diagnosis: Multiple myeloma with extramedullary plasmacytoma involving the skull
data.description: A malignant clonal plasma-cell disorder causing monoclonal light-chain production, marrow involvement, osteolytic bone disease, and end-organ damage. The skull mass represents a plasmacytoma, an aggregate of neoplastic plasma cells.
symptoms_in_common: Thoracic bone lesion containing monomorphic CD138-positive, lambda-restricted plasma cells
Lambda light chains detected in serum and urine
Plasma-cell infiltration on bone marrow aspirate
Imaging appearance consistent with extensive calvarial involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Low-level plasma-cell infiltration on marrow aspirate is less typical than substantial marrow involvement, although sampling variability and patchy disease can occur

data.description: A variant of multiple myeloma characterized by multiple bone or soft-tissue plasmacytomas with relatively limited bone marrow plasma-cell infiltration, but often with myeloma-defining organ damage or monoclonal protein production.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple apparent skeletal lesions including skull and thoracic involvement
Low-level plasma-cell infiltration on marrow aspirate
Lambda light-chain restriction in lesion tissue
Serum and urine lambda light chains
symptoms_not_in_common: Macro-focal myeloma is relatively uncommon
The full degree of diffuse skull expansion may be more extensive than in many cases

data.description: A localized clonal plasma-cell tumor arising in bone, commonly involving the axial skeleton, with little or no marrow involvement and without systemic myeloma-related organ damage.
symptoms_in_common: Skull mass compatible with a plasmacytoma
Thoracic lesion composed of CD138-positive, lambda-restricted plasma cells
Low-level marrow plasma-cell infiltration can occasionally be present
symptoms_not_in_common: Renal impairment
Hypercalcaemia
Anaemia
Immunoparesis
Lambda light chains in both serum and urine
More than one suspected skeletal site
Systemic features strongly favor multiple myeloma rather than solitary plasmacytoma

data.diagnosis: Primary systemic AL amyloidosis associated with a plasma-cell dyscrasia
data.description: A disorder in which monoclonal immunoglobulin light chains form amyloid deposits in organs, often occurring with an underlying plasma-cell clone and causing renal, cardiac, neurologic, or gastrointestinal dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: Lambda light chains in serum and urine
Evidence of a clonal plasma-cell population
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypercalcaemia
Anaemia due to marrow/bone disease
Large skull mass
Thoracic plasmacytoma
Back pain from skeletal lesions
CD138-positive mass of monomorphic plasma cells is more characteristic of plasmacytoma/myeloma
No described nephrotic syndrome, cardiomyopathy, neuropathy, macroglossia, or purpura

data.diagnosis: Metastatic carcinoma to the skull and spine
data.description: Cancer spread from a solid-organ primary tumor to bone can cause skull masses, spinal pain, anaemia, hypercalcaemia, and renal dysfunction, particularly when there is widespread skeletal involvement.
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy demonstrated monomorphic plasma cells rather than carcinoma cells
Strong CD138 expression with lambda light-chain restriction
Lambda light chains in serum and urine
Immunoparesis
Bone marrow plasma-cell infiltration
No known primary solid tumor is described

data.description: A 13-year-old male presented with pain in the right hypochondrium and loss of appetite for 1 month. There was no history of fever. The patient has a history of a successfully treated abdominal tuberculosis, for which he had taken anti-tubercular treatment for 1 year.

Localized hepatic infection by Mycobacterium tuberculosis that can form a solitary or conglomerate mass-like tuberculoma, sometimes with satellite nodules or calcification. It may occur as recurrent or residual disease after prior abdominal tuberculosis.
symptoms_in_common: History of previously treated abdominal tuberculosis
Mass-like hepatic lesion with additional small hepatic lesions/calcific foci on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
Only 1 month of symptoms

data.description: A benign-to-intermediate inflammatory spindle-cell lesion of the liver that can appear as a solitary hepatic mass and may be associated with prior infection or inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Solitary mass-like lesion in the liver
symptoms_not_in_common: History of abdominal tuberculosis is not a typical direct cause
No fever or inflammatory systemic symptoms
Possible multiple small hepatic lesions/calcific foci are less typical

data.description: A rare primary liver cancer that typically affects adolescents and young adults without cirrhosis. Imaging may show a large heterogeneous hepatic mass with a central scar and calcification.
symptoms_in_common: Large hepatic mass with scar-like central low attenuation/calcific appearance on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Previous abdominal tuberculosis is unrelated
Multiple small hepatic nodules may suggest an infectious process rather than a solitary fibrolamellar tumor
No reported weight loss, jaundice, or palpable abdominal mass

data.diagnosis: Hepatic abscess, including tuberculous or pyogenic abscess
data.description: A localized collection of infection in the liver that can cause upper abdominal pain and anorexia. Tuberculous abscesses may be relatively indolent and can lack high fever.
symptoms_in_common: Prior tuberculosis increases the possibility of a tuberculous abscess
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No reported leukocytosis or acute systemic illness
The lesion appears predominantly solid/mass-like rather than a classic fluid-filled abscess

data.description: A man in his 70s with a history of coronary artery disease, hypertension, and mild aortic stenosis presented with altered mental status, acute kidney injury requiring dialysis, and painful, dusky skin discoloration on his distal extremities. Three weeks prior to presentation, he had undergone coronary angiography and coronary artery bypass graft surgery after myocardial infarction. Laboratory examination revealed a white blood cell count of 9100/μL with 22% eosinophils, blood urea nitrogen level of 70 mg/dL (25 mmol/L), and creatinine level of 6.1 mg/dL (539.2 μmol/L). Urinalysis showed 1+ blood and 2+ protein.

data.diagnosis: Cholesterol crystal embolization syndrome (atheroembolic renal disease)
data.description: Systemic embolization of cholesterol crystals from disrupted atherosclerotic plaques, often occurring days to weeks after angiography, vascular surgery, or anticoagulation. It commonly causes renal failure, eosinophilia, livedo reticularis, and painful blue or dusky toes.
symptoms_in_common: Onset approximately 3 weeks after coronary angiography and coronary artery bypass surgery
Painful dusky/blue discoloration of distal toes and extremities
Skin lesions consistent with livedo reticularis or digital ischemia
Altered mental status, which can occur with systemic or cerebral embolization/uremia
symptoms_not_in_common: No major symptoms are atypical; the presentation is highly characteristic

data.description: A necrotizing medium-vessel vasculitis that can cause renal ischemia, hypertension, peripheral neuropathy, skin nodules, livedo reticularis, and digital ischemia. It generally does not cause glomerulonephritis.
symptoms_in_common: Painful distal digital ischemia and dusky skin discoloration
Altered mental status may occur with severe hypertension or central nervous system involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Clear temporal association with coronary angiography and bypass surgery
Marked eosinophilia is not typical
Urinalysis with blood and protein is less characteristic because polyarteritis nodosa usually spares glomeruli
Advanced atherosclerotic disease and recent vascular instrumentation more strongly support cholesterol emboli

data.diagnosis: ANCA-associated vasculitis (granulomatosis with polyangiitis or microscopic polyangiitis)
data.description: Small-vessel autoimmune vasculitis that can produce rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, constitutional symptoms, pulmonary disease, neuropathy, and purpuric skin lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Skin lesions that could be interpreted as vasculitic purpura or ischemic lesions
Altered mental status secondary to uremia
symptoms_not_in_common: Painful blue toes after coronary angiography is more typical of cholesterol embolization
Eosinophilia is not typical for granulomatosis with polyangiitis or microscopic polyangiitis
No pulmonary symptoms, sinus disease, hemoptysis, or systemic constitutional symptoms are described
The timing after vascular surgery strongly favors an atheroembolic process

data.description: Acute kidney injury following iodinated contrast exposure, usually caused by renal vasoconstriction and tubular injury. Creatinine typically rises within 24 to 72 hours after contrast administration and improves over days to weeks.
symptoms_in_common: Acute kidney injury after coronary angiography
Elevated blood urea nitrogen and creatinine
Need for dialysis in severe cases
Mild hematuria and proteinuria can occur nonspecifically
symptoms_not_in_common: Renal failure developing or persisting 3 weeks after angiography is less typical
Painful dusky toes and distal skin ischemia are not explained
Marked eosinophilia is not typical
Systemic embolic-appearing skin findings are not typical

data.description: An immune-mediated prothrombotic reaction to heparin exposure, usually occurring 5 to 10 days after exposure, causing thrombocytopenia and arterial or venous thrombosis that may produce limb ischemia.
symptoms_in_common: Recent cardiac surgery, during which heparin exposure is common
Painful distal extremity ischemia and dusky discoloration
Acute kidney injury can occur with renal ischemia or severe systemic thrombosis
Altered mental status can occur with thrombotic complications
symptoms_not_in_common: No thrombocytopenia is reported
Marked eosinophilia is not typical
The combination of blue toes, renal failure, and eosinophilia after angiography is more characteristic of cholesterol embolization
Diffuse livedo-like skin findings are less typical than focal thrombotic ischemia

data.description: A 79-year-old man with a history of hypertension, stroke, and glaucoma was brought to the emergency department after being found unresponsive by a caregiver. He was cold to the touch with vital signs showing blood pressure of 85/55 mm Hg, heart rate of 36/min, respiratory rate of 14/min, and pulse oximetry of 100% on ambient air. Multiple temperature measurements, including core temperature assessment via rectal method, did not yield a detectable temperature. Physical examination revealed clear bilateral chest auscultation. Chest radiographs and computed tomography of the head were negative for any acute pathology.
A dangerous reduction in core body temperature, often causing depressed consciousness, hypotension, marked bradycardia, and characteristic Osborn (J) waves on ECG.
symptoms_in_common: No detectable core temperature by rectal measurement
ECG with prominent J-point/Osborn waves, especially in precordial leads
Normal oxygen saturation despite depressed consciousness
symptoms_not_in_common: Clear bilateral chest examination
Negative chest radiograph
Negative head CT for acute pathology

data.description: Life-threatening decompensated severe hypothyroidism characterized by hypothermia, altered mental status, bradycardia, hypotension, and hypoventilation.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported history of hypothyroidism
No reported myxedema, dry skin, coarse hair, facial puffiness, or delayed reflexes
Respiratory rate is not markedly depressed
Osborn waves are more directly characteristic of severe hypothermia than hypothyroidism itself

data.description: Severe systemic infection can produce shock and altered consciousness; elderly patients may become hypothermic rather than febrile.
symptoms_in_common: Hypothermia can occur in severe sepsis, particularly in elderly patients
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked bradycardia is less typical, as sepsis more commonly causes tachycardia
No fever or infectious symptoms reported
Clear lung examination
Negative chest radiograph
ECG Osborn waves favor hypothermia as the immediate physiologic process rather than sepsis alone

data.description: Acute adrenal insufficiency causing circulatory collapse, weakness, altered mental status, and sometimes hypothermia or hypoglycemia.
symptoms_in_common: Bradycardia may occur in severe metabolic compromise
symptoms_not_in_common: No known adrenal disease or chronic corticosteroid use reported
No reported abdominal pain, vomiting, dehydration, hyperpigmentation, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, or hypoglycemia
Osborn waves are not a typical primary ECG finding of adrenal crisis

data.description: 34-year-old man with a previously unremarkable history presented with a generalized tonic-clonic seizure and transient right-sided weakness, along with recurrent hemoptysis for 1 month. Renal ultrasound was normal. Labs showed hemoglobin 10.5 g/dL, WBC 6.3 × 10³/mm³, normal complement, creatinine 1.04 mg/dL, and urinalysis without proteinuria but with a few old red blood cells. Anti-GBM antibody, ANCA, dsDNA, and anti-smooth muscle antibody were negative. Bronchoscopy cultures, viral serology, echocardiography, and other evaluations for infectious, embolic, and hematologic causes were negative. Immunofluorescence showed linear and granular IgG deposits in lung and renal tissue.

data.diagnosis: Seronegative anti-glomerular basement membrane disease (atypical Goodpasture syndrome)
data.description: An autoimmune pulmonary-renal syndrome caused by antibodies or immune reactivity directed at basement membranes, producing diffuse alveolar hemorrhage and glomerulonephritis. Some patients have negative circulating anti-GBM antibody tests despite tissue evidence of basement-membrane IgG deposition.
symptoms_in_common: CT findings compatible with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage/ground-glass pulmonary infiltrates
Microscopic hematuria with old red blood cells
Linear IgG deposits in lung and renal tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: Generalized tonic-clonic seizure
Transient right-sided weakness
Normal creatinine
Absence of proteinuria
Negative serum anti-GBM antibody

data.diagnosis: Goodpasture syndrome with central nervous system involvement
data.description: Goodpasture syndrome is the clinical combination of anti-GBM-mediated diffuse alveolar hemorrhage and glomerulonephritis. Rarely, neurologic manifestations such as seizures or focal deficits may occur through cerebral vascular or immune-mediated involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary ground-glass infiltrates consistent with alveolar hemorrhage
Linear IgG staining in renal and pulmonary tissue
Seizure and transient focal neurologic deficit can occur in rare CNS involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal renal function
No proteinuria
Normal renal ultrasound
Negative circulating anti-GBM antibody

data.description: A necrotizing small-vessel vasculitis that commonly affects the upper airways, lungs, kidneys, and occasionally the nervous system. It can cause pulmonary hemorrhage and glomerulonephritis.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary infiltrates that may represent alveolar hemorrhage
Possible neurologic manifestations including seizure or focal weakness
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative ANCA
No reported chronic sinus, nasal, ear, or upper-airway disease
Normal creatinine and no proteinuria
Linear and granular IgG deposits are not the typical pauci-immune biopsy pattern
No granulomatous inflammation reported

data.diagnosis: Systemic lupus erythematosus with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (lupus pneumonitis/capillaritis)
data.description: A systemic autoimmune disease that can cause immune-complex glomerulonephritis, pulmonary capillaritis with alveolar hemorrhage, anemia, and neurologic complications including seizures.
symptoms_in_common: Granular IgG immune deposits can occur in lupus nephritis
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative dsDNA antibody
Normal complement levels
Male sex without other reported systemic lupus features
No proteinuria or impaired renal function
Linear IgG deposition is not the classic full-house immune-complex pattern of lupus nephritis

data.diagnosis: IgA vasculitis or IgA nephropathy with pulmonary hemorrhage
data.description: IgA-mediated immune-complex disease usually affecting the kidneys and sometimes small vessels in the skin, gastrointestinal tract, and lungs. Rare severe cases can cause diffuse alveolar hemorrhage.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary infiltrates compatible with alveolar hemorrhage
Normal or near-normal creatinine can occur early in disease
Granular immune deposits may be present in renal tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported purpura, abdominal pain, or arthralgia
No proteinuria
Linear IgG deposition is not typical; IgA-dominant granular deposition would be expected
Seizure and transient hemiparesis are not typical presenting manifestations

data.description: 30-year-old Hispanic male with history of heavy NSAID use. Presented with melena and severe abdominal pain for 3 weeks, with similar but milder symptoms over prior 4-5 months. Initial hemoglobin 7.8 g/dL and mean corpuscular volume 78 fL. Later endorsed having a right swollen testicle (initially missed on previous exams). Physical exam revealed nontender enlarged right testicle. Laboratory markers showed: human chorionic gonadotropin 50 mIU/mL (normal <10), α-fetoprotein 1,990 ng/mL (normal <8), lactate dehydrogenase 534 IU/L (range 25-175).

data.diagnosis: Metastatic nonseminomatous testicular germ cell tumor (mixed germ cell tumor, likely with yolk sac tumor component)
data.description: A malignant testicular germ cell tumor that may contain mixed histologic elements such as yolk sac tumor, embryonal carcinoma, choriocarcinoma, and teratoma. Markedly elevated alpha-fetoprotein strongly supports a nonseminomatous component. These tumors can metastasize to retroperitoneal lymph nodes and, less commonly, the gastrointestinal tract, causing ulceration and bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Melena from gastrointestinal metastatic involvement or ulceration
Microcytosis consistent with chronic blood loss
Retroperitoneal abdominal imaging abnormality compatible with metastatic spread
symptoms_not_in_common: Heavy NSAID use is not caused by the tumor, although it can confound the gastrointestinal presentation

data.diagnosis: Testicular yolk sac tumor with gastrointestinal metastasis
data.description: Yolk sac tumor is a nonseminomatous germ cell tumor characterized by substantial alpha-fetoprotein production. In adults it often occurs as part of a mixed germ cell tumor and can spread through retroperitoneal lymphatics and hematogenously, occasionally involving the gastrointestinal tract.
symptoms_in_common: Iron-deficiency-pattern anemia with low hemoglobin and low mean corpuscular volume
Possible retroperitoneal metastatic disease on CT
Gastrointestinal ulcerative lesions that may represent metastases
symptoms_not_in_common: Beta-human chorionic gonadotropin elevation is less characteristic of a pure yolk sac tumor and suggests a mixed germ cell tumor or syncytiotrophoblastic component
Heavy NSAID use is unrelated to yolk sac tumor biology

data.diagnosis: Testicular embryonal carcinoma as part of a mixed nonseminomatous germ cell tumor
data.description: Embryonal carcinoma is an aggressive nonseminomatous testicular germ cell tumor that commonly occurs in mixed tumors. It can elevate alpha-fetoprotein and beta-human chorionic gonadotropin and has an early tendency toward lymphatic and hematogenous metastasis, including rare gastrointestinal metastases.
symptoms_not_in_common: Heavy NSAID use does not specifically support embryonal carcinoma
The relatively modest beta-human chorionic gonadotropin elevation is not specific for embryonal carcinoma

data.diagnosis: NSAID-associated peptic ulcer disease with upper gastrointestinal bleeding
data.description: Frequent NSAID use can damage gastric and duodenal mucosa, causing erosions or peptic ulcers that produce abdominal pain, melena, and chronic or acute blood-loss anemia.
symptoms_in_common: Endoscopic ulcerative and bleeding-appearing upper gastrointestinal lesions
Low mean corpuscular volume consistent with chronic gastrointestinal blood loss
symptoms_not_in_common: Painless enlarged right testicle
Markedly elevated alpha-fetoprotein
Elevated beta-human chorionic gonadotropin
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase
Retroperitoneal abnormality suggestive of metastatic lymphadenopathy
The combination of testicular mass and tumor-marker elevation is not explained by NSAID-related ulcer disease

data.description: 55-year-old man with a history of heart failure, obesity, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction presented with 3 days of अचानक right foot and calf swelling and pain, which progressed to the upper leg. On the day of presentation, he developed new dusky discoloration of the right toes. Exam showed a cold, dusky right leg and foot with marked asymmetric swelling, 4+ pitting edema of the right upper thigh, and distal pulses detectable only by Doppler. Vitals were temperature 36.1°C, heart rate 80 bpm, blood pressure 96/50 mmHg, and oxygen saturation 95% on room air.
A severe form of massive proximal deep-vein thrombosis causing near-total venous outflow obstruction, profound limb edema, cyanosis, and threatened limb ischemia.
symptoms_in_common: Acute unilateral right foot, calf, and upper-leg swelling
Marked asymmetric 4+ pitting edema of the right thigh
Dusky or cyanotic discoloration of the right toes
Distal pulses detectable only by Doppler
Progression of symptoms over several days
symptoms_not_in_common: No major symptoms are atypical; the presentation is highly characteristic

data.description: A thrombus involving the deep veins of the thigh and pelvis, often producing severe unilateral leg pain and swelling; extensive disease may progress to phlegmasia cerulea dolens.
symptoms_in_common: Unilateral right calf, foot, thigh, and upper-leg swelling
Dusky discoloration from severe venous congestion
symptoms_not_in_common: Cold limb
Marked toe ischemia and nearly absent palpable distal pulses

data.diagnosis: Acute limb ischemia due to arterial occlusion
data.description: Sudden reduction or interruption of arterial blood flow to a limb, commonly caused by embolism or thrombosis, resulting in pain, coolness, cyanosis, and reduced pulses.
symptoms_in_common: Acute right leg and foot pain
Distal pulses detectable only by Doppler
History of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, which increases embolic risk
symptoms_not_in_common: Massive unilateral swelling extending from the foot to the upper thigh
Marked 4+ pitting edema
Symptoms initially dominated by progressive swelling

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the stomach. Advanced gastric adenocarcinoma can create a hypercoagulable state and predispose to extensive venous thromboembolism, including iliofemoral thrombosis and phlegmasia.
symptoms_in_common: Extensive acute venous thrombosis consistent with a malignancy-associated hypercoagulable state
Imaging and endoscopic appearance of a gastric mass
Histologic appearance consistent with invasive adenocarcinoma
symptoms_not_in_common: No abdominal pain reported
No nausea or vomiting reported
No gastrointestinal bleeding reported
No weight loss or anorexia reported
Acute painful swollen cyanotic leg is not a direct local symptom of gastric cancer

diagnoses.name: Poorly differentiated invasive adenocarcinoma of gastric origin
diagnoses.title: Adenocarcinoma of stomach

data.description: 76-year-old man from the Indian subcontinent presented with fever and priapism. Physical exam showed painful, engorged penis with intact skin, no lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly, or splenomegaly. No skin rash or nodules were found.

data.diagnosis: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma (IVLBCL) involving the penis
data.description: A rare aggressive extranodal B-cell lymphoma in which malignant large B cells proliferate predominantly within small blood vessels, often without lymphadenopathy or a detectable mass. Penile vascular involvement can cause ischemic priapism.
symptoms_in_common: FDG-avid penile abnormality on PET imaging
Histology showing atypical cells within vascular spaces
Immunohistochemical appearance consistent with B-cell lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: No neurologic symptoms were reported
No respiratory symptoms were reported
No cytopenias or hemophagocytic syndrome were described

data.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) of the penis
data.description: An aggressive mature B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that can rarely arise in or infiltrate the penis, producing painful swelling, erectile dysfunction, or priapism. Most cases form a mass rather than being confined to vessels.
symptoms_in_common: Penile FDG uptake on PET imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No discrete penile mass was described
No lymphadenopathy was found
The histologic vascular localization is more characteristic of intravascular lymphoma than conventional DLBCL
No skin ulceration or penile skin lesion was present

data.description: A rare lymphoma localized initially to penile tissue, most commonly of diffuse large B-cell type. It may present with penile enlargement, pain, induration, nodules, ulceration, urinary symptoms, or priapism.
symptoms_in_common: Penile metabolic activity on PET imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No penile nodule, plaque, ulcer, or infiltrative mass was reported
Fever is less typical of strictly localized primary penile lymphoma
The apparent intravascular distribution of tumor cells is atypical for most primary penile lymphomas

data.diagnosis: Ischemic priapism secondary to malignant corporal infiltration or venous obstruction
data.description: Low-flow ischemic priapism is a painful prolonged erection caused by impaired venous drainage from the corpora cavernosa. Malignancy, including hematologic cancer, can produce this through infiltration, thrombosis, or vascular obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Potential malignant penile vascular or tissue involvement on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever is not a typical feature of uncomplicated ischemic priapism
No duration of erection, cavernosal blood gas results, or Doppler findings were provided
Systemic lymphoma-type histologic findings would indicate an underlying malignancy rather than isolated priapism

data.description: 50-year-old postmenopausal woman with 1 year of menopause presented with abdominal distention, anorexia, and exertional dyspnea. Examination showed a markedly distended abdomen. Imaging revealed gross ascites and a heterogeneous left adnexal/pelvic mass with enhancing solid components, thick septa, and small calcifications, without lymphadenopathy or peritoneal dissemination. Serum CA 125 was markedly elevated (1237 U/mL); CEA, CA 19-9, and SCC were normal. Repeated ascitic fluid cytology showed benign mesothelial cells without malignant cells. Thyroid function was normal despite strong uptake on thyroid scintigraphy.

A rare monodermal ovarian teratoma composed predominantly of thyroid tissue. It can produce ascites and pleural effusion (pseudo-Meigs syndrome), markedly elevate CA-125, and demonstrate radioiodine uptake despite normal thyroid function.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional dyspnea, consistent with pleural effusion
Solid and cystic heterogeneous ovarian mass with septa and calcifications
symptoms_not_in_common: Anorexia is nonspecific and not a defining feature
One year of menopause is not specifically characteristic

data.description: A malignant ovarian neoplasm, commonly high-grade serous carcinoma, that often presents after menopause with an adnexal mass, ascites, abdominal symptoms, and elevated CA-125.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional dyspnea related to fluid accumulation
Large complex adnexal mass with solid enhancing components and thick septa
symptoms_not_in_common: Repeated benign ascitic-fluid cytology without malignant cells
Absence of peritoneal dissemination
Absence of lymphadenopathy
Small calcifications and thyroid-scintigraphy uptake are not typical diagnostic features
Normal thyroid function does not support or exclude ovarian carcinoma but does not explain the scintigraphic uptake

data.description: A benign sex-cord stromal ovarian tumor that may cause the Meigs triad of ovarian fibroma, ascites, and pleural effusion; CA-125 can be elevated because of peritoneal irritation.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional dyspnea consistent with pleural effusion
No apparent metastatic lymphadenopathy or peritoneal carcinomatosis
symptoms_not_in_common: The mass has heterogeneous solid and cystic components with thick septa rather than the usual predominantly solid fibroma appearance
Calcifications are less typical
Strong thyroid scintigraphy uptake is not expected
CA-125 of 1237 U/mL is possible but relatively unusual for a benign fibroma/thecoma
Anorexia is nonspecific

data.diagnosis: Mature cystic teratoma containing thyroid tissue
data.description: A benign germ-cell tumor that can contain multiple mature tissue types, including thyroid tissue. When thyroid tissue predominates, it is classified as struma ovarii.
symptoms_in_common: Heterogeneous ovarian lesion with mixed internal components
Potential thyroid tissue explaining thyroid-scintigraphy uptake
symptoms_not_in_common: Gross ascites is uncommon in an uncomplicated mature cystic teratoma
Pleural effusion and exertional dyspnea are uncommon
Marked CA-125 elevation is not typical
Thick enhancing septa and substantial solid components are less typical of a routine mature cystic teratoma
Postmenopausal presentation is less common than in younger women

data.description: A 32 year-old male presented to his primary care provider with unremitting neck pain. He denied any history of trauma. The patient was unresponsive to conservative therapy and plain-film radiographic evaluation was negative. Patient was subsequently referred for a cervical spine MR for further evaluation.

data.diagnosis: Cervical spinal epidural abscess / vertebral osteomyelitis
data.description: Infection involving the vertebrae, intervertebral disc spaces, and/or epidural space that can produce inflammatory soft-tissue or epidural collections and spinal canal narrowing. MRI is substantially more sensitive than plain radiographs early in the disease.
symptoms_in_common: Pain not responding to conservative therapy
Initially negative plain-film radiographs can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, chills, systemic illness, neurologic deficit, or infectious risk factor was reported

data.description: Lymphoma may involve the cervical epidural space and vertebral marrow, producing an infiltrative soft-tissue mass with pain and possible spinal cord compression. Early radiographs may be normal.
symptoms_in_common: Lack of response to conservative treatment
Negative plain radiographs despite clinically significant disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No constitutional symptoms such as fever, night sweats, or weight loss were reported
No neurologic deficits were reported

data.description: Mycobacterial infection of the cervical spine can cause slowly progressive neck pain, marrow abnormalities, paraspinal soft-tissue inflammation or abscess, and epidural extension. Radiographs may be unrevealing early.
symptoms_in_common: Plain radiographs may be negative in early disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, weight loss, night sweats, pulmonary symptoms, or tuberculosis exposure was reported
No neurologic deficits were reported

data.diagnosis: Cervical spinal epidural tumor, such as metastatic disease
data.description: Epidural tumor involving vertebral marrow or the spinal canal may cause persistent pain before neurologic compression symptoms occur. MRI can detect marrow and epidural disease not visible on initial radiographs.
symptoms_in_common: Normal or nondiagnostic plain radiographs can occur early
symptoms_not_in_common: The patient is relatively young for most metastatic cancers
No known primary malignancy, weight loss, or neurologic symptoms were reported

data.diagnosis: Cervical spinal epidural venous malformation/epidural hemangioma
data.description: A vascular lesion in the epidural space or vertebra can cause neck pain and may appear as an enhancing epidural or paravertebral soft-tissue lesion on MRI; plain radiographs may be normal.
symptoms_not_in_common: No radicular pain, weakness, sensory loss, gait disturbance, or myelopathic symptoms were reported

data.description: A 13-month-old male infant presented to the Department of Dermatology with a single asymptomatic plaque on the lower back that was first noticed by parents at approximately 4 months of age. During observation, the lesion gradually became larger and firmer, and intermittent sweating on the surface was noticed.

A benign congenital or early-childhood soft-tissue hamartoma composed of fibrous tissue, immature mesenchyme, and fat. It typically presents before age 2 years as a painless, slowly enlarging, firm subcutaneous mass or plaque.
symptoms_in_common: Lesion first noted during early infancy
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent sweating over the lesion is unusual but may occur if adnexal structures are involved

data.description: A rare benign hamartoma involving eccrine sweat glands and vascular structures, often present at birth or arising in childhood. It may appear as a plaque or nodule and can cause focal hyperhidrosis, pain, or increased hair growth.
symptoms_in_common: Localized intermittent sweating on the lesion surface
symptoms_not_in_common: No pain or tenderness
No reported bluish, violaceous, or vascular discoloration
No reported hypertrichosis

data.description: A benign localized overgrowth of eccrine sweat glands that presents as a circumscribed plaque, most often in childhood, with focal excessive sweating as the principal clinical feature.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent focal sweating over the lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive firmness is less typical
Progressive enlargement into a substantial subcutaneous lesion is less typical
Lower-back location is less common than extremity locations

data.description: A benign developmental proliferation of arrector pili smooth muscle, usually recognized at birth or in early childhood as a skin-colored or hyperpigmented plaque, often on the trunk or lumbosacral region. The lesion may become more prominent over time.
symptoms_in_common: Gradual increase in prominence or firmness
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent sweating is not a typical feature
No reported hypertrichosis
No reported pseudo-Darier sign, such as transient piloerection or elevation after rubbing

data.description: A 15-year-old boy presented with recent onset of breathlessness, weight loss, and tiredness for two months and a crusting erythematous scalp rash for six months. The investigations revealed neutrophilia, raised C-reactive protein (CRP), and Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT). The blood urea and electrolytes, thyroid function tests, anti-nuclear antibodies, and clotting studies were normal

A clonal inflammatory disorder involving Langerhans cells that can affect skin, bone, lungs, liver, and other organs. In children, a persistent crusted scalp eruption, lytic bone lesions, and cystic/nodular lung disease are characteristic.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated ALT suggesting possible hepatic involvement
Diffuse bilateral pulmonary nodular and cystic changes on imaging
Possible lytic sternal bone lesion on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal clotting studies, although these may remain normal when liver involvement is mild
Normal urea and electrolytes

data.description: An inherited CFTR-related disorder causing chronic airway infection, bronchiectasis, systemic inflammation, poor weight gain, and occasionally hepatobiliary disease.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral bronchiectatic/cystic-appearing lung abnormalities on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Recent onset at age 15 without a reported history of recurrent childhood chest infections
Crusting erythematous scalp rash
Possible lytic sternal lesion
No reported chronic productive cough, recurrent sinus disease, pancreatic insufficiency, or gastrointestinal symptoms

data.diagnosis: Pulmonary tuberculosis with skeletal and cutaneous involvement
data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection can cause constitutional symptoms and pulmonary infiltrates or cavitation; disseminated disease may involve bone and skin.
symptoms_in_common: Possible bony lesion involving the sternum
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse thin-walled cystic and bronchiectatic lung pattern is less typical than cavitation, consolidation, nodules, or lymphadenopathy
Crusting scalp rash is not a usual presentation
Neutrophilia is less typical than a normal count or lymphocyte-predominant response
No reported fever, night sweats, cough, hemoptysis, or tuberculosis exposure

data.description: A necrotizing small-vessel vasculitis that can affect the upper and lower respiratory tract, kidneys, skin, and other organs; pulmonary nodules may cavitate.
symptoms_not_in_common: Crusting scalp rash is not characteristic
Diffuse cystic bronchiectasis is not the usual lung pattern
Normal renal-related testing and no reported hematuria
No reported chronic sinus disease, nasal crusting, epistaxis, ear symptoms, or hemoptysis
Possible lytic sternal lesion is not typical

data.description: A granulomatous inflammatory disease that most commonly affects the lungs, lymph nodes, skin, eyes, and occasionally liver or bone.
symptoms_in_common: Raised ALT can occur with hepatic involvement
Skin and lung involvement can coexist
symptoms_not_in_common: Crusting erythematous scalp rash is not a classic sarcoid lesion
Cystic bronchiectatic changes are less typical than hilar lymphadenopathy and perilymphatic nodules
Possible lytic sternal lesion is uncommon
Neutrophilia is not a typical defining laboratory finding
Age 15 is less common than young adulthood

diagnoses.name: Pulmonary involvement in Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
diagnoses.title: Adult pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis

diagnoses.name: Skeletal involvement in Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
diagnoses.title: Langerhans cell histiocytosis

data.description: A 40-year-old woman presented with a palpable lump in her left superior breast. Mammography and US and biopsy performed, confirming invasive carcinoma NST Grade 2. MRI performed pre-operatively due to occult on mammography. Subsequent left breast mastectomy and reconstruction with right breast mastopexy.

data.diagnosis: Invasive breast carcinoma of no special type (NST), grade 2
data.description: The most common form of invasive breast cancer, historically termed invasive ductal carcinoma. Malignant epithelial cells invade beyond the breast ducts into surrounding breast tissue.
symptoms_in_common: Palpable lump in the superior left breast
Irregular hypoechoic breast mass on ultrasound
Suspicious enhancing mass on breast MRI
Core biopsy confirming invasive carcinoma NST, grade 2
Mammographically occult lesion in dense breast tissue

data.diagnosis: Locally extensive or multifocal invasive breast carcinoma
data.description: Invasive breast carcinoma may have a larger extent on MRI than is evident on mammography or ultrasound, including additional adjacent foci or non-mass enhancement that can influence selection of mastectomy rather than breast-conserving surgery.
symptoms_in_common: Large approximately 37 mm abnormality on ultrasound
MRI demonstrates conspicuous enhancing disease in the left breast
Mammography did not adequately demonstrate the known cancer
symptoms_not_in_common: No documented breast skin thickening, nipple retraction, nipple discharge, or inflammatory breast changes

data.diagnosis: Regional lymph node metastasis from left breast carcinoma
data.description: Breast cancer can spread to regional lymph nodes, including axillary, intramammary, or internal mammary chain nodes. Suspicious enhancing nodal findings on staging MRI warrant correlation with dedicated nodal imaging or pathology.
symptoms_in_common: MRI shows a suspicious enhancing focus in the regional/internal mammary nodal region
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported palpable axillary lymph nodes
No documented biopsy confirmation of nodal metastatic disease
No reported arm swelling or lymphedema

data.description: A 68-year-old woman with a longstanding history of non-specific inflammatory arthritis presented with a three-month history of flashing lights and blurred vision. She had been taking 400 mg hydroxychloroquine daily for 15 years, along with meloxicam, omeprazole, and amitriptyline. She was of normal body weight. Ophthalmological assessment revealed reduced visual acuity at 6/18 in the right eye and 6/12 in the left eye, with mild depression in color vision on Ishihara plate testing. Early cataracts were present.

A toxic retinopathy caused by long-term hydroxychloroquine exposure, characterized by parafoveal retinal pigment epithelium and photoreceptor damage that can progress to bull's-eye maculopathy and irreversible central visual loss.
symptoms_in_common: Long-term hydroxychloroquine use at 400 mg daily for 15 years
Reduced visual acuity in both eyes
Bilateral parafoveal macular abnormalities on fundus and fluorescein imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Early cataracts, which may contribute to reduced visual acuity but do not explain the characteristic bilateral paracentral field loss
Inflammatory arthritis itself is not a typical symptom of hydroxychloroquine retinal toxicity

data.description: A degenerative disorder of the macula in older adults that causes central visual impairment, often associated with drusen, retinal pigment epithelial change, geographic atrophy, or choroidal neovascularization.
symptoms_not_in_common: Flashing lights are not a typical presenting feature
Bilateral ring-shaped/paracentral visual field defects are less typical than central distortion or central scotoma
Long-term high cumulative hydroxychloroquine exposure strongly suggests an alternative toxic cause
No reported drusen, hemorrhage, exudation, or choroidal neovascularization

data.diagnosis: Retinitis pigmentosa or retinal dystrophy with ring scotoma
data.description: A group of inherited retinal degenerations causing progressive photoreceptor dysfunction, commonly with night blindness, peripheral field constriction, pigmentary retinal changes, and sometimes a ring scotoma.
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of childhood or early-adult onset visual problems
No reported night blindness
No reported progressive peripheral visual-field constriction
No typical bone-spicule pigmentation, attenuated retinal vessels, or waxy optic discs described
Long-term hydroxychloroquine exposure provides a more likely acquired explanation

data.description: An immune-mediated retinal degeneration that may occur alone or in association with systemic autoimmune disease or malignancy, producing photopsias, visual-field loss, dyschromatopsia, and progressive retinal dysfunction.
symptoms_not_in_common: The characteristic long-term hydroxychloroquine exposure favors drug toxicity
No rapid severe progression, night blindness, or marked peripheral field loss reported
No evidence provided of malignancy-associated retinopathy
Fundus and angiographic findings are more suggestive of parafoveal hydroxychloroquine toxicity

data.description: 50-year-old woman with right nasal congestion and right parotid swelling for an unspecified duration, unresponsive to antibiotics and steroids. She had no significant past medical history and was a current smoker (35 pack-years). Exam and nasal endoscopy showed right-predominant adenoid pad swelling; CT revealed a 4.1 cm nasopharyngeal soft tissue mass. Initial biopsy showed atypical lymphoid hyperplasia with scattered large atypical CD30-positive, focally CD15-positive cells. After adenoidectomy, MRI at 3 months showed recurrence; repeat excision demonstrated a nodular infiltrate of small lymphocytes. PET-CT showed isolated FDG uptake in the nasopharynx without lymphadenopathy, and bone marrow biopsy was negative.

data.diagnosis: Primary extranodal classical Hodgkin lymphoma of the nasopharynx, lymphocyte-rich subtype
data.description: A rare localized form of classical Hodgkin lymphoma arising in extranodal tissue of the nasopharynx. The lymphocyte-rich subtype can show a nodular background of small lymphocytes with scattered Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells that express CD30 and often CD15.
symptoms_in_common: Scattered large atypical cells positive for CD30
Focal CD15 positivity in atypical cells
Nodular infiltrate of small lymphocytes on repeat excision
No lymphadenopathy and negative bone marrow, compatible with localized stage I extranodal disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Right parotid swelling is not a classic direct manifestation, although it may be reactive or due to regional involvement
Lack of constitutional B symptoms is possible but less suggestive of more advanced Hodgkin lymphoma

data.description: An indolent Hodgkin lymphoma characterized by nodular aggregates of small B lymphocytes and scattered large lymphocyte-predominant cells. It usually involves lymph nodes and typically has CD20-positive, CD45-positive large cells that are negative for CD15 and CD30.
symptoms_in_common: Nodular infiltrate composed predominantly of small lymphocytes
Localized disease without lymphadenopathy or bone marrow involvement can occur
Slowly persistent or recurrent mass after local excision
symptoms_not_in_common: Large atypical cells are CD30-positive
Large atypical cells show focal CD15 positivity
Primary nasopharyngeal presentation is unusual
The described immunophenotype is more typical of classical Hodgkin lymphoma than nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma

data.diagnosis: Reactive atypical lymphoid hyperplasia of the adenoids/nasopharynx
data.description: A benign reactive proliferation of lymphoid tissue that may occur with infection, chronic inflammation, or immune stimulation and can produce adenoidal enlargement and nasal obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Initial biopsy interpreted as atypical lymphoid hyperplasia
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent 4.1 cm mass despite antibiotics and steroids
Recurrence after adenoidectomy
Scattered large atypical CD30-positive and focally CD15-positive cells
Isolated FDG-avid lesion on PET-CT
Nodular infiltrate suggesting a lymphoproliferative neoplasm rather than simple reactive hyperplasia

data.description: 83-year-old woman with hypertension and biopsy-proven vaginal melanoma diagnosed 4 months earlier, with invasive locoregional disease and a small left upper lung nodule on PET-CT, treated with four cycles of ipilimumab (last dose 3 weeks before admission). After the third dose she developed pruritus, lethargy, and malaise, and after the fourth dose diarrhea. Over the 2 weeks before admission she had progressively worsening substernal chest pain and dyspnea. On admission, ECG showed sinus tachycardia with ST elevations in leads I, V2, and V3; troponin-I was elevated. Echocardiography showed ejection fraction 50% with left ventricular outflow tract obstruction and systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve. Coronary angiography showed only 30% proximal LAD stenosis without thrombus.

Immune-mediated inflammation of the heart muscle caused by ipilimumab, a CTLA-4 immune checkpoint inhibitor. It can present with chest pain, ST-segment elevation, elevated troponin, arrhythmias, and nonobstructive coronary arteries.
symptoms_in_common: Recent ipilimumab treatment, with last dose 3 weeks before admission
ST elevations in leads I, V2, and V3
No obstructive coronary artery disease on angiography
Systemic immune-related symptoms after treatment, including pruritus, lethargy, malaise, and diarrhea
symptoms_not_in_common: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction with systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve is not a classic primary myocarditis finding

data.diagnosis: Takotsubo syndrome (stress cardiomyopathy), potentially triggered by immunotherapy-associated inflammation
data.description: A transient stress-induced cardiomyopathy that mimics acute myocardial infarction, often with chest pain, ST elevation, troponin elevation, and unobstructed coronary arteries. It may be triggered by severe illness, emotional stress, malignancy, or immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy.
symptoms_in_common: Coronary angiography without obstructive coronary disease
Physiologic stress from advanced melanoma and recent immunotherapy
Dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction and systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve can occur in Takotsubo syndrome
symptoms_not_in_common: No described characteristic apical ballooning or typical regional wall-motion pattern
Immune-related diarrhea, pruritus, and malaise more strongly suggest systemic ipilimumab toxicity than isolated Takotsubo syndrome
Ejection fraction of 50% is only mildly reduced

data.description: Inflammation involving both the myocardium and pericardium, causing chest pain, ST-segment changes, and troponin elevation. In this setting, it could be immune-mediated from ipilimumab.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported pleuritic or positional chest pain
No reported pericardial friction rub
No reported pericardial effusion
Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction is not typical

data.diagnosis: Myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA)
data.description: A clinical syndrome of myocardial infarction with elevated cardiac biomarkers and ischemic ECG changes but no obstructive coronary lesion on angiography. Potential mechanisms include coronary vasospasm, microvascular dysfunction, embolism, myocarditis, or stress cardiomyopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Only 30% proximal LAD stenosis and no coronary thrombus on angiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive immune-related symptoms after ipilimumab, including pruritus and diarrhea, suggest an inflammatory drug toxicity rather than a primary ischemic syndrome
Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction with systolic anterior motion is not a usual MINOCA feature
No demonstrated coronary spasm, embolus, plaque rupture, or dissection

data.description: Melanoma can metastasize to the heart, including the myocardium or pericardium, and may cause chest pain, dyspnea, arrhythmias, myocardial injury, or pericardial disease. Cardiac imaging is needed to identify a focal infiltrative mass.
symptoms_in_common: Possible pulmonary metastatic disease indicated by a left upper lung nodule on PET-CT
Elevated troponin may occur with myocardial infiltration
symptoms_not_in_common: Close temporal association with ipilimumab and multiple immune-related adverse symptoms favors treatment-related myocarditis
ST elevations are more typical of acute inflammatory or ischemic myocardial injury than isolated cardiac metastasis
No described intracardiac mass, myocardial mass, or pericardial effusion

data.description: 33-year-old bisexual Brazilian man with a 4-month history of painful bowel movements and bright red rectal bleeding on toilet paper, without blood mixed in stool. He denied abdominal pain and weight loss. He reported a sexual encounter with a man 6 weeks before presentation. Initial exam showed a tender external hemorrhoid with normal vital signs. Follow-up and surgical evaluation revealed bleeding hemorrhoids, large superficial anterior and posterior midline anal fissures with sentinel skin tags, moderate rectal tenderness, small internal hemorrhoids, and flexible sigmoidoscopy showing mild-to-moderate distal rectal mucosal inflammation, edema, and patchy erythema. HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C tests were negative.

data.diagnosis: Syphilitic proctitis (anorectal syphilis due to Treponema pallidum)
data.description: Sexually transmitted rectal infection caused by Treponema pallidum, which can cause painful proctitis, rectal bleeding, fissures, and a plasma cell-rich inflammatory infiltrate. The immunohistochemical image is consistent with spirochetes in the rectal tissue.
symptoms_in_common: Recent sexual encounter with a man
Distal rectal inflammation, edema, and patchy erythema on sigmoidoscopy
Large anal fissures with sentinel skin tags
Histologic rectal inflammation with prominent plasma cell-rich infiltrate
symptoms_not_in_common: External and internal hemorrhoids, which may be concurrent rather than directly caused by syphilis
Absence of other reported systemic secondary-syphilis manifestations such as rash, fever, or lymphadenopathy

data.description: An invasive sexually transmitted infection caused by Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1-L3 that can produce severe proctitis in men who have sex with men, including rectal pain, bleeding, and inflammatory mucosal changes.
symptoms_in_common: Inflammatory distal proctitis on flexible sigmoidoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Large superficial midline anal fissures are less characteristic
Spirochete-positive tissue staining is not expected
No reported mucopurulent rectal discharge
No reported fever, inguinal lymphadenopathy, or systemic symptoms

data.description: Sexually acquired HSV infection of the anorectum that may cause severe anorectal pain, tenesmus, bleeding, ulceration, and proctitis, particularly after receptive anal sexual exposure.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported perianal or rectal vesicles
No typical painful discrete ulcerations described
Spirochete-positive immunohistochemical staining is not consistent with HSV
Histology does not describe viral cytopathic changes such as multinucleation or nuclear inclusions

data.diagnosis: Inflammatory bowel disease, especially Crohn disease with perianal involvement
data.description: Crohn disease can involve the rectum and anus, causing chronic proctitis, rectal bleeding, fissures, skin tags, and perianal pain. Ulcerative proctitis is another inflammatory bowel disease consideration but is less associated with fissures and perianal skin tags.
symptoms_in_common: Distal rectal mucosal inflammation and erythema
symptoms_not_in_common: No abdominal pain
No weight loss
No reported chronic diarrhea or change in bowel habits
No granulomas or chronic architectural distortion described on biopsy
Spirochete-positive staining supports an infectious cause rather than primary inflammatory bowel disease

data.description: Hemorrhoids are dilated anal vascular cushions that commonly cause painless bright red blood on toilet paper, while anal fissures cause sharp pain during defecation and may produce small-volume bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Bright red blood on toilet paper without blood mixed in stool
symptoms_not_in_common: Moderate rectal tenderness
Distal rectal mucosal edema and patchy erythema on sigmoidoscopy
Histologic active inflammatory proctitis
Spirochete-positive immunohistochemical staining

data.description: 65-year-old man with a history of hypertension and prior laminectomy, never-smoker, with family history of prostate cancer in his father, evaluated with normal prostate-specific antigen and digital rectal examination. Urinalysis was largely normal except for trace blood on dipstick; no protein, glucose, ketones, nitrites, or leukocytes.
The presence of blood detected on urine testing without visible blood in the urine or urinary symptoms; dipstick blood should be confirmed with microscopic urinalysis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal urinalysis otherwise, including no protein, nitrites, or leukocytes

data.diagnosis: Urinary tract malignancy (bladder, kidney, or upper tract urothelial cancer)
data.description: Cancers of the urinary tract can present with painless microscopic or gross hematuria, particularly in older adults, although risk is lower in never-smokers.
symptoms_not_in_common: Never-smoker status
No visible hematuria reported
No urinary irritative symptoms
No flank pain
Normal urinalysis without protein, nitrites, or leukocytes

data.description: A malignant growth of the prostate that may be asymptomatic early and is more likely with increasing age and a first-degree family history.
symptoms_in_common: Family history of prostate cancer in his father
Possible microscopic hematuria can rarely occur with advanced urinary tract involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal prostate-specific antigen
Normal digital rectal examination
No lower urinary tract symptoms
No bone pain, weight loss, or systemic symptoms

data.description: Noncancerous enlargement of the prostate that commonly occurs in older men and can occasionally be associated with hematuria from prostatic vascularity.
symptoms_not_in_common: No urinary frequency, urgency, weak stream, hesitancy, nocturia, or incomplete emptying reported
Normal digital rectal examination

data.description: Urinary stones can cause microscopic hematuria, sometimes without symptoms, although they more commonly cause sudden flank pain or renal colic.
symptoms_not_in_common: No flank or abdominal pain
No nausea or vomiting
No dysuria
No urinary urgency or frequency
No reported prior stone history

data.description: 20-year-old male with a neonatal history of bleeding tendency and a family history of easy bruisability in his father. He also had conductive hearing difficulty after childhood meningitis and was evaluated preoperatively for chronic maxillary sinusitis surgery. He had no known coagulation abnormalities after birth. On preoperative workup, blood counts and chemistry were normal, but coagulation screening showed prolonged PT and aPTT with normal bleeding time. Mixing studies suggested factor deficiency. Plasma fibrinogen activity was markedly low by Clauss method, while fibrinogen antigen was normal. Factor levels were otherwise largely normal, with no FGA or FGB mutations detected. His parents had normal coagulation tests and fibrinogen activity, consistent with a de novo mutation.

An inherited disorder in which fibrinogen antigen concentration is normal or near normal but the fibrinogen molecule functions poorly, causing reduced Clauss fibrinogen activity and prolonged clotting times. It may result from a de novo FGG mutation.
symptoms_in_common: Mixing study consistent with a factor deficiency rather than an inhibitor
Markedly low functional fibrinogen by Clauss assay
Otherwise largely normal coagulation factor levels
Possible de novo mutation involving the fibrinogen gamma-chain gene
symptoms_not_in_common: Conductive hearing difficulty after meningitis
Chronic maxillary sinusitis

data.description: A hereditary fibrinogen disorder with both reduced fibrinogen function and, in many cases, reduced fibrinogen quantity. Some variants may have near-normal antigen values despite markedly impaired clot-based fibrinogen activity.
symptoms_in_common: Bleeding tendency beginning in the neonatal period
Easy bruising in a family member
Correction pattern on mixing studies suggesting a deficiency
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal fibrinogen antigen is less typical because hypodysfibrinogenemia often lowers antigen concentration
No persistent recognized coagulation abnormality after birth
Conductive hearing difficulty after childhood meningitis
Chronic maxillary sinusitis

data.description: A severe inherited quantitative fibrinogen deficiency that can cause neonatal bleeding and marked prolongation of clotting studies. It is usually caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in fibrinogen genes and produces very low or absent fibrinogen antigen.
symptoms_in_common: Mixing study compatible with a coagulation-factor deficiency
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal fibrinogen antigen level, which argues strongly against afibrinogenemia
