No FGA or FGB mutations detected
Parents with normal coagulation testing, whereas severe inherited quantitative deficiency is commonly recessive
Normal bleeding time
Conductive hearing difficulty after meningitis
Chronic maxillary sinusitis

data.description: 60-year-old man with 1 year of progressive exertional dyspnea, worse over the prior 4 months, with persistent nonproductive cough. Five days before admission, he developed sore throat, neck and bilateral arm swelling, and orthopnea. Three days before transfer, he was evaluated at another hospital after facial flushing/redness was noted. On exam there was flushed face, swollen neck, and absent breath sounds in the right lung fields. History notable for heavy tobacco use (2 packs/day for 40 years), occasional marijuana use, and alcohol intake of five beers twice weekly. Family history of pancreatic cancer in his mother.

data.diagnosis: Non-small cell lung cancer (poorly differentiated carcinoma, likely squamous cell carcinoma)
data.description: A malignant epithelial lung tumor strongly associated with heavy tobacco exposure. A central right hilar or mediastinal tumor can obstruct the right main bronchus and compress or invade the superior vena cava, producing superior vena cava syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Absent breath sounds over the right lung fields consistent with central airway obstruction or right-lung collapse
Imaging appearance of a central mediastinal/right hilar mass with vascular obstruction
PET-avid thoracic mass and probable distant metastatic disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat is not a classic primary symptom, although it may result from neck venous congestion

data.description: An aggressive, smoking-associated neuroendocrine lung cancer that commonly arises centrally in the hilum or mediastinum. It frequently presents with bulky mediastinal disease, bronchial obstruction, early metastasis, and superior vena cava syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Absent right-sided breath sounds from bronchial obstruction or atelectasis
Findings compatible with superior vena cava obstruction
Possible metastatic lesion on PET imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported paraneoplastic endocrine syndrome such as hyponatremia, Cushing syndrome, or Lambert-Eaton syndrome
The illustrated tumor cytology appears to contain relatively large pleomorphic cells rather than the classic small hyperchromatic cells with nuclear molding

data.diagnosis: Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the lung
data.description: A high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma that occurs predominantly in older heavy smokers. It can form a large central lung or mediastinal mass, cause airway and superior vena cava compression, and metastasize early.
symptoms_in_common: Central thoracic mass causing right lung airway compromise
Facial flushing and upper-body venous congestion
Possible distant metastatic disease on PET imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No specifically reported neuroendocrine paraneoplastic syndrome
Sore throat is not a typical direct manifestation

data.diagnosis: Pulmonary pleomorphic carcinoma (sarcomatoid non-small cell lung carcinoma)
data.description: A rare, poorly differentiated and highly aggressive non-small cell lung cancer composed of pleomorphic large malignant cells, sometimes with spindle-cell or giant-cell features. It is strongly associated with smoking and may present as a bulky invasive thoracic mass.
symptoms_in_common: Right-sided absent breath sounds due to airway obstruction or lung collapse
Facial and upper-extremity swelling from mediastinal vascular compression
symptoms_not_in_common: Pleomorphic carcinoma is more often described as a peripheral lung mass than as a classic central mediastinal mass
Sore throat is not typical

data.diagnosis: Superior vena cava syndrome secondary to an intrathoracic malignancy
data.description: A clinical syndrome caused by obstruction of the superior vena cava, most often from lung cancer or mediastinal tumor compression, invasion, or thrombosis. It produces impaired venous drainage from the head, neck, upper chest, and arms.
symptoms_in_common: Sore throat or throat fullness due to cervical venous congestion
Imaging evidence of mediastinal mass effect and venous obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent cough is not caused directly by superior vena cava obstruction, although it may be caused by the underlying lung tumor
Absent right lung breath sounds are not a direct feature of superior vena cava syndrome
One year of progressive exertional dyspnea suggests an underlying pulmonary malignancy or airway obstruction rather than superior vena cava syndrome alone

diagnoses.name: Poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the lung
diagnoses.title: lung adenocarcinoma

data.description: Male infant born at term to healthy, nonconsanguineous parents, with no known family history of immune deficiency, presented at 20 days of age with profound T-cell lymphopenia detected on newborn screening (no detectable TRECs). Examination showed neonatal teeth, hypotonia, umbilical hernia, and erythematous psoriasiform dermatitis. Imaging demonstrated wormian skull bones, mild pulmonary artery stenosis, and absence of the corpus callosum. No evidence of maternal engraftment was found.

data.diagnosis: BCL11B-related severe combined immunodeficiency with neurodevelopmental abnormalities
data.description: A rare genetic disorder caused by pathogenic BCL11B variants that can impair thymic T-cell development and cause profound T-cell lymphopenia, along with craniofacial, neurologic, skin, and developmental abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Profound T-cell lymphopenia with absent TRECs on newborn screening
Neonatal presentation consistent with severe combined immunodeficiency
Absent corpus callosum or other neurodevelopmental brain abnormality
symptoms_not_in_common: Neonatal teeth
Wormian skull bones
Mild pulmonary artery stenosis
Umbilical hernia

data.diagnosis: PAX1 deficiency (otofaciocervical syndrome type 2 with severe T-cell immunodeficiency)
data.description: An autosomal-recessive disorder caused by PAX1 deficiency, characterized by defective thymic development causing severe T-cell immunodeficiency, often with craniofacial and skeletal abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Profound T-cell lymphopenia with no detectable TRECs
symptoms_not_in_common: Neonatal teeth
Psoriasiform dermatitis
Absence of the corpus callosum
Umbilical hernia
Hypotonia

data.diagnosis: 22q11.2 deletion syndrome with congenital athymia (complete DiGeorge syndrome)
data.description: A chromosomal deletion syndrome that may cause thymic aplasia or hypoplasia, resulting in severe T-cell lymphopenia, together with congenital heart defects, hypocalcemia, and characteristic craniofacial findings.
symptoms_in_common: Severe neonatal T-cell lymphopenia with absent TRECs
Congenital cardiovascular abnormality including pulmonary artery stenosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Neonatal teeth
Wormian skull bones
Erythematous psoriasiform dermatitis
Umbilical hernia
Absence of the corpus callosum is not a classic finding

data.diagnosis: PGM3-congenital disorder of glycosylation with immunodeficiency
data.description: A congenital glycosylation disorder that can cause combined immunodeficiency, eczema or dermatitis, hypotonia, developmental abnormalities, and skeletal or craniofacial findings.
symptoms_not_in_common: Complete absence of TRECs and profound isolated T-cell lymphopenia are less typical
Neonatal teeth
Wormian skull bones
Umbilical hernia
Absence of the corpus callosum

data.description: A disorder of NF-kappa-B signaling that can produce combined immunodeficiency and ectodermal abnormalities involving the skin, teeth, hair, and sweat glands. Severe forms in males may present in infancy.
symptoms_in_common: Severe immune deficiency that may include T-cell dysfunction
Dental abnormality, including abnormal early dentition
symptoms_not_in_common: Profound absent-TREC T-cell lymphopenia is not the usual presentation
Wormian skull bones
Absence of the corpus callosum
Pulmonary artery stenosis
Umbilical hernia
Hypotonia

data.description: 47-year-old male presented with tenesmus and mucoid stool. He had a 20-pack-year smoking history and a remote history of pulmonary tuberculosis treated with 9 months of anti-tuberculosis medication 20 years earlier. On admission, he had no weight loss, fever, or night sweats. Physical examination was largely unremarkable except for a depressed anterior chest wall; no lymphadenopathy was noted, and heart and lung exams were normal. Chest radiograph showed a right upper lung field scar consistent with prior tuberculosis. Further evaluation showed no abdominal lymphadenopathy and no remarkable findings on bone marrow aspiration/biopsy.

data.diagnosis: Primary rectal extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma)
data.description: An indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma arising in mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue. In the rectum it can appear as submucosal nodules, erosions, or polypoid lesions and histology commonly shows dense lymphoid infiltration with lymphoepithelial lesions.
symptoms_in_common: No fever, night sweats, or weight loss, which is compatible with localized indolent lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Remote treated pulmonary tuberculosis is not a typical defining feature
Depressed anterior chest wall is unrelated

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the rectum that may cause altered bowel habits, mucus discharge, rectal urgency, tenesmus, bleeding, or obstructive symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss
No abdominal lymphadenopathy
Endoscopic appearance of multiple lymphoid-appearing lesions rather than a typical ulcerated or annular epithelial mass
Histologic lymphoid infiltration with lymphoepithelial lesions would not be typical of adenocarcinoma

data.diagnosis: Ulcerative proctitis (ulcerative colitis limited to the rectum)
data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease confined to the rectum, typically causing continuous mucosal inflammation, urgency, tenesmus, rectal bleeding, and mucus discharge.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported rectal bleeding
No diarrhea
No systemic inflammatory symptoms
Localized mass-like or nodular lesions are less typical than diffuse continuous erythematous friable mucosa
Dense monoclonal-appearing lymphoid infiltrate with lymphoepithelial lesions would be atypical

data.diagnosis: Intestinal tuberculosis involving the colon or rectum
data.description: Gastrointestinal infection by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, usually affecting the ileocecal region but occasionally involving the colon. It may produce ulceration, strictures, nodules, abdominal pain, fever, weight loss, or bowel obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Chest radiograph scar consistent with prior tuberculosis
Tenesmus can occur with rectal involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No night sweats
No weight loss
No abdominal lymphadenopathy
No reported abdominal pain
Rectal involvement is uncommon compared with ileocecal disease
Lymphoepithelial lesions and B-cell lymphomatous histology would not be typical of tuberculosis

data.description: 24-year-old woman with no significant medical history presented with 2 days of left leg crampy pain radiating to the left lower abdomen and buttock, associated with swelling and exertional dyspnea. She denied fever, chest pain, dyspnea at rest, or trauma. Exam showed tachycardia (102 bpm) and left leg pitting edema, erythema, and increased warmth from thigh to calf. History notable for oral contraceptive use since age 15, prior light smoking, and family history of DVT in her father after surgery. Labs showed mild leukocytosis with otherwise normal blood counts and coagulation studies; troponin and NT-proBNP were normal.

data.diagnosis: Acute left iliofemoral deep venous thrombosis with pulmonary embolism
data.description: Acute clot formation in the deep veins of the left lower extremity/pelvis with embolization to pulmonary arteries. The CT images are consistent with pulmonary arterial filling defects and pelvic venous thrombosis.
symptoms_in_common: Oral contraceptive use, a venous thromboembolism risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain radiating to the left lower abdomen and buttock is less typical of isolated distal leg DVT but can occur with iliac vein involvement
Mild leukocytosis is nonspecific

data.description: Compression of the left common iliac vein by the overlying right common iliac artery, causing impaired venous drainage and predisposing young women to extensive left-sided iliofemoral DVT and pulmonary embolism.
symptoms_in_common: Left-sided pelvic, lower abdominal, and buttock pain
Extensive symptoms involving the thigh through calf
Oral contraceptive use as an additional thrombosis risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: Erythema and increased warmth are more characteristic of acute thrombosis or cellulitis than venous compression alone
Exertional dyspnea is due to pulmonary embolism rather than May-Thurner syndrome itself

data.description: Obstruction of pulmonary arterial branches by embolized venous thrombus, most commonly originating from a lower-extremity or pelvic DVT. The chest CT demonstrates pulmonary arterial filling defects.
symptoms_in_common: Evidence of a likely lower-extremity/pelvic venous clot source
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked unilateral left leg edema
Left leg erythema and warmth
Left leg cramping pain
Lower abdominal and buttock pain
No chest pain
No dyspnea at rest
Normal troponin and NT-proBNP, which may occur in lower-risk pulmonary embolism but do not indicate severe right-heart strain

data.diagnosis: Cellulitis of the left lower extremity
data.description: A bacterial infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissues that typically causes localized erythema, warmth, tenderness, and swelling.
symptoms_in_common: Increased warmth of the left leg
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
Pitting edema involving the leg from thigh to calf is more suggestive of venous obstruction
Exertional dyspnea
Tachycardia may be explained by pulmonary embolism rather than skin infection
Pelvic/lower abdominal and buttock pain
Pulmonary arterial filling defects on CT are not explained by cellulitis

data.description: Inflammation and thrombosis of superficial veins, usually causing a painful, warm, erythematous, cord-like area along the course of a superficial vein.
symptoms_in_common: Oral contraceptive use as a thrombosis risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse pitting edema from thigh to calf is more suggestive of deep venous thrombosis
Lower abdominal and buttock pain suggests proximal pelvic venous involvement
Exertional dyspnea
Pulmonary emboli are much more consistent with deep venous thrombosis than isolated superficial thrombophlebitis
Tachycardia

data.description: 3-year-old boy, born at 41 weeks gestation without perinatal problems, birth weight 3.4kg. Parents were not consanguineous and had no medical history. History of 3 prior hospitalizations for viral pneumonia at 12, 18, and 27 months. Presented with recurrent and persistent pneumonia. Current symptoms included cough, sputum and fever. Physical exam showed: temperature 39.5°C, pulse 129/min, respiration 28/min, BP 95/55 mmHg. Weight 15.3kg (50-75th percentile), height 96.5cm (50-75th percentile). Two 3mm ulcers in uvula, fine crackles in both lung fields, palpable liver 1 finger-breadth below right costal margin, palpable spleen tip.

A primary immunodeficiency caused by defective NADPH oxidase activity in phagocytes, resulting in impaired oxidative burst and susceptibility to recurrent severe bacterial and fungal infections. The flow-cytometry pattern is consistent with absent oxidative burst, and sequencing suggests a CYBB-related defect.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent severe pneumonia requiring multiple hospitalizations
Persistent current pneumonia with cough, sputum, fever and bilateral crackles
Possible bilateral pulmonary consolidation and pleural effusion on imaging
Onset of recurrent serious infections in early childhood
symptoms_not_in_common: Uvula ulcers are not a classic defining feature
Normal growth percentiles are possible but do not specifically support CGD

data.description: A form of CGD caused by defects in other NADPH oxidase components, such as NCF1, NCF2, NCF4, or CYBA. It produces impaired neutrophil oxidative burst and recurrent infections with catalase-positive organisms.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent pneumonia in infancy and early childhood
Bilateral crackles and radiographic pulmonary infiltrates
Hepatosplenomegaly, which may occur with recurrent infection or inflammatory complications
symptoms_not_in_common: The genetic sequencing pattern described is more suggestive of an X-linked CYBB-associated disorder than an autosomal recessive form
Uvula ulcers are not typical
No consanguinity is reported, although autosomal recessive CGD can still occur without consanguinity

data.description: A primary immunodeficiency, commonly due to STAT3-related disease, characterized by recurrent staphylococcal skin and lung infections, eczema, markedly elevated IgE, and possible lung structural damage such as pneumatoceles.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent pneumonias beginning in early childhood
Current fever, cough, sputum production and pulmonary crackles
symptoms_not_in_common: No eczema is described
No recurrent skin abscesses are described
No characteristic skeletal, dental, or facial findings are described
Hepatosplenomegaly is not a typical principal feature
The absent oxidative-burst flow-cytometry pattern is not typical of hyper-IgE syndrome

data.description: A 34-year-old woman presented with acute abdominal and back pain 3 years before evaluation at the oncology clinic. She had been well until this onset. Her medical history was notable for migraines. She did not smoke cigarettes, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. She worked full time as a social worker and lived in New Jersey with her husband and child. Family history included breast cancer in maternal grandmother (70s), uterine cancer in paternal aunt (40s), and colon cancer in two paternal cousins (30s and 50s). On physical examination: temperature 36.5°C, blood pressure 108/78 mm Hg, heart rate 78 beats per minute, body-mass index 27.7. The abdomen had well-healed surgical scars; remainder of physical examination was normal. Laboratory results showed elevated tumor marker CA 19-9 at 110 IU per milliliter (reference <35), while alpha-fetoprotein and carcinoembryonic antigen levels were normal.

A primary adenocarcinoma arising from bile ducts within the liver. It commonly produces a desmoplastic gland-forming tumor on pathology, may present as multifocal liver masses, and can elevate CA 19-9.
symptoms_in_common: Gland-forming adenocarcinoma with desmoplastic stromal reaction on histology
symptoms_not_in_common: No jaundice reported
No pruritus reported
No fever or cholangitis symptoms reported
Young age for the usual presentation

data.diagnosis: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with liver metastases
data.description: An aggressive pancreatic exocrine adenocarcinoma that often causes abdominal pain radiating to the back, elevated CA 19-9, and liver metastases. Histology typically shows infiltrative malignant glands in dense desmoplastic stroma.
symptoms_in_common: Liver lesions compatible with metastatic disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No pancreatic primary mass is described
No jaundice reported
No weight loss reported
No diabetes or pancreatic insufficiency symptoms reported
Age is substantially younger than typical for pancreatic adenocarcinoma

data.diagnosis: Metastatic upper gastrointestinal or pancreatobiliary adenocarcinoma of occult primary
data.description: Adenocarcinomas originating in the stomach, pancreas, biliary tract, or ampullary region may metastasize to the liver and produce glandular tumors with fibrosis. CA 19-9 can be elevated in pancreatobiliary and some upper gastrointestinal cancers.
symptoms_in_common: Adenocarcinoma with infiltrative glands and stromal desmoplasia
symptoms_not_in_common: No nausea, vomiting, early satiety, or gastrointestinal bleeding reported
No weight loss reported
No identified gastric, pancreatic, ampullary, or biliary primary lesion described
Young age for most gastrointestinal adenocarcinomas

data.diagnosis: Metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma to the liver
data.description: Colorectal cancer frequently metastasizes to the liver and can form glandular lesions. It may be considered given the family history of colorectal cancer, although the normal CEA and elevated CA 19-9 are less characteristic.
symptoms_not_in_common: Carcinoembryonic antigen is normal
CA 19-9 elevation is less typical than CEA elevation
No change in bowel habits reported
No rectal bleeding reported
No iron-deficiency anemia or unexplained weight loss reported
Young age for sporadic colorectal cancer

data.description: A 37-year-old woman presented with a 4-month history of right facial pain and a 3-month history of progressive painful swelling beneath the right ear lobe. Physical examination revealed a soft swelling in the anteroinferior auricular area that was smooth, elastic, mobile and painful on pressure, but not fluctuant. The facial nerve function was normal and the cervical lymph node was not palpable. There were no systemic symptoms. The patient was screened for metastases, and no lung or abdomen lesions were detected.

A rare benign smooth-muscle tumor arising from vascular smooth muscle within or adjacent to the parotid gland. It often forms a well-circumscribed mobile mass and may be painful because of vascular contraction or nerve irritation.
symptoms_in_common: Slowly progressive preauricular or infra-auricular mass

data.diagnosis: Pleomorphic adenoma of the parotid gland
data.description: The most common benign salivary-gland tumor, usually presenting as a slowly growing, mobile, well-defined parotid mass. Histology generally contains epithelial and myoepithelial elements in a chondromyxoid stroma rather than pure smooth-muscle spindle cells.
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain and pressure tenderness are less typical for an uncomplicated pleomorphic adenoma
Soft rather than classically firm consistency
Spindle-cell smooth-muscle-like histology rather than mixed epithelial and myxochondroid histology

data.description: A benign salivary-gland tumor composed of papillary cystic epithelial structures and lymphoid stroma, usually occurring in the parotid gland of older adults, especially male smokers.
symptoms_not_in_common: Patient is a 37-year-old woman, whereas Warthin tumor is more common in older men
Painful pressure-sensitive swelling is not the usual presentation
Mass was not fluctuant or cystic on examination
Spindle-cell histology is not typical
No characteristic epithelial and lymphoid tumor components are described

data.description: A benign peripheral nerve-sheath tumor that may arise from intraparotid branches of the facial nerve or other nerves in the parotid region. It is usually slow growing and may cause pain from nerve compression.
symptoms_in_common: Spindle-cell tumor appearance can occur histologically
symptoms_not_in_common: Painful swelling beneath the ear rather than a clearly nerve-distribution-related lesion
Histology described as smooth-muscle-like whorled fascicles rather than Antoni A/Antoni B areas or Verocay bodies
Immunohistochemical profile consistent with smooth-muscle differentiation would be atypical for schwannoma
No facial nerve symptoms despite possible intraparotid nerve origin

data.diagnosis: Parotid gland carcinoma, including carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma or other salivary malignancy
data.description: Malignant salivary-gland tumors can present with a painful parotid mass and may invade surrounding tissues, regional lymph nodes, or the facial nerve. Imaging and pathology are needed to establish the specific subtype.
symptoms_in_common: Pain, which can be a warning feature of malignancy
symptoms_not_in_common: Mass is mobile, smooth, soft, and elastic rather than fixed or infiltrative
Normal facial nerve function
No cervical lymphadenopathy
No systemic symptoms
No detected lung or abdominal metastatic lesions
Benign-appearing spindle-cell smooth-muscle histology without described atypia, necrosis, or mitotic activity

data.description: At the age of 30 months, the patient began presenting an evolving framework of severe cognitive and neurological impairment, with tetraparesis and mixed spastic-dystonic features, language delay and deafness. Moreover, she has coarse facial features, presenting a high forehead and hypertelorism; her tongue is protruding due to macroglossia.

An X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by iduronate-2-sulfatase deficiency, leading to accumulation of glycosaminoglycans. Severe forms cause progressive neurodevelopmental decline, coarse facies, hearing impairment, macroglossia, spasticity, and characteristic brain white-matter/perivascular-space abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive severe cognitive and neurological impairment beginning in early childhood
Tetraparesis with mixed spastic-dystonic motor impairment
MRI appearance compatible with white-matter changes, enlarged perivascular spaces, and ventriculomegaly seen in mucopolysaccharidoses
symptoms_not_in_common: Female sex is atypical because Hunter syndrome is X-linked and predominantly affects males

data.description: A lysosomal storage disease caused by alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency. The severe Hurler phenotype produces developmental regression, coarse facial features, macroglossia, hearing loss, progressive motor disability, and white-matter abnormalities with ventricular enlargement on brain MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Severe cognitive impairment and language delay
Dystonic features can occur with progressive central nervous system involvement
MRI white-matter signal abnormalities and ventriculomegaly
symptoms_not_in_common: No hepatosplenomegaly is reported
No skeletal dysplasia or joint contractures are reported
No corneal clouding is reported
No cardiac or respiratory involvement is reported

data.description: A group of lysosomal disorders involving impaired heparan-sulfate degradation. It is characterized primarily by progressive neurocognitive decline, severe language impairment, behavioral changes, hearing problems, mild coarse facies, and progressive brain atrophy or white-matter abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive neurological and cognitive deterioration beginning in early childhood
Motor decline with spasticity and dystonia in advanced disease
MRI white-matter abnormalities and ventricular enlargement/atrophy-related ventriculomegaly
symptoms_not_in_common: Macroglossia with persistent tongue protrusion is less typical than in Hurler or Hunter syndrome
Marked tetraparesis at an early age is less characteristic
Behavioral hyperactivity, sleep disturbance, and autistic-like behavior are not reported

data.description: A severe autosomal-recessive lysosomal trafficking disorder caused by deficient mannose-6-phosphate targeting of multiple lysosomal enzymes. It causes coarse facies, gingival/mucosal enlargement, developmental delay, severe skeletal disease, growth failure, and progressive neurologic impairment.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive motor disability and spasticity can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Typical severe skeletal abnormalities, joint stiffness, hip dislocation, and growth failure are not reported
Presentation usually begins in infancy rather than with neurological deterioration beginning at 30 months
The described MRI white-matter pattern is more classically associated with mucopolysaccharidosis

data.description: An autosomal-recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by alpha-mannosidase deficiency. It can cause intellectual disability, speech delay, hearing loss, immune dysfunction, coarse facial features, skeletal abnormalities, ataxia, and progressive motor impairment.
symptoms_in_common: Developmental delay and severe cognitive impairment
symptoms_not_in_common: Macroglossia is not a prominent typical feature
Severe spastic-dystonic tetraparesis is less typical than in severe mucopolysaccharidoses
Recurrent infections, immune deficiency, skeletal abnormalities, and ataxia are not reported
The MRI findings are less specifically characteristic of alpha-mannosidosis

data.description: A male neonate, born at 36+1 weeks gestation via cesarean section due to scarred uterus and fetal heart rate deceleration, weighing 2700g with Apgar scores of 2-8-9. The infant experienced severe asphyxia at birth requiring intubation and chest compressions. After resuscitation, he presented with respiratory distress and difficulty breathing. Following extubation from mechanical ventilation on day 6, the patient developed recurrent inspiratory dyspnea and stridor. The infant had no relevant family history and no history of laryngeal or thoracic surgery.
Impaired movement of both vocal folds, typically leaving them in a paramedian or near-midline position and causing a critically narrowed glottic airway. It is an important cause of neonatal stridor.
symptoms_in_common: Endoscopic appearance of a markedly narrowed glottic opening with vocal folds near the midline
Symptoms occurring in the neonatal period
No history of laryngeal or thoracic surgery
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe perinatal asphyxia requiring chest compressions is not a typical primary manifestation, although hypoxic neurologic injury can be associated with vocal fold paralysis
Initial respiratory failure at birth may have had additional pulmonary or hypoxic causes

data.diagnosis: Acquired bilateral vocal fold paralysis secondary to hypoxic-ischemic neurologic injury
data.description: Bilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve dysfunction or central neurologic injury after severe hypoxia can cause immobility of both vocal folds and upper-airway obstruction after extubation.
symptoms_in_common: Need for intubation and mechanical ventilation
Stridor and inspiratory dyspnea after extubation
Endoscopic narrow glottic aperture consistent with bilateral vocal-fold immobility
symptoms_not_in_common: No documented neurologic abnormalities, brain injury, seizures, or abnormal tone are provided
No history of cardiothoracic surgery or neck surgery, which are common acquired causes of recurrent laryngeal nerve injury

data.diagnosis: Posterior glottic stenosis with bilateral cricoarytenoid fixation
data.description: Scarring or fixation of the posterior glottis and cricoarytenoid joints can prevent vocal-fold abduction, producing a clinical picture similar to bilateral vocal fold paralysis. It may occur after prolonged or traumatic intubation.
symptoms_not_in_common: The intubation duration of approximately 6 days is relatively short for severe post-intubation posterior glottic scarring
Symptoms in the immediate neonatal period may favor congenital vocal-fold dysfunction over established scar stenosis
No reported posterior glottic scar band, granulation tissue, or arytenoid fixation

data.description: Narrowing of the subglottic airway due to edema, scar formation, or cartilage injury after endotracheal intubation. It commonly causes persistent or recurrent stridor after extubation.
symptoms_in_common: Prior endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation
Prematurity, which increases vulnerability to airway injury
symptoms_not_in_common: The described endoscopic images primarily suggest glottic narrowing rather than a subglottic lesion
Inspiratory stridor can occur, but subglottic stenosis often causes biphasic stridor
No reported subglottic scar, circumferential narrowing, or failed passage of an appropriately sized endotracheal tube

data.description: A common congenital cause of neonatal stridor caused by dynamic collapse of supraglottic structures during inspiration. Symptoms often worsen with feeding, crying, or supine positioning.
symptoms_not_in_common: Symptoms became prominent after extubation rather than being clearly present from birth
The endoscopic appearance of a fixed narrow glottic opening is not typical of laryngomalacia
No reported omega-shaped epiglottis, prolapsing arytenoid mucosa, or dynamic supraglottic collapse
Severe airway obstruction requiring prolonged ventilatory support is less typical in uncomplicated laryngomalacia

diagnoses.name: Bilateral vocal cord paralysis
diagnoses.title: Paralysis of vocal cords or larynx[Bilateral]

data.description: 24-year-old man presented with a 2-day history of swelling on the left side of neck and fever. Past medical history included two similar neck abscesses 2 years and 6 years ago, which were treated with antibiotics and drainage. Physical examination showed a 2 cm diameter swelling at the level of thyroid cartilage.

data.diagnosis: Fourth branchial pouch sinus (pyriform sinus fistula) with recurrent left neck abscess
data.description: A congenital tract arising from the apex of the pyriform sinus that commonly causes recurrent infections or abscesses in the left lower anterior neck, often near or involving the thyroid gland.
symptoms_in_common: Swelling at the level of the thyroid cartilage
Prior episodes requiring drainage and antibiotics

data.diagnosis: Acute suppurative thyroiditis due to a pyriform sinus fistula
data.description: A bacterial infection of the thyroid gland, frequently caused in young patients by an underlying congenital pyriform sinus tract that permits contamination from the pharynx.
symptoms_in_common: Location near the thyroid cartilage and thyroid region
History of treatment with antibiotics and drainage
symptoms_not_in_common: No thyroid-specific symptoms such as dysphagia, odynophagia, hoarseness, or thyroid dysfunction are reported

data.diagnosis: Second branchial cleft cyst with recurrent infection
data.description: A congenital epithelial cyst in the lateral neck that may become infected, enlarge rapidly, and form an abscess.
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion is described near the thyroid cartilage rather than the typical upper lateral neck near the angle of the mandible
Repeated left-sided deep neck infections favor a pyriform sinus fistula over a second branchial cleft cyst
Imaging appearance suggesting a tract near the hypopharynx is not typical for a second branchial cleft cyst

data.description: Infection and suppuration of cervical lymph nodes, usually from bacterial infection of the upper aerodigestive tract, skin, or dental sources.
symptoms_in_common: Abscess requiring antibiotic treatment and drainage
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple recurrent episodes over several years in the same left neck region suggest an underlying congenital tract rather than isolated lymph node infection
No preceding sore throat, dental infection, skin infection, or upper respiratory symptoms are reported
The location near the thyroid cartilage is less typical for routine cervical lymphadenitis

data.description: 35-year-old female with intermittent rhinitis presented with 5 days of urticaria, fever, headache, myalgia, and arthralgia. She developed pruritic, painful wheals and erythematous macules >1 cm with burning on the limbs, lasting >24 hours and leaving pigmentation changes. Angioedema involved the hands, fingers, ankles, and feet without pitting. Symptoms included severe headache and myalgia limiting daily activities, with fever up to 39.5°C. She had taken over-the-counter diet pills 18 days before symptom onset and had been seen 6 days earlier for dehydration and violaceous hives on the palms, after which she stopped the pills. Exam showed large confluent wheals and macules on the limbs with marked pruritus and muscle pain. Labs showed lymphopenia and elevated C-reactive protein, with other routine tests and autoimmune studies normal. Skin biopsy showed vacuolar interface change, papillary dermal edema, superficial perivascular lymphocytic and eosinophilic infiltrate, focal fibrin in vessel walls, and erythrocyte extravasation.

A small-vessel immune-complex vasculitis presenting with urticarial-appearing lesions that are painful or burning, persist for about 24 hours or longer, and may leave bruising or hyperpigmentation. Medications and supplements can trigger it.
symptoms_in_common: Pruritic erythematous macules and confluent wheals
Residual pigmentation changes after lesions resolve
Angioedema of hands, fingers, ankles, and feet
Skin biopsy with focal fibrin in vessel walls, erythrocyte extravasation, dermal edema, and perivascular inflammatory infiltrate
Recent exposure to over-the-counter diet pills before symptom onset
symptoms_not_in_common: None clearly atypical; severe myalgia and headache are less common but can occur with systemic involvement

data.diagnosis: Serum sickness-like reaction due to dietary supplement or medication
data.description: A delayed drug-related hypersensitivity reaction, usually occurring days to several weeks after exposure, characterized by rash or urticaria, fever, joint pain, muscle pain, and edema. Unlike classic serum sickness, complement levels are often normal and major immune-complex organ disease is uncommon.
symptoms_in_common: Symptoms began about 18 days after starting over-the-counter diet pills
Angioedema and nonpitting swelling of the hands, feet, and ankles
symptoms_not_in_common: Individual wheals lasting 24 hours with residual pigmentation
Burning and painful lesions rather than predominantly transient itchy hives
Biopsy evidence suggesting vascular injury, including focal fibrin in vessel walls and erythrocyte extravasation

data.description: A systemic form of urticarial vasculitis in which recurrent painful urticarial lesions persist longer than ordinary hives and may be accompanied by fever, arthralgia, angioedema, and inflammatory laboratory abnormalities. It is often associated with low complement levels and sometimes renal, pulmonary, ocular, or gastrointestinal disease.
symptoms_in_common: Biopsy findings compatible with urticarial vasculitis
symptoms_not_in_common: A clear recent medication or supplement trigger favors drug-induced urticarial vasculitis instead
No reported low complement levels
No reported kidney, lung, eye, or gastrointestinal involvement
Normal autoimmune studies

data.description: A mast-cell-mediated medication or supplement reaction causing transient pruritic wheals and deeper swelling of the skin or soft tissues. Lesions usually resolve within hours and do not leave pigmentation or bruising.
symptoms_in_common: Angioedema involving the hands, fingers, ankles, and feet
Recent exposure to over-the-counter diet pills
History of intermittent rhinitis suggesting an atopic tendency
symptoms_not_in_common: Wheals persisting for approximately 24 hours
Painful and burning lesions
Pigmentation changes after lesions resolve
High fever
Severe headache, myalgia, and arthralgia
Elevated C-reactive protein
Biopsy findings of focal fibrin in vessel walls and erythrocyte extravasation

data.description: 16-year-old girl with 4 weeks of intermittent sharp epigastric and upper abdominal pain, worsening over 2 weeks from every few days to twice daily, lasting 2 minutes initially and up to 15 minutes by admission. Two weeks before admission she developed nausea and vomiting, with progression to poor school attendance, decreased appetite, fatigue, dizziness, generalized weakness, and worsening constipation; pain was sometimes relieved after vomiting and worsened with ibuprofen. She had dry mucous membranes and diffuse abdominal tenderness with guarding over the epigastrium and upper quadrants. Initial labs showed leukocytosis, mild anemia, thrombocytosis, and microcytosis; urinalysis and abdominal/pelvic ultrasound were normal. Past history included iron-deficiency anemia and anxiety disorder; she also had pica as a toddler.

data.diagnosis: Rapunzel syndrome (gastric trichobezoar with intestinal extension)
data.description: A large mass of swallowed hair (trichobezoar) filling the stomach with a tail extending into the small intestine, causing gastric outlet or intermittent intestinal obstruction. It is most common in adolescent girls and may be associated with trichotillomania, trichophagia, pica, or psychiatric conditions.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent epigastric and upper abdominal pain
Diffuse abdominal tenderness and epigastric guarding
Microcytic anemia and history of iron-deficiency anemia
Imaging showing a large intragastric mass with extension beyond the stomach
symptoms_not_in_common: Dry mucous membranes are secondary to dehydration rather than a defining feature
Leukocytosis is not always present but may occur with inflammation or obstruction
Thrombocytosis is nonspecific

data.description: A compact accumulation of ingested hair within the stomach. It can cause abdominal pain, vomiting, early satiety, anemia, and gastric outlet obstruction; when it extends into the small bowel it is termed Rapunzel syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Large hair-containing mass seen on endoscopy and CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Dizziness is nonspecific and likely related to dehydration or anemia
Leukocytosis is not a classic isolated finding
Normal abdominal-pelvic ultrasound does not exclude a trichobezoar

data.description: Ulceration of the stomach or duodenal lining, commonly related to Helicobacter pylori infection or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug exposure. It can cause epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, and iron-deficiency anemia from occult bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Microcytic anemia consistent with possible iron deficiency
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive constipation is not typical
A large intragastric mass with hair-like internal material is not consistent with peptic ulcer disease
Pain relieved by vomiting is more suggestive of obstructive gastric pathology
History of pica does not specifically support peptic ulcer disease

data.description: Mechanical blockage at the distal stomach or proximal duodenum, causing impaired gastric emptying. In this case, the obstruction would be caused by the large trichobezoar rather than a tumor or ulcer-related stricture.
symptoms_in_common: Constipation due to reduced intake and dehydration
Palpable or radiographic intragastric obstructing mass
symptoms_not_in_common: Microcytic anemia is not a typical direct consequence of acute gastric outlet obstruction
History of pica is not typical unless the obstruction is due to a bezoar
Thrombocytosis is nonspecific

data.description: Inflammation and injury of the gastric mucosa caused or worsened by nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs such as ibuprofen. It commonly causes epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, and occasionally bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Possible contribution to iron-deficiency anemia if mucosal bleeding occurred
symptoms_not_in_common: The large gastric mass with hair-like appearance on imaging is not explained by gastritis
Progressive obstructive symptoms and vomiting relieved by emesis are less typical
Constipation is not a classic feature
History of pica is not specifically associated with gastritis

data.description: A 45-year-old white man was found dead at home and underwent autopsy as the cause of death was not apparent. He had recently been under review by the respiratory team for poor respiratory function and patchy fibronodular lung changes. His medical history included osteomyelitis of the elbow, congenital kyphoscoliosis, and testicular seminoma, which had been treated with orchidectomy and chemotherapy. At postmortem examination, the abdominal cavity contained copious pus covering the serosal aspect of the small bowel. There was an obvious perforation at the level of the mid-ileum, as well as three ulcers on the mucosal aspect of the ileum, one of which had perforated. Widespread pale nodules measuring up to 5 mm each were noted throughout the parenchyma of both lungs and a small pale lesion was present in the left kidney. No abnormalities were seen in the cardiovascular, endocrine, or central nervous systems.
Systemic infection by Mycobacterium tuberculosis involving the lungs, ileum, and kidney. Ileal tuberculous ulcers can undergo transmural necrosis and perforation, causing fatal purulent peritonitis.
symptoms_in_common: Numerous small pale pulmonary nodules consistent with miliary/disseminated disease
Small pale renal lesion compatible with extrapulmonary tuberculosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Previous testicular seminoma treated with orchidectomy and chemotherapy
Congenital kyphoscoliosis
History of elbow osteomyelitis

data.description: Systemic infection with environmental mycobacteria, particularly Mycobacterium avium complex, which may occur in immunocompromised individuals and can produce pulmonary and gastrointestinal disease with acid-fast organisms.
symptoms_in_common: History of chemotherapy, which may have contributed to impaired immunity
symptoms_not_in_common: Ileal perforation with fatal purulent peritonitis is less typical than in intestinal tuberculosis
Renal lesion is less characteristic
No documented severe immunodeficiency such as advanced HIV infection
Previous testicular seminoma
Congenital kyphoscoliosis

data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that commonly affects the terminal ileum and can cause deep ulceration, transmural inflammation, fistulation, obstruction, or bowel perforation. Noncaseating granulomas may be present.
symptoms_not_in_common: Widespread pale nodules throughout both lungs
Patchy fibronodular pulmonary changes
Small pale kidney lesion
Acid-fast bacilli in tissue
Poor respiratory function as a dominant preceding clinical problem
History of testicular seminoma treated with chemotherapy

data.description: A systemic fungal infection caused by Histoplasma species that may involve lungs, gastrointestinal tract, and other organs, particularly in immunocompromised patients. It can produce granulomatous inflammation and intestinal ulceration.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary nodules and impaired respiratory function
Possible disseminated involvement of lung, bowel, and kidney
Potential association with prior chemotherapy-related immunosuppression
symptoms_not_in_common: Acid-fast bacilli are not a feature of histoplasmosis
Fibronodular lung changes are more suggestive of mycobacterial infection
Ileal perforation is less typical
No described fungal yeast forms in tissue
Previous elbow osteomyelitis
Congenital kyphoscoliosis

data.description: 33-year-old man admitted with chest pain. Two hours before admission, he developed epigastric pain that progressed to central chest pain, with one episode of vomiting, dizziness, dyspnea, sweating, and distal paresthesias; the pain had resolved on arrival. Later that day, he developed nausea, diaphoresis, pallor, blurred vision, muffled hearing, and tingling in both hands, with systolic blood pressure falling to 89 mm Hg and cardiac monitoring showing a 3–4 second pause without P waves. History included syncope with phlebotomy. He had recent flu-like symptoms and a daughter with gastroenteritis. Physical examinations were normal.

data.diagnosis: Cardioinhibitory vasovagal syncope (neurally mediated syncope with sinus arrest)
data.description: A reflex-mediated autonomic event causing abrupt increased vagal tone, hypotension, bradycardia, and sometimes transient sinus arrest or asystole. It is often triggered by pain, nausea, vomiting, emotional stress, or medical procedures.
symptoms_in_common: Nausea and diaphoresis preceding the event
Blurred vision and muffled hearing as presyncopal symptoms
Hypotension with systolic blood pressure of 89 mm Hg
Transient 3-4 second cardiac pause without P waves, consistent with sinus arrest
Tingling in both hands during the episode
symptoms_not_in_common: Initial epigastric pain progressing to central chest pain
Recent flu-like illness
Family exposure to gastroenteritis

data.description: An inherited cardiac sodium-channel disorder that predisposes to ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. ECG findings may include right precordial ST-segment elevation with a coved or saddleback morphology, and the pattern may be unmasked by fever or acute illness.
symptoms_in_common: Possible right precordial ECG repolarization abnormalities in V1-V3
Recent flu-like illness, which may unmask a Brugada ECG pattern
symptoms_not_in_common: Clear vasovagal prodrome with nausea, pallor, sweating, blurred vision, and muffled hearing
Hypotension associated with a pause lacking P waves, suggesting sinus arrest rather than ventricular tachyarrhythmia
Prior syncope specifically triggered by phlebotomy
Epigastric pain and vomiting as the initial presentation
Distal paresthesias

data.description: Inflammation of the myocardium and/or pericardium, often following a viral illness. It can cause chest pain, ECG ST-segment changes, arrhythmias, and occasionally impaired cardiac function.
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain resolved quickly before arrival
No abnormal findings on physical examination
Strong reflex-syncope prodrome including blurred vision, muffled hearing, pallor, and nausea
History of phlebotomy-induced syncope
Sinus pause without P waves in association with hypotension, more typical of a vagal event

data.diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome due to coronary vasospasm (Prinzmetal vasospastic angina)
data.description: Transient coronary artery spasm can cause episodic chest pain and temporary ST-segment elevation, often resolving when the spasm ends. Significant ischemia can occasionally provoke bradyarrhythmias or other rhythm disturbances.
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 33 years without stated coronary risk factors
Prominent vasovagal presyncope symptoms including pallor, muffled hearing, blurred vision, and bilateral hand tingling
History of syncope with phlebotomy
Sinus arrest without P waves associated with nausea and hypotension
Recent viral and gastrointestinal illness exposure

data.diagnosis: Hyperventilation syndrome associated with panic or acute autonomic distress
data.description: Hyperventilation during acute anxiety, pain, or autonomic distress can produce dyspnea, dizziness, chest discomfort, sweating, and distal paresthesias through respiratory alkalosis.
symptoms_in_common: Symptoms occurring during an acute episode
symptoms_not_in_common: Documented systolic hypotension of 89 mm Hg
Documented 3-4 second pause without P waves
Pallor and nausea with a classic vasovagal pattern
History of phlebotomy-triggered syncope
Initial epigastric pain and vomiting

data.description: A 21-year-old man presented to his general practitioner with intermittent left-sided pain in the anterior chest wall associated with neck discomfort. The pain was described as 'stabbing' in nature and had arisen suddenly while watching television, with no history of trauma before onset. The pain was not exacerbated by inspiration or effort. His medical history and physical examination were initially unremarkable. Several days later, he attended the emergency department with worsening chest pain and dyspnea. On examination, chest expansion was equal and breath sounds were normal, although there was crepitus on auscultation of the precordium. Palpation of the neck and supraclavicular fossae detected subcutaneous emphysema. His respiratory rate was 25 breaths per minute and oxygen saturations were 100%. His full blood count and inflammatory markers were within normal limits.

Free air within the mediastinum occurring without trauma or an invasive procedure, often due to rupture of small alveoli with air tracking along bronchovascular sheaths. It can occur in otherwise healthy young adults.
symptoms_in_common: Subcutaneous emphysema in the neck and supraclavicular fossae
CT showing mediastinal air around the trachea

data.description: Air in the pleural space causing partial or complete lung collapse, commonly presenting in young adults with sudden pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath.
symptoms_not_in_common: Chest pain was not worsened by inspiration
Equal chest expansion
Normal breath sounds
Precordial crepitus
Neck and supraclavicular subcutaneous emphysema
Imaging demonstrating mediastinal rather than pleural air

data.description: A full-thickness tear of the esophagus that can release air and gastrointestinal contents into the mediastinum, producing pneumomediastinum and potentially severe mediastinitis.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported vomiting or retching before symptom onset
No fever or systemic inflammatory response
Normal inflammatory markers
Initially well appearance and unremarkable examination
Pain began while resting without an obvious precipitating event

data.description: Inflammation of the pericardium that typically causes sharp chest pain, often worsened by inspiration or lying flat and relieved by sitting forward.
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain was not exacerbated by inspiration
Subcutaneous emphysema
Precordial crepitus
Neck emphysema
Pneumomediastinal air on imaging
Normal inflammatory markers

data.description: 34-year-old man in Scotland presented with an expanding itchy rash on the right flank that persisted for three months. He did not recall any insect bite or foreign travel history, but regularly visits the Scottish highlands. Initial Borrelia serology performed at 4 weeks after rash onset was negative.

data.diagnosis: Erythema migrans due to Lyme borreliosis
data.description: The characteristic expanding annular skin lesion of early Lyme disease, caused by Borrelia infection transmitted by Ixodes ticks. Serology may be negative early in infection, and many patients do not recall a tick bite.
symptoms_in_common: Expanding annular rash with central clearing
Rash persisted and enlarged over weeks to months
Regular exposure to the Scottish Highlands, where tick exposure can occur
No recalled insect bite, which is common in Lyme disease
Negative Borrelia serology at 4 weeks, which does not exclude early Lyme disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Itch is possible but erythema migrans is often not itchy
Three-month persistence without reported systemic symptoms is less typical for untreated early erythema migrans

data.description: A superficial dermatophyte fungal infection causing an itchy, enlarging ring-shaped rash, often with a more active red edge and relative central clearing.
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion appears relatively smooth without clearly described scaling or a raised scaly border
Highland exposure and Lyme testing are not specifically relevant to fungal infection

data.description: A reactive inflammatory skin eruption characterized by slowly enlarging annular red patches or plaques with central clearing; a trailing inner scale may occur.
symptoms_not_in_common: No trailing scale has been described
The large, erythema-migrans-like appearance and tick-exposure setting may favor Lyme disease instead

data.description: A benign inflammatory skin condition producing annular plaques, usually without scale, often on the hands or feet but occasionally elsewhere on the body.
symptoms_in_common: Minimal or absent scaling may fit the image
symptoms_not_in_common: Granuloma annulare is usually asymptomatic rather than itchy
It typically consists of firm papules forming a ring rather than a rapidly expanding erythematous patch
The flank is a less common location than the hands, feet, wrists, or ankles

data.description: A 39-year-old man with a history of current smoking and no other medical history presented with left-sided squeezing chest pain that was worse in the early morning after drinking alcohol and lasted 30 minutes. Initial vital signs showed blood pressure of 132/89 mmHg and pulse rate of 98 beats/minute. Initial laboratory findings revealed creatine kinase 118 U/L (normal 58-348), CK-MB 1.7 ug/L (normal 0-5.0), elevated highly sensitive troponin-T 0.027 ng/mL (normal 0-0.014), and microcytic hypochromic anemia with hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL. Echocardiography showed normal-sized cardiac chambers with good left ventricular systolic function (ejection fraction of 61%) and no regional wall motion abnormality.
Transient epicardial coronary artery spasm causing episodic myocardial ischemia, often occurring at rest during the night or early morning. Smoking and alcohol exposure are recognized triggers.
symptoms_in_common: Left-sided squeezing chest pain at rest
Pain occurring in the early morning
Preserved left ventricular systolic function without regional wall-motion abnormality
symptoms_not_in_common: Microcytic hypochromic anemia

data.diagnosis: Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) due to coronary vasospasm
data.description: Acute myocardial infarction without persistent ST-segment elevation, caused here potentially by prolonged coronary vasospasm producing myocardial injury despite no fixed obstructive coronary lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Smoking as a cardiovascular risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal CK-MB level
Normal creatine kinase level
No regional wall-motion abnormality on echocardiography
Microcytic hypochromic anemia

data.diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome from nonobstructive coronary artery disease (MINOCA)
data.description: Myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries, which may result from coronary vasospasm, plaque disruption, embolism, spontaneous coronary dissection, or microvascular dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated high-sensitivity troponin T indicating myocardial injury
Coronary imaging without clear severe fixed obstructive disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Microcytic hypochromic anemia
Alcohol-associated early-morning timing is more specifically suggestive of vasospastic angina than MINOCA as a general syndrome

data.diagnosis: Unstable angina due to transient coronary vasomotor dysfunction
data.description: New or worsening ischemic chest discomfort occurring at rest due to transient reduction in coronary blood flow, including episodes caused by dynamic coronary spasm.
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated high-sensitivity troponin T, which favors myocardial infarction rather than unstable angina
Microcytic hypochromic anemia

data.description: 12-year-old Saudi boy presented with severe spontaneous dental pain for 3 days. He was the fourth of five siblings. Parents were not related. His mother had 5 previous spontaneous abortions in first trimester. Mother took acetazolamide 1000mg/day for idiopathic intracranial hypertension before and throughout pregnancy. Patient was born at full term via spontaneous vaginal delivery, weighing 2,270g (below 5th percentile). He presented without major dysmorphic features, was intelligent with good behavior, and had normal skin, hair and nails. Intraoral exam showed mixed dentition with retained primary lower central incisors, hypocalcified permanent upper incisors, and multiple carious teeth. Tongue, floor of mouth, upper lip, hard and soft palate were normal.

A congenital limb-malformation disorder characterized by absence or hypoplasia of central fingers and/or toes, producing cleft or lobster-claw-like hands and feet. Dental agenesis and enamel abnormalities can occur in some forms.
symptoms_in_common: Congenital abnormalities of both hands with missing or malformed digits
Congenital abnormalities of both feet with missing or malformed toes
Multiple missing permanent teeth on panoramic radiography
Retained primary lower central incisors, consistent with absent or delayed permanent successors
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe spontaneous dental pain for 3 days
Multiple carious teeth
Low birth weight
Maternal first-trimester spontaneous abortions
Maternal acetazolamide exposure during pregnancy

data.description: A TP63-associated ectodermal dysplasia syndrome characterized by split-hand/split-foot malformations, ectodermal abnormalities, dental agenesis or enamel defects, and frequently cleft lip and/or palate.
symptoms_in_common: Dental caries, which may occur because of enamel defects
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal skin, hair and nails
No cleft lip or cleft palate
Normal tongue, floor of mouth and palate
No major dysmorphic features
Normal intelligence and behavior
Maternal acetazolamide exposure is not a typical cause of EEC syndrome

data.diagnosis: Acetazolamide embryopathy (teratogenic fetal exposure to acetazolamide)
data.description: A congenital malformation pattern attributed to prenatal exposure to acetazolamide, a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor. Reported fetal effects include growth restriction and limb/digital abnormalities; dental developmental abnormalities may be associated with disrupted fetal development.
symptoms_in_common: Documented maternal acetazolamide use before and throughout pregnancy
Low birth weight below the fifth percentile
Congenital hand and foot digital malformations
Dental developmental abnormalities, including hypocalcified incisors
Multiple missing teeth and retained primary teeth
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe acute dental pain is more consistent with caries or pulpal disease than teratogenic exposure itself
Multiple carious teeth are not a defining feature of acetazolamide embryopathy
Maternal recurrent first-trimester spontaneous abortions are not specific for acetazolamide embryopathy
Normal skin, hair and nails do not specifically support or exclude this diagnosis

data.diagnosis: Ectodermal dysplasia with hypodontia and limb anomalies
data.description: A heterogeneous group of genetic disorders affecting ectoderm-derived tissues, often causing hypodontia, enamel hypoplasia, delayed eruption, and sometimes digital malformations such as ectrodactyly or syndactyly.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple dental caries associated with poor enamel quality
Congenital hand and foot digital abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal skin
Normal hair
Normal nails
No reported sweating abnormality
No reported facial dysmorphism
Maternal acetazolamide exposure is not characteristic of a genetic ectodermal dysplasia

data.description: 62-year-old man with hypertension on amlodipine presented with 4 episodes of palpitations over 1 week, described as fast heartbeat and shortness of breath; symptoms varied in timing and duration, and 2 episodes followed alcohol intake. He denied chest pain or syncope. Physical examination showed blood pressure 160/90 mm Hg, regular heart rate of 82 bpm, and normal heart and respiratory findings. Holter monitoring showed frequent supraventricular ectopy and 2 episodes of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
An intermittent supraventricular arrhythmia characterized by episodic, irregular atrial electrical activity that starts and stops spontaneously. Holter monitoring directly documented two episodes.
symptoms_in_common: Variable timing and duration of episodes
Holter-documented episodes of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
symptoms_not_in_common: No chest pain
No syncope
Normal regular heart rate between symptomatic episodes

data.description: Premature atrial contractions are early beats originating in the atria. They can cause skipped beats, fluttering, or brief palpitations and may trigger atrial fibrillation.
symptoms_in_common: Frequent supraventricular ectopic beats on Holter monitoring
Supraventricular couplets and runs on Holter monitoring
Alcohol-associated episodes, as alcohol can increase atrial ectopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Shortness of breath is less typical with isolated premature atrial contractions
Documented sustained paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is beyond isolated atrial ectopy
No chest pain
No syncope

data.description: Alcohol-associated atrial arrhythmia, most commonly atrial fibrillation, occurring after alcohol intake even in people without severe structural heart disease.
symptoms_in_common: Two palpitation episodes followed alcohol intake
Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented on Holter monitoring
symptoms_not_in_common: Not all episodes were clearly associated with alcohol intake
No chest pain
No syncope
Normal physical examination between episodes

data.description: A 58-year-old man presented with a 3-month history of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. He also experienced urinary symptoms including frequency, urgency, and dysuria. Initial colonoscopy revealed prominent congestion and edema, loss of vascular pattern, and multiple moth-eaten ulcers with purulent exudates involving the entire colon. A repeat colonoscopy showed scattered irregular ulcers with with granular background mucosa and 'fuzzy' vasculature. The ileum appeared normal.

data.diagnosis: Intestinal T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (ITCL-NOS)
data.description: A rare aggressive peripheral T-cell lymphoma involving the gastrointestinal tract, often presenting with ulcerative colitis-like colonic lesions, abdominal symptoms, weight loss, and destructive lymphoid infiltration on biopsy.
symptoms_in_common: Normal ileum can occur when disease is limited to the colon
symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary frequency
Urinary urgency
Dysuria

data.diagnosis: Primary colorectal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
data.description: An aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that can arise in the colon and produce abdominal pain, diarrhea, weight loss, ulcerated mucosal lesions, and inflammatory-appearing colonoscopic findings.
symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary frequency
Urinary urgency
Dysuria
No discrete mass lesion was described
Entire-colon inflammatory involvement is less typical than focal or segmental disease

data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease characterized by continuous mucosal inflammation of the colon, causing diarrhea, abdominal discomfort, weight loss, erythema, edema, loss of vascular pattern, friability, and ulceration.
symptoms_not_in_common: Age at first presentation of 58 years is less typical
Moth-eaten irregular ulcers with purulent exudate are not classic
Urinary frequency
Urinary urgency
Dysuria

data.description: A form of Crohn disease confined predominantly to the colon, characterized by patchy transmural inflammation, irregular ulcers, abdominal pain, diarrhea, weight loss, and possible extraintestinal complications.
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse involvement of the entire colon without described skip areas
Normal ileum
No perianal disease, fistula, stricture, or small-bowel involvement described
Urinary frequency
Urinary urgency
Dysuria

data.description: A previously healthy 9-year-old boy presented to the emergency department with a 6-hour history of left chest pain and increasing respiratory distress. His vital signs showed a respiratory rate of 40/min and heart rate of 105/min. Physical examination revealed unremarkable cardiac auscultation, while auscultation of lung fields showed diminished breath sounds over the left side.

data.diagnosis: Ruptured pulmonary hydatid cyst with secondary hydropneumothorax
data.description: Pulmonary echinococcosis caused by Echinococcus larvae can form a lung cyst. Rupture into a bronchus or pleural space may produce an air-fluid level, detached internal membranes (water-lily/camellia sign), pneumothorax, and pleural effusion.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging appearance of a left pleural air-fluid level with internal membrane-like structures
symptoms_not_in_common: Very abrupt 6-hour presentation is less typical for an intact hydatid cyst, although it is typical after rupture
No reported cough, hemoptysis, expectoration of membranes, fever, or known exposure to dogs/sheep

data.description: Hydropneumothorax is the simultaneous presence of air and fluid in the pleural space, causing partial lung collapse. It may occur spontaneously or secondary to infection, trauma, a ruptured cyst, or an underlying lung lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Reduced breath sounds on the affected side
Large left-sided pleural air-fluid level on chest radiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Internal membrane-like radiographic structures are not typical of uncomplicated spontaneous hydropneumothorax
No documented trauma, recent procedure, or pre-existing lung disease

data.description: A spontaneous pneumothorax occurs when air enters the pleural space, leading to partial or complete lung collapse. It classically causes sudden pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, and reduced breath sounds.
symptoms_not_in_common: A prominent pleural fluid level is not typical of a simple pneumothorax
Membrane-like structures within the air-fluid collection are not typical
No reported hyperresonance or unilateral increase in chest size

data.description: Empyema is infected pleural fluid, usually following pneumonia. If a bronchopleural fistula develops, air enters the pleural collection and produces a pyopneumothorax or hydropneumothorax.
symptoms_in_common: Decreased breath sounds over the affected hemithorax
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported fever
No reported cough or preceding pneumonia
No systemic toxic appearance described
Membrane-like structures on imaging are atypical for empyema

data.description: 63-year-old man with well-controlled hypertension and diabetes was referred from primary clinic due to hepatic mass found on ultrasonography. Physical examination was unremarkable. Laboratory findings showed normal hematological indexes, liver function tests, and renal functions. Patient was negative for viral markers with normal α-fetoprotein levels. Bone marrow biopsy showed 30% marrow cellularity but was otherwise normal. Serum calcium, β-2 microglobulin, and serum/urine protein immunoelectrophoresis were normal. Skeletal radiography revealed no abnormalities.
A rare localized plasma-cell neoplasm arising outside the bone marrow, in this case involving the liver, without evidence of systemic multiple myeloma.
symptoms_in_common: Normal bone marrow examination without clonal plasma-cell infiltration
Normal serum and urine protein immunoelectrophoresis
Histology showing sheets of plasmacytoid cells
Immunohistochemical appearance consistent with plasma-cell differentiation
symptoms_not_in_common: No constitutional symptoms such as weight loss, fever, or night sweats
No hepatomegaly or abdominal pain on examination

data.diagnosis: Multiple myeloma with hepatic plasmacytoma involvement
data.description: A systemic malignant plasma-cell disorder that typically involves bone marrow and may rarely produce extramedullary masses in the liver.
symptoms_in_common: Plasma-cell tumor morphology in the hepatic lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal serum and urine protein immunoelectrophoresis without monoclonal protein
Normal serum calcium
Normal renal function
Normal hematologic indices without anemia
Bone marrow biopsy without significant plasma-cell infiltration
No lytic skeletal lesions
No bone pain
No systemic symptoms

data.description: A lymphoma predominantly involving the liver, often presenting as a solitary or multifocal hepatic mass and potentially showing lymphoid-appearing cells on biopsy.
symptoms_in_common: Potentially normal liver function tests in localized disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Histology is more consistent with plasma-cell proliferation than typical lymphoma
No fever, night sweats, or weight loss
No lymphadenopathy reported
No splenomegaly reported
Normal hematologic indices

data.description: A primary malignant tumor of hepatocytes, usually occurring in patients with chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, or other chronic liver disease.
symptoms_in_common: Hepatic mass on ultrasonography and cross-sectional imaging
Diabetes, which may be associated with metabolic liver disease risk
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal alpha-fetoprotein
Negative viral markers
Normal liver function tests
No reported cirrhosis or chronic liver disease
Histology showing plasma-cell-like cells rather than malignant hepatocytes
No abdominal pain, weight loss, or hepatomegaly

diagnoses.title: Extramedullary plasmacytoma

data.description: Young female European traveler presenting to a medical clinic in central Australia with vaginal discharge after sexual intercourse with a new partner, another European traveler, 1 week earlier in Sydney.
A sexually transmitted infection caused by Chlamydia trachomatis that commonly causes cervicitis and may be asymptomatic or present with abnormal vaginal discharge.
symptoms_in_common: Recent unprotected or new-partner sexual exposure
Symptoms occurring about 1 week after intercourse
symptoms_not_in_common: No pelvic or lower abdominal pain reported
No dysuria reported
No intermenstrual or postcoital bleeding reported
No fever reported

data.description: A sexually transmitted infection caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae that can infect the cervix and cause increased, mucopurulent vaginal discharge.
symptoms_in_common: Recent sexual contact with a new partner
Possible onset within days to a week after exposure
symptoms_not_in_common: No purulent discharge description provided
No pain with urination reported
No pelvic pain reported
No fever reported

data.description: A sexually transmitted vaginal infection caused by the protozoan Trichomonas vaginalis, often causing discharge, vaginal irritation, and sometimes a characteristic frothy or malodorous discharge.
symptoms_in_common: Recent sexual exposure to a new partner
symptoms_not_in_common: No vaginal itching or irritation reported
No foul-smelling discharge reported
No frothy or yellow-green discharge described
No pain during urination or intercourse reported

data.description: An imbalance of normal vaginal bacteria that can cause thin vaginal discharge with a fishy odor, sometimes more noticeable after intercourse.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fishy vaginal odor reported
No thin gray or white discharge description provided
New sexual partner is a risk association but bacterial vaginosis is not necessarily sexually transmitted

data.description: A yeast infection of the vagina, usually caused by Candida species, which commonly causes itching and thick white discharge.
symptoms_not_in_common: No vulvar or vaginal itching reported
No thick white or curd-like discharge described
No vulvar redness or soreness reported
Temporal association with a new sexual partner is less typical

data.description: A sexually transmitted bacterial infection that can cause cervicitis, abnormal vaginal discharge, dysuria, or postcoital bleeding and may be asymptomatic.
symptoms_in_common: Recent exposure to a new sexual partner
symptoms_not_in_common: No dysuria reported
No postcoital bleeding reported
No pelvic pain reported
No fever reported

data.description: A 44-year-old man with a 17-year history of tobacco and cannabis use presented with acute dyspnoea and left-sided pleuritic chest pain. He had no other medical conditions and took no regular medications. On examination, he was thin and hypoxic, with a silent, hyper-resonant left hemithorax. Laboratory results showed normal α-1 antitrypsin concentration (1.4 g/L), normal immunoglobulins, and specific IgE for Aspergillus. Spirometry revealed severe obstruction with FVC of 2.95 L (57% predicted), FEV1 of 1.37 L (34% predicted), and FEV1/FVC ratio of 59% predicted.

A severe form of bullous emphysema characterized by very large air-filled bullae, often affecting the upper lobes and compressing adjacent functioning lung. It is strongly associated with cigarette smoking and cannabis use and can mimic pneumothorax on chest radiography.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging showing a very large left-sided bulla with compression of remaining lung

data.diagnosis: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with emphysema
data.description: A progressive obstructive lung disease, usually caused by smoking, in which destruction of alveolar walls causes air trapping, hyperinflation, and impaired airflow. Bullae may develop in advanced emphysema.
symptoms_in_common: Severe airflow obstruction with reduced FEV1 and FEV1/FVC ratio
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset of pleuritic left-sided chest pain
Markedly unilateral silent left hemithorax
Very large focal left-sided bulla causing substantial compression of adjacent lung

data.diagnosis: Secondary spontaneous pneumothorax due to bullous emphysema
data.description: A pneumothorax caused by rupture of a bulla or bleb in a person with underlying lung disease, such as emphysema. It typically presents suddenly with pleuritic chest pain, dyspnoea, reduced breath sounds, and hyper-resonance.
symptoms_not_in_common: Imaging appearance is more consistent with a giant intrapulmonary bulla than a pleural air collection
No clearly described pleural line or complete collapse of the left lung
Severe chronic obstructive spirometry suggests substantial pre-existing emphysema rather than an isolated pneumothorax

data.description: Bullous emphysema occurring in association with chronic cannabis smoking, often in relatively young adults and frequently involving large upper-lobe or paraseptal bullae. Concurrent tobacco use increases risk.
symptoms_in_common: Relatively young age for severe emphysematous disease
Large bullous abnormality on chest imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Cannabis-associated bullous disease is not always associated with severe diffuse airflow obstruction
Hypoxia is more typical when bullae are very extensive or complicated by compression or pneumothorax

data.description: 62-year-old man with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus presented with 3 months of progressive fatigue, anorexia, weight loss, and vague upper abdominal pain. Past history included a 40-pack-year smoking history (quit 2 years earlier) and moderate alcohol use. Family history was notable for smoking-related lung cancer in his mother. On presentation, he had renal insufficiency (creatinine 3.2 mg/dL), severe anemia (hemoglobin 7 g/dL), thrombocytopenia (77,000/µL), hypercalcemia (12.7 mg/dL), elevated total protein (>10 g/dL), biochemical evidence of tumor lysis syndrome (LDH 1,157 U/L, uric acid 20.8 mg/dL), and coagulopathy consistent with disseminated intravascular clotting (prolonged PT and aPTT, low fibrinogen, elevated D-dimer and fibrin split products).

An aggressive mature B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma characterized by very rapid proliferation, frequent bulky abdominal disease, a high risk of spontaneous tumor lysis syndrome, and possible bone marrow and renal involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Vague upper abdominal pain with bulky abdominal mass on imaging
Severe hyperuricemia and biochemical tumor lysis syndrome
Severe anemia and thrombocytopenia suggesting bone marrow involvement
Histology showing a high-grade lymphoid neoplasm with a starry-sky appearance
B-cell marker staining consistent with CD20-positive lymphoma
Possible disseminated intravascular coagulation in advanced aggressive lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypercalcemia is less typical than in multiple myeloma or some other lymphomas
Markedly elevated total protein is not a classic defining feature
Age 62 years is older than the more typical age for sporadic Burkitt lymphoma

data.description: The most common aggressive non-Hodgkin B-cell lymphoma in adults; it can produce bulky nodal or extranodal abdominal masses, constitutional symptoms, marrow infiltration, renal dysfunction, and tumor lysis syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Fatigue, anorexia, weight loss, and abdominal pain
Anemia and thrombocytopenia compatible with marrow involvement
Coagulopathy/DIC can occur in advanced aggressive disease
symptoms_not_in_common: The highly monomorphic starry-sky histologic pattern is more characteristic of Burkitt lymphoma
Extreme uric acid elevation and fulminant spontaneous tumor lysis syndrome are especially suggestive of Burkitt lymphoma
Hypercalcemia and elevated total protein are not typical primary features

data.description: A malignant plasma-cell disorder causing excess monoclonal immunoglobulin production, anemia, renal impairment, hypercalcemia, and marrow replacement; it may occasionally form extramedullary plasmacytomas.
symptoms_not_in_common: Bulky abdominal lymphomatous mass is not typical
