Very high LDH and marked spontaneous tumor lysis syndrome are unusual
Disseminated intravascular coagulation is uncommon
Starry-sky high-grade lymphoid morphology is not typical
CD20-positive B-cell lymphoma staining would not be expected for typical plasma cell myeloma
No lytic bone lesions, bone pain, or documented monoclonal protein studies are provided

data.description: A 26-year-old woman presented with a one-year history of rash on her lower legs, abdomen, and arms, accompanied by a six-month history of paraesthesia in her right hand and left foot. She had no history of fatigue, weight loss, fever, or arthralgia. Neurological examination showed reduced sensation to light touch in the right ring and little fingers, the lateral palmar and dorsal hand, the left lateral calf, and the dorsum of the left foot. She experienced clumsiness in her right hand causing difficulty with writing, but no weakness was noted. Blood tests, including a full autoimmune screen, were normal. Electromyography demonstrated sensory damage in the right ulnar nerve and asymmetrical superficial sensory damage in the peroneal nerve, with greater involvement on the left side.

data.diagnosis: Cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa (cutaneous PAN) with mononeuritis multiplex
data.description: A necrotizing vasculitis of small-to-medium muscular arteries limited predominantly to the skin, sometimes associated with peripheral nerve involvement. Skin biopsy typically shows necrotizing inflammation of a medium-sized vessel.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic purpuric/livedoid rash on the legs, abdomen, and arms
Asymmetric sensory neuropathy involving separate peripheral nerves
Hand clumsiness related to sensory dysfunction
Normal autoimmune blood tests can occur
Absence of systemic constitutional symptoms is consistent with skin-limited disease
Biopsy appearance of necrotizing vasculitis involving a muscular vessel

data.description: A necrotizing vasculitis of medium-sized arteries that can affect skin, peripheral nerves, kidneys, gastrointestinal tract, and other organs. Mononeuritis multiplex and livedo-like skin lesions are characteristic manifestations.
symptoms_in_common: Asymmetric peripheral neuropathy consistent with mononeuritis multiplex
Ulnar and peroneal nerve sensory involvement
Histologic necrotizing vasculitis of a medium-sized vessel
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, fatigue, or weight loss
No arthralgia
No reported hypertension, renal disease, abdominal pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, or other visceral organ involvement
No motor weakness

data.description: Small-vessel vasculitis, including microscopic polyangiitis or granulomatosis with polyangiitis, can cause painful asymmetric peripheral neuropathy and skin purpura, often with systemic renal, pulmonary, or constitutional features.
symptoms_in_common: Vasculitic inflammation on skin biopsy may be present
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal autoimmune screen, with no reported ANCA positivity
No renal symptoms or urinary abnormalities reported
No respiratory, sinus, or pulmonary symptoms
No systemic constitutional symptoms
Histology of a medium-sized muscular artery is more suggestive of polyarteritis nodosa than classic ANCA-associated small-vessel vasculitis

data.description: An immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis, often associated with hepatitis C or autoimmune disease, that may cause palpable purpura, arthralgia, weakness, renal disease, and peripheral neuropathy.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fatigue or weakness
No arthralgia
No renal manifestations reported
Normal autoimmune blood tests
Distribution includes abdomen and arms rather than predominantly dependent lower-limb palpable purpura
Medium-vessel necrotizing vasculitis is less typical than small-vessel leukocytoclastic vasculitis

data.description: An ANCA-associated necrotizing vasculitis characterized by asthma, eosinophilia, sinus disease, pulmonary involvement, skin lesions, and frequently mononeuritis multiplex.
symptoms_in_common: Mononeuritis multiplex pattern affecting ulnar and peroneal nerves
symptoms_not_in_common: No asthma reported
No allergic rhinitis or sinus disease reported
No eosinophilia reported
No pulmonary symptoms
No constitutional symptoms
Biopsy does not describe eosinophil-rich inflammation or granulomatous disease

data.description: 17-year-old male with high myopia and craniofacial-skeletal abnormalities. Full-term vaginal birth, birth weight 4.3 kg. Height tracked at the 80th percentile until age 15, then plateaued at the 55th percentile. At age 12, had dental crowding, class III dentofacial growth pattern, and retroclined lower teeth. At age 13, developed a grade 3/6 systolic heart murmur. Pectus excavatum was present at birth. Current exam/measurements: weight 66.3 kg, height 177.5 cm, head circumference 58.5 cm (98th percentile), with scoliosis and loss of normal upper spinal curvature. Laboratory findings show marked hyperhomocysteinemia with elevated methionine; vitamin B12, folate, methylmalonic acid, hemoglobin, hematocrit, and MCV were normal.

data.diagnosis: Classic homocystinuria due to cystathionine beta-synthase (CBS) deficiency
data.description: An autosomal-recessive disorder of methionine metabolism causing markedly elevated homocysteine and methionine. It commonly produces ectopia lentis, severe myopia, marfanoid skeletal features, osteoporosis, and increased thromboembolic risk.
symptoms_in_common: Lens abnormalities consistent with ectopia lentis/subluxation
Low bone mineral density and vertebral deformities on imaging
Tall or relatively long-limbed skeletal habitus
Dental crowding and class III dentofacial growth pattern
Heart murmur, potentially related to valvular disease
Normal vitamin B12, folate, methylmalonic acid, and blood indices
symptoms_not_in_common: No thromboembolic event has been reported
No developmental delay or intellectual impairment has been reported

data.description: An autosomal-dominant connective-tissue disorder caused most often by pathogenic variants in FBN1. It is characterized by skeletal overgrowth, pectus deformity, scoliosis, ectopia lentis, myopia, and cardiovascular disease such as aortic-root dilation and mitral-valve prolapse.
symptoms_in_common: Scoliosis and loss of normal spinal curvature
Relatively tall stature or marfanoid body habitus
Dental crowding and craniofacial skeletal abnormalities
Heart murmur, which could occur with mitral-valve prolapse
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked hyperhomocysteinemia
Elevated methionine
Biochemical findings indicating an inborn error of methionine metabolism
No reported aortic-root dilation or aortic aneurysm
No reported family history of autosomal-dominant connective-tissue disease

data.diagnosis: Homocystinuria due to a remethylation defect, such as methionine synthase or methionine synthase reductase deficiency
data.description: These inherited disorders impair remethylation of homocysteine to methionine, causing hyperhomocysteinemia and often neurologic, developmental, hematologic, and ophthalmologic manifestations. Unlike CBS deficiency, methionine is usually low or normal rather than elevated.
symptoms_in_common: High myopia or other ophthalmologic involvement can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated methionine, which is atypical because remethylation defects usually lower methionine
Normal methylmalonic acid is less supportive of combined cobalamin-processing disorders
Normal hemoglobin, hematocrit, and MCV without megaloblastic anemia
Prominent pectus excavatum, scoliosis, and marfanoid skeletal phenotype
Lens subluxation is less characteristic than in CBS deficiency
No reported neurologic regression, seizures, cognitive impairment, or peripheral neuropathy

data.diagnosis: Vitamin B12 or folate deficiency causing acquired hyperhomocysteinemia
data.description: Deficiency of vitamin B12 or folate can impair homocysteine remethylation and elevate plasma homocysteine. It commonly causes macrocytic/megaloblastic anemia and, in vitamin B12 deficiency, elevated methylmalonic acid and neurologic symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated methionine
Normal vitamin B12 and folate concentrations
Normal methylmalonic acid
Normal hemoglobin, hematocrit, and MCV
High myopia with lens subluxation
Pectus excavatum
Scoliosis and vertebral bone abnormalities
Dental and craniofacial skeletal abnormalities
No reported neuropathy, cognitive change, glossitis, or fatigue

data.description: 29-year-old right-hand dominant male with hypothyroidism on thyroxine presented with 4 days of gradually worsening dull left-sided neck pain radiating to the head, diplopia, right-sided numbness, dropping objects at work, and unsteadiness. He denied alcohol or illicit drug use, seizure, head injury, or loss of consciousness. On examination, he was alert and oriented, with right-sided weakness (MRC grade 4), pronator drift, and decreased pinprick, light touch, and proprioception on the right. He also had resting and intention tremor, dysdiadochokinesia, broad-based cerebellar gait, right upgoing plantar response, and diplopia on extreme gaze without ocular palsy or papilloedema.

data.diagnosis: Pontine cavernous malformation (brainstem cavernoma) with recent hemorrhage
data.description: A cerebral cavernous malformation is a cluster of fragile, low-flow vascular channels that can bleed repeatedly. In the pons, even a small hemorrhage can cause prominent long-tract, cranial-nerve, and cerebellar symptoms. The hyperdense pontine lesion on CT and mixed-signal brainstem lesion on MRI are compatible with a hemorrhagic cavernoma.
symptoms_in_common: Subacute progressive headache and left-sided neck pain
Right-sided loss of pinprick, light touch, and proprioception
Dropping objects due to impaired right-sided motor control
Imaging evidence of a focal pontine lesion with hemorrhagic appearance
Ventricular enlargement consistent with obstructive hydrocephalus from posterior fossa/brainstem pathology
symptoms_not_in_common: No prior known episodes of neurological deficits or prior intracranial hemorrhage
No seizure
No loss of consciousness

data.description: Pontine hemorrhage is bleeding within the pons that can produce contralateral weakness and sensory loss, ataxia, tremor, diplopia, and obstructive hydrocephalus. In a young patient without hypertension, an underlying vascular lesion such as a cavernoma is more likely than spontaneous hypertensive hemorrhage.
symptoms_in_common: CT appearance of a hyperdense pontine focus suggesting acute or subacute blood
Hydrocephalus/ventricular dilatation due to obstruction of cerebrospinal-fluid pathways
symptoms_not_in_common: Gradual progression over 4 days rather than abrupt severe onset
Young age with no stated hypertension
Alert, oriented mental status without coma or marked reduced consciousness
No vomiting or severe abrupt headache reported

data.diagnosis: Brainstem glioma (pontine tumor), possibly with intratumoral hemorrhage
data.description: A brainstem glioma is a tumor arising within the pons or adjacent brainstem structures. It may cause progressive cranial-nerve symptoms, corticospinal tract signs, sensory deficits, cerebellar dysfunction, and hydrocephalus when it obstructs the fourth ventricle or cerebral aqueduct. Hemorrhage within a tumor can create a hyperdense CT focus.
symptoms_in_common: Tremor and impaired rapid alternating movements
Ventricular enlargement compatible with obstructive hydrocephalus
symptoms_not_in_common: Very short 4-day clinical course is less typical for most gliomas
Focal hyperdense hemorrhagic appearance is more suggestive of a vascular lesion or hemorrhage than a typical diffuse glioma
No persistent cranial-nerve palsy despite diplopia
No papilloedema despite ventricular enlargement

data.description: 18-year-old male with 4 days of fatigue, subjective fever, chills, headache, non-bloody non-bilious vomiting, diarrhea, decreased appetite, low back pain, dysuria, and fever with pain in the lower abdomen, groin, and scrotum. Past history: exercise-induced asthma and childhood hospitalization for diarrhea; born in Central America and moved to the US at age 15. Recent tests were negative for tuberculosis IGRA, HIV, syphilis, gonorrhea, and chlamydia. On examination, he appeared tired, ताप 39.4°C, tachycardic, tachypneic, and had low back paraspinal muscle tenderness.

Systemic infection caused by Histoplasma capsulatum, often acquired by inhalation of fungal spores and capable of disseminating through macrophages to bone marrow, liver, spleen, lymph nodes, and other tissues. Bone-marrow histology may show intracellular small yeasts within macrophages.
symptoms_in_common: Origin from Central America, an endemic region
Imaging and marrow findings potentially consistent with disseminated fungal infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Dysuria
Prominent groin and scrotal pain
Low back paraspinal muscle tenderness

data.description: A systemic protozoal infection caused by Leishmania species and transmitted by sandflies. It can cause prolonged fever, constitutional symptoms, hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, and bone-marrow macrophages containing intracellular amastigotes.
symptoms_in_common: Central American birth, with possible prior exposure in an endemic region
Bone marrow appearance potentially showing intracellular organisms in macrophages
symptoms_not_in_common: Very acute 4-day presentation
Dysuria
Scrotal and groin pain
Low back paraspinal tenderness
No reported hepatosplenomegaly
No reported weight loss or pancytopenia

data.description: A bacterial infection of the kidney and upper urinary tract, usually caused by enteric gram-negative organisms such as Escherichia coli. Severe disease can cause systemic inflammatory response or sepsis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Diarrhea is less typical as a prominent symptom
Scrotal and groin pain are not classic for uncomplicated pyelonephritis
Bone-marrow intracellular-organism findings would not be expected
Imaging suggesting a pelvic soft-tissue or muscle process would be atypical for isolated pyelonephritis

data.description: An acute bacterial infection of the prostate, commonly caused by urinary gram-negative bacteria. It can produce fever, systemic toxicity, dysuria, pelvic or lower abdominal pain, and pain radiating to the groin, scrotum, or low back.
symptoms_not_in_common: Diarrhea is not a usual major feature
Headache is nonspecific rather than typical
Bone marrow histology with intracellular organisms is not expected
Possible disseminated infectious imaging findings would be unusual for uncomplicated prostatitis

data.description: A deep bacterial infection of the iliopsoas or adjacent pelvic musculature, often caused by Staphylococcus aureus or enteric organisms. It may cause fever, systemic illness, abdominal pain, groin pain, hip-region pain, and low back pain; CT or MRI may demonstrate muscle enlargement, inflammation, or abscess.
symptoms_in_common: Low back pain and paraspinal tenderness
Imaging potentially showing pelvic or iliopsoas muscle abnormality
symptoms_not_in_common: Dysuria is not typical unless there is associated urinary tract involvement
Scrotal pain is not a classic primary symptom
Diarrhea and vomiting are nonspecific
Bone-marrow intracellular fungal or protozoal-appearing organisms would not be explained by isolated bacterial pyomyositis

data.description: This is a 56-year-old woman who underwent radical nephrectomy and lymph-node resection for clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma in February 2012. During subsequent follow-up, a single metastasis to the body of the left mandible was detected. She was referred in October 2012 for resection of the mandibular metastasis and fibular free-flap reconstruction. Two months later, bone scintigraphy revealed good vascularization of the flap, though additional bone metastases to the right humerus and pelvis were detected. In January 2014, the patient presented with visible bone exposure in the area of the graft with inflammation of surrounding tissues. Over days, there was an increase in bone exposure and necrosis without evidence of acute secondary infection.

data.diagnosis: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ), likely bisphosphonate- or denosumab-associated
data.description: Progressive exposed, nonhealing necrotic jaw bone in a patient receiving or previously exposed to antiresorptive therapy, commonly used for skeletal metastases. It may occur in native mandibular bone or in vascularized bone grafts.
symptoms_in_common: No evidence of acute secondary infection
History of metastatic cancer with additional skeletal metastases, a setting in which bone-targeted antiresorptive treatment is commonly used
Mandibular surgery and fibular free-flap reconstruction, which can act as local precipitating factors
symptoms_not_in_common: Antiresorptive medication exposure is not explicitly stated in the provided history
Pain, purulent drainage, fistula formation, and tooth loosening are not described

data.diagnosis: Chronic osteomyelitis of the reconstructed mandible
data.description: A persistent inflammatory or infectious process involving mandibular bone that can cause devitalized bone, sequestrum formation, mucosal breakdown, and exposed bone after major oral surgery or reconstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Exposed bone in the reconstructed mandibular region
History of extensive mandibular surgery and free-flap reconstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: No acute secondary infection was identified
Fever, leukocytosis, purulent drainage, severe pain, and systemic illness are not reported
The rapid progression of exposed necrotic bone without clear infection is more suggestive of osteonecrosis than primary infection

data.diagnosis: Recurrent or progressive metastatic clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma involving the mandible or fibular graft
data.description: Clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma can metastasize to bone and produce destructive osteolytic lesions. Local recurrence or metastatic involvement of the reconstructed mandible could contribute to bone destruction and mucosal breakdown.
symptoms_in_common: Additional documented bone metastases to the humerus and pelvis
Progressive bony destruction/necrosis in the mandibular reconstruction area
symptoms_not_in_common: The presentation emphasizes exposed devitalized bone rather than a growing mass or destructive tumor lesion
No bleeding, facial swelling, pain, paresthesia, or biopsy evidence of recurrent tumor is described
Inflammation around exposed bone without acute infection is more characteristic of jaw osteonecrosis

data.diagnosis: Ischemic necrosis or failure of the fibular free-flap bone graft
data.description: Compromised vascular supply to a vascularized fibular bone flap can lead to graft nonunion, bone devitalization, mucosal dehiscence, and eventual exposure of necrotic graft bone.
symptoms_in_common: Bone exposure located in the area of the fibular graft
History of mandibular reconstruction with a fibular free flap
symptoms_not_in_common: Prior bone scintigraphy showed good vascularization of the flap
The flap problem developed more than a year after reconstruction rather than in the early postoperative period
No flap skin-paddle ischemia, acute flap loss, or early wound-healing failure is reported

data.description: Radiation-induced hypovascular, hypocellular bone injury causing chronic nonhealing exposed bone and necrosis, typically after therapeutic radiation to the head and neck.
symptoms_in_common: Lack of an acute infection despite necrotic bone
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of radiotherapy to the mandible or head and neck is provided
The mandibular lesion was treated surgically with free-flap reconstruction rather than described as having received radiation
Medication-related osteonecrosis or graft-associated necrosis is more plausible in the provided clinical context

data.description: 67-year-old man with 10 days of nausea, nonbloody vomiting, bloating, and epigastric pain unrelieved by omeprazole, followed on the day of presentation by exertional substernal, nonradiating chest heaviness that progressed to rest pain with diaphoresis and dyspnea. Past history includes mild asthma and prior hemicolectomy for dysplastic polyps with ventral hernia; remote 20 pack-year smoking history. On exam he was tachycardic, hypotensive, tachypneic, and mildly hypoxemic on oxygen, appearing uncomfortable with pallor and diaphoresis. He had elevated jugular venous pressure, a grade 2/6 holosystolic apical murmur, left basilar rales, a palpable liver edge 4 cm below the costal margin, and cool, clammy extremities with thready pulses.

A rare, rapidly progressive inflammatory myocarditis characterized histologically by multinucleated giant cells, myocyte necrosis, and mixed inflammatory infiltrates. It can mimic acute myocardial infarction and rapidly cause severe heart failure, arrhythmias, cardiogenic shock, and mitral regurgitation.
symptoms_in_common: Acute substernal chest heaviness progressing from exertional to rest pain
Left basilar rales consistent with pulmonary congestion
Hepatomegaly consistent with systemic venous congestion
Cool clammy extremities and thready pulses consistent with cardiogenic shock
Holosystolic apical murmur consistent with acute functional mitral regurgitation
Nausea, vomiting, and epigastric pain that may represent a prodromal systemic illness or low-output state
ECG abnormalities and imaging findings compatible with acute cardiac dysfunction
Myocardial biopsy appearance with inflammatory infiltrates, myocyte injury, and giant cells
symptoms_not_in_common: Ten days of prominent bloating
Prior hemicolectomy for dysplastic colonic polyps
Ventral hernia

data.description: An acute inflammatory injury to the myocardium, often following a viral or other systemic illness, which can produce chest pain, acute systolic heart failure, arrhythmias, pulmonary edema, and cardiogenic shock. Unlike giant cell myocarditis, typical biopsy findings are predominantly lymphocytic inflammation without characteristic multinucleated giant cells.
symptoms_in_common: Recent gastrointestinal prodrome with nausea and vomiting
Chest pain resembling acute coronary syndrome
Cool clammy extremities and poor peripheral pulses
Possible acute mitral regurgitation from severe ventricular dysfunction
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy features suggesting multinucleated giant cells rather than purely lymphocytic myocarditis
Older age is less typical than for many viral myocarditis presentations
Ten days of marked bloating
Prior hemicolectomy and ventral hernia

data.diagnosis: Acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock
data.description: Acute myocardial necrosis caused by abrupt coronary artery occlusion, commonly due to plaque rupture and thrombosis. A large anterior infarction can cause severe left-ventricular dysfunction, pulmonary edema, acute ischemic mitral regurgitation, and cardiogenic shock.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional substernal chest heaviness progressing to rest pain
Epigastric discomfort, which can occur as an anginal equivalent
Remote smoking history as a coronary risk factor
Cool clammy extremities and thready pulses indicating shock
Left basilar rales indicating pulmonary edema or congestion
Apical holosystolic murmur compatible with acute ischemic mitral regurgitation
ECG changes in anterior precordial leads that may suggest anterior myocardial injury or infarction
symptoms_not_in_common: Ten-day prodrome of bloating and persistent vomiting is less typical for an abrupt coronary occlusion
Myocardial biopsy showing diffuse inflammatory infiltrates and giant cells would not be expected in routine acute myocardial infarction
Hepatomegaly developing with the acute presentation is less specific for isolated acute infarction

data.diagnosis: Acute decompensated systolic heart failure with cardiogenic shock
data.description: A syndrome of severe pump failure in which inadequate cardiac output and elevated filling pressures cause pulmonary congestion, systemic venous congestion, tissue hypoperfusion, and shock. In this case, myocarditis or acute myocardial infarction could be the underlying cause.
symptoms_in_common: Palpable enlarged liver from venous congestion
Apical holosystolic murmur suggestive of mitral regurgitation
Nausea and vomiting, which can occur with low cardiac output and visceral hypoperfusion
symptoms_not_in_common: The prolonged epigastric pain and bloating are not specific for heart failure
A specific inflammatory giant-cell myocardial biopsy pattern would indicate an underlying myocarditis rather than heart failure alone
Prior hemicolectomy for dysplastic polyps and ventral hernia are unrelated to heart failure

data.description: A 30-month-old boy presented with sudden cardiac arrest during anesthesia induction with sevoflurane and nitric oxide before plastic surgery on June 7, 2004. The patient had never undergone ECG before the operation. Physical examination revealed distinctive facial features including a round face, small upper jaw and teeth, and nearly bald head. He had normal toes, with no history of seizure or syncope, and normal neurodevelopment. The patient was born via vaginal delivery without complications. Echocardiogram showed no intracardiac anomaly with normal ventricular function. Preoperative biochemical analysis and electrolyte levels were normal. Family history was notable for his older sister showing paradoxical QT interval prolongation on epinephrine stress test (QTc baseline 0.4 → peak 0.53 sec), though she was asymptomatic. The QT intervals of parents and sister were not significantly prolonged on ECG, and there was no family history of syncope, seizure, or sudden death.

data.diagnosis: Andersen-Tawil syndrome (KCNJ2-related channelopathy; Long QT syndrome type 7)
data.description: A rare autosomal-dominant potassium-channel disorder caused most often by KCNJ2 variants, characterized by ventricular arrhythmias, prominent U waves/QU prolongation, periodic paralysis, and distinctive craniofacial and skeletal features.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden cardiac arrest during anesthesia induction
ECG features consistent with prolonged QU/QT interval and prominent U waves
Family member with paradoxical QT prolongation during epinephrine stress testing
Small upper jaw and small teeth
Normal echocardiogram and normal ventricular function
Heterozygous c.1216G>A (p.G406R) variant, consistent with a pathogenic KCNJ2 mutation
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported episodic muscle weakness or periodic paralysis
Normal toes without typical syndactyly or other pedal skeletal abnormalities
No prior syncope or seizure history

data.diagnosis: Congenital long QT syndrome, especially LQT1
data.description: An inherited cardiac repolarization disorder that predisposes to torsades de pointes, ventricular fibrillation, syncope, and sudden cardiac arrest, often triggered by adrenergic stimulation, stress, exercise, or some anesthetic medications.
symptoms_in_common: Repolarization abnormality with QT/QU prolongation on ECG
Paradoxical QT prolongation during epinephrine testing in the sister
Family pattern suggestive of inherited arrhythmia susceptibility
Normal cardiac structure and ventricular function
Normal electrolyte levels, making acquired electrolyte-mediated QT prolongation less likely
symptoms_not_in_common: Distinctive craniofacial abnormalities
Small upper jaw and teeth
Nearly bald or sparse hair
Hand skeletal/radiographic abnormalities
Identified KCNJ2 variant, which supports Andersen-Tawil syndrome rather than classic LQT1

data.description: An inherited arrhythmia syndrome in which adrenergic stress triggers bidirectional or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia despite a structurally normal heart and often a normal resting ECG.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac arrest in the setting of anesthesia induction and physiologic stress
Possible adrenergic sensitivity suggested by the sister's epinephrine stress-test response
Normal echocardiogram and normal ventricular function
No biochemical or electrolyte abnormality to explain the arrest
No prior symptoms may occur in young children with CPVT
symptoms_not_in_common: QT/QU interval prolongation and prominent U waves are not typical primary CPVT findings
Distinctive facial dysmorphism
Small upper jaw and teeth
Nearly bald or sparse hair
KCNJ2 p.G406R variant favors Andersen-Tawil syndrome rather than CPVT

data.diagnosis: Timothy syndrome (CACNA1C-related long QT syndrome type 8)
data.description: A severe multisystem calcium-channel disorder associated with marked QT prolongation, malignant ventricular arrhythmias, syndactyly, characteristic facial features, and frequently developmental delay or autism-spectrum features.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac arrest at a young age
Normal structural echocardiogram can be present
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal toes without syndactyly
Normal neurodevelopment
No reported congenital heart defect
No reported immune dysfunction or hypoglycemia
KCNJ2 p.G406R variant rather than a CACNA1C variant
Nearly bald hair and small upper jaw/teeth are more supportive of Andersen-Tawil syndrome

data.description: 27-year-old man with a history of ulcerative colitis presented with 2 weeks of fatigue and 11 days of bloating and persistent nonbloody loose diarrhea after moving from Indonesia to the United States, with recent travel to rural India. He also reported decreased exercise tolerance and about 4.5 kg weight loss, without fever, chills, vomiting, cramping, or abdominal pain. He had been treated previously for ulcerative colitis with mesalamine and was taking mesalamine 1.2 g daily. On examination, vital signs were normal, the spleen tip was palpable, and an erythematous papular rash was present on the anterior thorax. Laboratory testing showed marked leukocytosis with severe eosinophilia.

Infection with the intestinal nematode Strongyloides stercoralis, acquired through contaminated soil in tropical and subtropical regions. It can cause chronic diarrhea, rash, weight loss, and prominent eosinophilia.
symptoms_in_common: Recent travel to rural India and prior residence in Indonesia
symptoms_not_in_common: Palpable spleen tip

data.description: Intestinal infection with Ancylostoma or Necator species acquired through skin contact with contaminated soil. It can produce eosinophilia, gastrointestinal symptoms, rash at the site of penetration, and fatigue from iron-deficiency anemia.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported iron-deficiency anemia
Palpable spleen tip
Rash on the anterior thorax rather than a typical soil-exposure site such as the feet

data.description: Parasitic infection caused by Schistosoma species, acquired from freshwater exposure in endemic areas. Intestinal schistosomiasis can cause diarrhea, weight loss, eosinophilia, rash, and hepatosplenic disease.
symptoms_in_common: Travel to an endemic rural region
symptoms_not_in_common: No known freshwater exposure
No abdominal pain
No bloody diarrhea
No fever or chills
No evidence provided of liver disease or portal hypertension

data.description: An eosinophil-predominant inflammatory disorder of the gastrointestinal tract that can cause diarrhea, abdominal bloating, weight loss, and peripheral eosinophilia. It may be triggered by allergy, medications, or parasitic infection.
symptoms_in_common: Colonic tissue with prominent eosinophilic inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: Recent travel to rural India strongly favors a parasitic cause
Erythematous papular rash is less characteristic
Palpable spleen tip is not typical
No abdominal pain or cramping

data.description: A relapse of chronic inflammatory bowel disease affecting the colonic mucosa. Typical flares cause frequent diarrhea, urgency, rectal bleeding, abdominal discomfort, fatigue, and weight loss.
symptoms_not_in_common: Diarrhea is nonbloody
No abdominal pain or cramping
Marked severe eosinophilia is unusual for an uncomplicated ulcerative colitis flare
Erythematous papular rash
Palpable spleen tip
Recent high-risk travel for helminth infection

data.description: A disorder characterized by persistent marked eosinophilia that can infiltrate and damage multiple organs, including the skin, gastrointestinal tract, lungs, heart, and spleen. Secondary causes such as parasitic infection must be excluded first.
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute onset after travel to rural India is more suggestive of parasitic infection
No reported cardiac, pulmonary, neurologic, or thrombotic manifestations
No fever, chills, or systemic organ damage described

data.description: 28-year-old male who suddenly went into coma for 9 hours preceded by tonic-clonic seizures lasting 10 minutes. No fever, vomiting or micturition. No focal neurological signs. Past medical history was unremarkable. Neurological examination revealed normal cranial nerves, normal power and reflexes. Routine laboratory tests were normal.

data.diagnosis: Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype (hemorrhagic high-grade diffuse astrocytic glioma)
data.description: An aggressive primary glial brain tumor that commonly shows central necrosis, irregular ring enhancement, extensive vasogenic edema, and occasionally intratumoral hemorrhage. The imaging and immunohistochemical pattern of GFAP and Olig2 positivity with retained ATRX and absent/low IDH1 staining favors a high-grade astrocytic glioma.
symptoms_in_common: Ring-enhancing lesion with central necrosis on MRI
Young adult presentation can occur, although less common
symptoms_not_in_common: No focal neurological deficits despite a sizeable frontal lesion
No preceding headache, vomiting, or other symptoms of raised intracranial pressure reported
Abrupt presentation without a prior progressive neurological history

data.description: A WHO grade 3 diffuse glioma, classically occurring in young to middle-aged adults and often presenting with seizures. It is defined molecularly by IDH mutation and 1p/19q codeletion; imaging may show calcification, enhancement, necrosis, and hemorrhage in higher-grade tumors.
symptoms_in_common: Olig2 immunoreactivity can be seen in oligodendroglial tumors
Hemorrhage and ring enhancement may occur in anaplastic lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: Sudden prolonged coma is less typical as an initial presentation
No chronic seizure history or slowly progressive symptoms reported
No characteristic calcification described on imaging
The reported IDH1 immunostaining does not clearly support the typical IDH-mutant molecular profile

data.description: A focal intracranial infection producing a pus-filled lesion with a smooth ring-enhancing capsule and surrounding edema. It can cause seizures, reduced consciousness, and mass effect, but usually has clinical or laboratory evidence of infection.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
Normal routine laboratory tests
No reported leukocytosis or infectious source
Intratumoral-appearing hemorrhage is not typical of a simple pyogenic abscess
No vomiting, headache, or focal neurological deficit reported

data.description: Metastatic tumors to the brain can present as well-circumscribed enhancing lesions with extensive edema and intralesional bleeding. Common hemorrhagic metastases include melanoma, renal cell carcinoma, choriocarcinoma, thyroid carcinoma, and some lung cancers.
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 28 years is less typical for most metastatic malignancies
No known primary cancer or systemic symptoms
Solitary frontal lesion without other reported intracranial lesions
No past medical history suggesting malignancy

data.description: 82-year-old man with a 6-month history of worsening back and left hip pain, occasional nocturnal awakening, worse with activity, not relieved by bending forward, and without leg radiation, morning stiffness, fever, chills, night sweats, or bowel/bladder incontinence. He also reported 9 kg weight loss over several months. Pain began after recovery from pneumonia treated with levofloxacin. Past history includes sick sinus syndrome with pacemaker, diastolic heart failure, pulmonary fibrosis, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, gout, herpes zoster with postherpetic neuralgia, and basal-cell carcinoma. On examination, he was afebrile and in no acute distress, with no spinal or sacroiliac tenderness, normal hip exam, no neurologic deficits, slightly diminished patellar reflexes bilaterally, intact sensation, normal rectal tone, and negative straight-leg raise.

Blastomycosis is a systemic fungal infection caused by Blastomyces species, usually acquired by inhalation. It can cause pulmonary disease and disseminate hematogenously to bone, including the spine, producing destructive vertebral osteomyelitis and paraspinal soft-tissue masses. Tissue may show broad-based budding yeast.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging consistent with destructive vertebral infection and adjacent soft-tissue involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain worse with activity
Absence of fever or chills
Absence of night sweats
No spinal tenderness

data.diagnosis: Vertebral osteomyelitis/discitis due to bacterial infection
data.description: Vertebral osteomyelitis is infection of vertebral bone, often with involvement of the adjacent intervertebral disc and possible epidural or paraspinal extension. Common causes include Staphylococcus aureus and gram-negative bacteria, but fungal causes should be considered when the course is indolent.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent worsening back pain over months
Imaging showing vertebral destructive changes and paraspinal soft-tissue abnormality
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No chills
No focal spinal tenderness
No neurologic deficits
No bowel or bladder incontinence
Prolonged indolent 6-month course

data.description: Spinal tuberculosis is a chronic granulomatous infection of the vertebrae caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It commonly produces slowly progressive back pain, vertebral destruction, disc-space involvement, paraspinal abscesses, and constitutional symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging compatible with destructive vertebral disease and a paraspinal soft-tissue collection
Indolent course without marked systemic toxicity
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No night sweats
No reported chronic cough or active respiratory symptoms
Pain worsened by activity
No neurologic deficits or bowel/bladder dysfunction

data.diagnosis: Metastatic malignancy involving the lumbar spine
data.description: Metastatic cancer can involve the vertebrae and cause progressive mechanical or nocturnal back pain, weight loss, vertebral destruction, and occasionally neurologic compromise. In an older adult, lung, prostate, renal, gastrointestinal, and hematologic malignancies are important considerations.
symptoms_in_common: Pain that awakens him at night
symptoms_not_in_common: Recent pneumonia-like pulmonary illness preceding the spinal symptoms
Imaging suggestion of disc-centered infection and paraspinal inflammatory soft-tissue change
No known internal malignancy
No neurologic deficits despite prolonged symptoms

data.description: A 47-year-old woman presented with intermittent cough, shortness of breath, fever (body temperature up to 38.5°C), accompanied by right eyelid swelling around June 17, 2017, which worsened day by day. Weight loss was about 9 kg. Physical examination included high body temperature of 39°C, right eyelid swelling, and a painless enlarged lymph node about 2 cm × 2 cm in size in the left axilla. Auscultation of lungs revealed coarse respiratory sounds with moist rale. No hepatosplenomegaly and edema in lower limbs.

Systemic infection caused by Cryptococcus species, usually involving the lungs and potentially spreading to skin, lymph nodes, soft tissue, and the central nervous system. Histology may show encapsulated yeast with prominent clear halos.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules/infiltrates on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No hepatosplenomegaly
No lower-limb edema

data.description: A systemic dimorphic fungal infection that can cause fever, weight loss, pulmonary disease, lymphadenopathy, and skin or subcutaneous lesions, particularly in immunocompromised patients.
symptoms_not_in_common: Painless isolated left axillary lymph node enlargement rather than generalized lymphadenopathy
No hepatosplenomegaly
No reported typical umbilicated papular skin lesions

data.description: A systemic fungal infection caused by Histoplasma species that may produce constitutional symptoms, diffuse lung abnormalities, lymph-node enlargement, and skin or soft-tissue involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary nodules and bilateral infiltrative changes
Possible skin or soft-tissue manifestation causing eyelid swelling
symptoms_not_in_common: No hepatosplenomegaly
No reported oral ulcers or mucosal lesions
No reported pancytopenia or other bone-marrow failure manifestations

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection can cause chronic constitutional symptoms, cough, pulmonary infiltrates or nodules, and peripheral lymphadenopathy; less commonly, it can involve the eyelid or other soft tissues.
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute progressive eyelid swelling is less typical
Painless isolated axillary lymphadenopathy is less typical than cervical lymph-node disease
No reported night sweats
No reported hemoptysis

data.diagnosis: Lymphoma with pulmonary and extranodal involvement
data.description: Lymphoma is a malignancy of lymphoid cells that may produce fever, weight loss, painless lymph-node enlargement, lung lesions, and occasionally orbital or eyelid involvement.
symptoms_not_in_common: Moist rales and coarse breath sounds suggest an infectious pulmonary process rather than lymphoma alone
Acute cough and shortness of breath with high fever are less typical as the primary presentation
Rapidly worsening inflammatory-appearing eyelid swelling is less typical

data.description: A 19-year-old previously healthy gravida 3 para 2002 female presented at 28 weeks' gestation after emigrating to the U.S. at 25 weeks of gestation. During the 20th week of gestation, she experienced a maculopapular rash, conjunctivitis, fever, and headache. She and her spouse had unprotected intercourse through the first and second trimester. The patient's initial fetal ultrasound with neurosonography revealed cerebral ventriculomegaly (20-25 mm) with dangling choroid, prominent 3rd ventricle, and a widened cavum septum pellucidum. Amniocentesis showed negative NAT for ZIKV with no evidence of chromosomal variations by CMA; TORCH panel was negative.

data.diagnosis: Congenital Zika syndrome due to maternal Zika virus infection
data.description: Fetal neurologic injury caused by in-utero Zika virus infection, often following maternal infection with fever, rash, conjunctivitis, and headache. Prenatal imaging may show ventriculomegaly, cortical malformations, calcifications, corpus callosum abnormalities, and microcephaly, although microcephaly is not always present.
symptoms_in_common: Maternal maculopapular rash at approximately 20 weeks' gestation
Residence in or exposure history from a Zika-endemic area
Unprotected sexual intercourse with spouse during pregnancy, allowing possible sexual transmission
Negative chromosomal microarray and negative TORCH evaluation, supporting consideration of Zika
symptoms_not_in_common: No fetal microcephaly reported
Negative Zika virus nucleic acid testing of amniotic fluid

data.diagnosis: Fetal aqueductal stenosis causing obstructive hydrocephalus
data.description: Narrowing or obstruction of the cerebral aqueduct impairs cerebrospinal fluid flow from the third to fourth ventricle, producing enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles. It may be isolated or associated with infection, hemorrhage, or genetic conditions.
symptoms_in_common: Dangling choroid plexus, consistent with severe ventricular dilation
No chromosomal copy-number abnormality detected by microarray
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal maculopapular rash
Maternal fever
Maternal headache
Maternal conjunctivitis
Epidemiologic risk for Zika virus infection
Widened or dysplastic cavum septum pellucidum, which may suggest broader brain developmental injury rather than isolated obstruction

data.description: In-utero cytomegalovirus infection can cause fetal ventriculomegaly, intracranial calcifications, cortical developmental abnormalities, growth restriction, hepatosplenomegaly, and hearing loss. Maternal infection is often asymptomatic but may resemble a nonspecific viral illness.
symptoms_in_common: Maternal febrile viral-like illness during pregnancy
Possible fetal central nervous system developmental abnormality
symptoms_not_in_common: Maculopapular rash and conjunctivitis are more characteristic of Zika than CMV
Negative TORCH panel
No reported intracranial calcifications
No reported fetal growth restriction
No reported hepatosplenomegaly, ascites, or placental abnormalities
No reported microcephaly

data.description: Transplacental infection with Toxoplasma gondii may cause hydrocephalus or ventriculomegaly, intracranial calcifications, chorioretinitis, and neurologic impairment. Maternal infection may be asymptomatic or produce a mild influenza-like syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Maternal fever and headache could occur with a nonspecific infectious illness
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal maculopapular rash and conjunctivitis are not typical of toxoplasmosis
Negative TORCH panel
No reported intracranial calcifications
No reported chorioretinitis or other ocular fetal abnormalities
No reported hepatosplenomegaly or ascites
Exposure history suggests Zika risk rather than toxoplasmosis risk

data.description: 26-year-old Chinese female with a 2-year history of progressive lower-limb weakness and scissor gait starting at age 24, later developing dysphagia and severe cognitive impairment (MMSE 16/30). Exam showed severe spasticity in the lower extremities, mild spasticity in the upper extremities, and left patellar clonus. Birth and developmental history were normal. She was initially considered sporadic, but later genetic testing showed compound heterozygous mutations consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

data.diagnosis: SPG11-associated hereditary spastic paraplegia (spatacsin-related complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia)
data.description: An autosomal recessive complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia caused by biallelic SPG11 variants. It commonly produces progressive lower-limb spasticity, gait impairment, cognitive decline, dysphagia, white-matter abnormalities, and thinning of the corpus callosum.
symptoms_in_common: MRI findings consistent with corpus callosum thinning and periventricular white-matter abnormalities
Compound heterozygous mutations with autosomal recessive inheritance
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal birth and early development are not abnormal for SPG11, although some affected individuals can have earlier developmental or learning difficulties

data.diagnosis: SPG15-associated hereditary spastic paraplegia (ZFYVE26-related spastic paraplegia)
data.description: A rare autosomal recessive complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia that resembles SPG11, often causing progressive spastic paraparesis, intellectual decline, dysphagia, peripheral neuropathy, and thinning of the corpus callosum.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive spastic weakness of the lower limbs
MRI pattern including a thin corpus callosum and white-matter changes
symptoms_not_in_common: SPG11 compound heterozygous mutations support SPG11 rather than ZFYVE26-related SPG15
Peripheral neuropathy, distal muscle wasting, and retinal abnormalities were not reported
The onset at age 24 is somewhat later than the frequent adolescent onset of SPG15

data.diagnosis: SPG47-associated hereditary spastic paraplegia (AP4B1-related AP-4 deficiency syndrome)
data.description: An autosomal recessive complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia due to AP4B1 deficiency, characterized by spastic paraplegia, intellectual disability, speech impairment, microcephaly, and sometimes a thin corpus callosum.
symptoms_in_common: Upper motor neuron signs including clonus
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal early development is atypical because AP-4 deficiency usually begins in infancy or childhood with developmental delay
Adult onset at age 24 is atypical
Microcephaly, early severe speech delay, seizures, and dystonia were not reported
SPG11 mutations rather than AP4B1 mutations were identified

data.description: An autosomal recessive complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia caused by biallelic SPG21 variants. It may include progressive spastic paraparesis, intellectual disability or dementia, dysarthria, extrapyramidal manifestations, and brain atrophy.
symptoms_not_in_common: SPG21 disease more often begins in childhood or adolescence rather than at age 24
Typical features such as dysarthria, extrapyramidal signs, facial weakness, and peripheral neuropathy were not described
The characteristic SPG11 genetic findings argue against SPG21

data.diagnosis: Adult-onset leukodystrophy with axonal spheroids and pigmented glia (CSF1R-related leukoencephalopathy)
data.description: A progressive white-matter neurodegenerative disorder that often presents in adulthood with cognitive or psychiatric decline followed by gait dysfunction, spasticity, and motor impairment. It is usually autosomal dominant but can occasionally appear sporadic.
symptoms_in_common: Spasticity and upper motor neuron signs
symptoms_not_in_common: The inheritance pattern is usually autosomal dominant rather than autosomal recessive
Compound heterozygous SPG11 mutations strongly favor SPG11-associated hereditary spastic paraplegia
Corpus callosum thinning and the specific hereditary-spastic-paraplegia phenotype are more characteristic of SPG11
Psychiatric symptoms, parkinsonism, seizures, and rapid behavioral decline were not reported

diagnoses.name: Complex hereditary spastic paraplegia
diagnoses.title: Autosomal recessive complex hereditary spastic paraplegia

data.description: A 25-year-old female in her third trimester of pregnancy presented with paroxysmal headache, palpitations, sweating, and hypertension up to 230/130 for three weeks. Her medical history was negative for previous hypertension, and physical examination was unremarkable. Initial work-up excluded pre-eclampsia. Her urine catecholamines were markedly elevated: Dopamine 607 μg/24 hours (range 65-400), Norepinephrine 978 μg/24 hours (range 15-80), Metanephrine 108 μg/24 hours (range 24-96), Normetanephrine 4067 μg/24 hours (range 75-375), and Vanillyl mandelic acid 13.6 mg/24 hours (range 2-7). Epinephrine level was normal at 0.8 μg/24 hours (range 0.0-20.0). Initial abdominal MRI showed a 28×19 mm left juxta-adrenal mass that was later found to be brown fat.

A catecholamine-secreting neuroendocrine tumor arising from sympathetic paraganglia in the mediastinum, often near the great vessels or heart. These tumors commonly produce norepinephrine and normetanephrine rather than epinephrine.
symptoms_in_common: Normal epinephrine level, which is compatible with an extra-adrenal sympathetic paraganglioma
No prior history of chronic hypertension
symptoms_not_in_common: Third-trimester pregnancy is not a typical symptom, although pregnancy can unmask or worsen catecholamine-secreting tumors
Initial apparent left juxta-adrenal mass was brown fat rather than tumor

data.description: A rare functional paraganglioma located adjacent to the heart, commonly near the left atrium, aortic root, pulmonary artery, or atrioventricular groove. It may cause severe catecholamine-mediated hypertension and can be detected as an intensely avid mediastinal mass.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated urinary dopamine and vanillylmandelic acid
Normal urinary epinephrine, consistent with many cardiac paragangliomas
Imaging showing a lesion in the mediastinum adjacent to cardiac structures
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported chest pain
No reported dyspnea or heart-failure symptoms
No reported arrhythmia, syncope, or cardiac obstruction symptoms

data.description: A catecholamine-secreting tumor of adrenal medullary chromaffin cells that classically causes episodic headache, sweating, palpitations, and hypertension. Most pheochromocytomas are adrenal, whereas paragangliomas occur outside the adrenal glands.
symptoms_in_common: Classic triad of headache, palpitations, and sweating
Marked elevation of urinary catecholamine metabolites
symptoms_not_in_common: No confirmed adrenal mass
The initially suspected juxta-adrenal lesion was brown fat
Predominantly norepinephrine/normetanephrine secretion with normal epinephrine is more characteristic of an extra-adrenal paraganglioma
Imaging localizes the likely lesion to the mediastinum rather than the adrenal gland

data.description: A pregnancy-specific hypertensive disorder occurring after 20 weeks of gestation, typically characterized by new-onset hypertension with proteinuria and/or maternal organ dysfunction. Severe disease may cause headache and marked hypertension.
symptoms_not_in_common: Paroxysmal palpitations
Profuse sweating
Markedly elevated urinary norepinephrine, normetanephrine, dopamine, and vanillylmandelic acid
Presence of a hypermetabolic mediastinal mass
Preeclampsia was excluded during the initial evaluation
No reported proteinuria, thrombocytopenia, liver dysfunction, or fetal/placental complications

data.description: A 71-year-old woman presented with a 3-day history of headache and fatigue, followed by sudden onset of confusion and language production difficulties while typing at work. The confusion resolved briefly but recurred later that evening. She had a history of myasthenia gravis (diagnosed 18 years prior, treated with mycophenolate mofetil for 7 years), vitamin B12 deficiency, and hypertension. Past surgical history included supracervical hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (31 years prior), transsternal thymectomy and wedge resection of right upper lobe for cortical thymoma (22 years prior), and sigmoid colectomy for recurrent diverticulitis (7 years prior). On examination at the current hospital, she had severe expressive aphasia, followed commands intermittently, disconjugate gaze at rest, motor strength 5/5 in left extremities and 4/5 in right extremities. Blood phosphorus was 2.2 mg/dL (reference range 2.6-4.5); other routine labs were normal.

An opportunistic bacterial infection caused by Nocardia species that can produce suppurative, ring-enhancing brain abscesses, particularly in patients receiving chronic immunosuppressive therapy. The imaging and histology are most consistent with a cerebral Nocardia abscess.
symptoms_in_common: Ring-enhancing intracranial mass with surrounding edema
Suppurative inflammatory histology with filamentous bacterial-appearing organisms
symptoms_not_in_common: Disconjugate gaze at rest
Mild hypophosphatemia
History of myasthenia gravis

data.description: Toxoplasma gondii reactivation is an opportunistic parasitic infection that commonly causes multiple ring-enhancing brain lesions with edema in severely immunocompromised patients.
symptoms_not_in_common: A solitary dominant lesion rather than the more typical multiple lesions
Histology suggesting a neutrophilic abscess and bacterial organisms rather than tachyzoites or tissue cysts
No reported fever
Disconjugate gaze at rest
Mild hypophosphatemia

data.description: A lymphoma confined to the brain, meninges, spinal cord, or eyes. It is more frequent in immunosuppressed patients and may cause focal neurologic deficits and enhancing brain lesions.
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt fluctuating onset over hours is less typical
Restricted diffusion and ring-enhancing appearance favor abscess in this case
Suppurative inflammatory pathology rather than malignant lymphoid cells
Headache for only 3 days
Disconjugate gaze at rest
Mild hypophosphatemia

data.description: A high-grade primary glial tumor that commonly occurs in older adults and can produce an irregular enhancing mass with central necrosis, edema, headache, cognitive changes, and focal deficits.
symptoms_in_common: Enhancing brain mass with surrounding edema
symptoms_not_in_common: Very acute symptom onset and transient fluctuation
Chronic immunosuppression favors opportunistic infection
Imaging features compatible with a pyogenic abscess rather than infiltrative tumor
Suppurative inflammatory histology with organisms rather than neoplastic glial cells
Disconjugate gaze at rest
Mild hypophosphatemia

data.description: 36-year-old obese woman with a 5-year history of type 2 diabetes presented with 5 days of fever, chills, cough with yellow sputum, and sharp right lower chest pain worsened by deep breathing. She had a positive Mantoux test in 1976, smoked one pack per day, and drank alcohol socially. One week before symptom onset, she stayed at her sister’s cottage by a local lake and slept in a gazebo for two nights. On return to hospital 5 days later, she was febrile at 39°C, mildly tachycardic (104 bpm), with normal blood pressure, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation. Examination showed decreased air entry and bronchial breath sounds in the right lower chest.

A potentially severe atypical bacterial pneumonia caused by Legionella species, often associated with exposure to aerosolized freshwater or contaminated water systems and capable of rapidly progressing to multilobar pneumonia.
symptoms_in_common: Right lower-lobe consolidation progressing to bilateral/multilobar infiltrates on imaging
Recent stay near a lake/freshwater exposure
Diabetes and smoking, which increase risk for severe Legionella infection
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported diarrhea
No reported nausea or vomiting
No reported confusion or other neurologic symptoms
Normal oxygen saturation at presentation

data.diagnosis: Community-acquired bacterial pneumonia, likely pneumococcal pneumonia
data.description: An acute bacterial infection of the lung parenchyma, commonly caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, producing fever, productive cough, pleuritic pain, and lobar consolidation.
symptoms_in_common: Sharp chest pain worsened by deep inspiration
Bronchial breath sounds and reduced air entry over the right lower chest
Right lower-lobe air-space consolidation on chest imaging
Diabetes and smoking as risk factors for pneumonia
symptoms_not_in_common: Progression to bilateral patchy lower-lung infiltrates can occur but is less typical of uncomplicated lobar pneumococcal pneumonia
Recent freshwater/lake exposure is not specifically associated with pneumococcal pneumonia
Normal oxygen saturation despite radiographic progression may be less typical in extensive multilobar disease

data.description: Pneumonia caused by inhalation of oropharyngeal or gastric contents, typically involving dependent lung regions such as the right lower lobe and sometimes causing bilateral lower-lobe infiltrates.
symptoms_in_common: Right lower-lobe predominance on initial imaging
Bilateral dependent lower-lung infiltrates on later imaging
Social alcohol use, which can modestly increase aspiration risk
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported vomiting, altered consciousness, seizure, dysphagia, or witnessed aspiration event
Only social alcohol intake rather than heavy intoxication
Lake-side/gazebo exposure is not characteristic
Abrupt febrile illness with chills is more suggestive of infectious community-acquired pneumonia than simple aspiration pneumonitis

data.description: A chronic granulomatous lung infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, usually presenting with prolonged cough, constitutional symptoms, and often upper-lobe infiltrates or cavitation in reactivation disease.
symptoms_in_common: History of a positive Mantoux test
Diabetes, which increases the risk of active tuberculosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Very acute onset over five days
Chills and yellow purulent sputum
Sharp pleuritic chest pain
Right lower-lobe then bilateral lower-lobe consolidation rather than typical upper-lobe/cavitary disease
No reported chronic cough, weight loss, night sweats, hemoptysis, or prolonged constitutional symptoms

data.description: A rare viral zoonotic illness acquired through inhalation of aerosolized rodent excreta, initially causing fever and myalgias and potentially progressing rapidly to pulmonary edema, hypoxemia, and shock.
symptoms_in_common: Recent sleeping outdoors in a gazebo, which could permit rodent exposure
Rapid development of bilateral pulmonary infiltrates
symptoms_not_in_common: Yellow sputum is not typical
Localized right lower-lobe consolidation and bronchial breath sounds favor bacterial pneumonia
No reported severe shortness of breath
Normal oxygen saturation
No hypotension or shock
No reported thrombocytopenia, hemoconcentration, or prominent myalgias

data.description: 19-year-old female with congenital hypotonia and weak breathing/crying at birth. In the first month of life she developed respiratory failure requiring tracheotomy and mechanical ventilation. She had patent ductus arteriosus surgically repaired at age 2, recurrent respiratory infections, and scoliosis surgery at age 12. Prior testing at age 4 showed a 36% decrement in compound muscle action potential area with nerve stimulation and no repetitive CMAPs; AChR and MuSK antibodies were negative. Recent examination showed normal cognition, bilateral ptosis, mild limitation of upgaze, facial, bulbar, neck, and proximal limb weakness, with intact deep tendon reflexes.

data.diagnosis: Congenital myasthenic syndrome (CMS), postsynaptic acetylcholine receptor deficiency
data.description: A genetic neuromuscular-junction disorder causing impaired transmission of acetylcholine signals to muscle, often due to variants in CHRNE, CHRNA1, CHRNB1, CHRND, or RAPSN. It produces fatigable ocular, facial, bulbar, respiratory, and limb weakness from infancy.
symptoms_in_common: Weak cry and breathing difficulty at birth
Severe neonatal respiratory failure requiring tracheotomy and mechanical ventilation
36% decrement in compound muscle action potential with repetitive nerve stimulation
symptoms_not_in_common: Patent ductus arteriosus
Severe scoliosis requiring surgery

data.description: A postsynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by rapsyn deficiency, which impairs clustering and stabilization of acetylcholine receptors at the motor endplate. Severe neonatal respiratory crises and episodic respiratory decompensation are characteristic.
symptoms_in_common: Need for chronic ventilatory support and tracheotomy
Decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
symptoms_not_in_common: Patent ductus arteriosus is not a usual feature
Scoliosis can occur secondarily to chronic weakness but is not a defining feature

data.diagnosis: CHAT-related congenital myasthenic syndrome (choline acetyltransferase deficiency)
data.description: A presynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by deficient acetylcholine synthesis. It commonly presents in infancy with episodic apnea or respiratory failure, hypotonia, ptosis, and a decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation.
symptoms_in_common: Weak breathing and crying at birth
Respiratory failure in the first month of life
Requirement for tracheotomy and mechanical ventilation
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly described episodic apnea triggered by fever, infection, or stress
Mild ophthalmoparesis is less prominent than in many postsynaptic CMS forms
Patent ductus arteriosus is not typical
Scoliosis is not a primary characteristic

data.description: A 52-year-old man was brought to the emergency department with acute onset shortness of breath and confusion. On physical examination, he was agitated and taking deep breaths at a rate of 28/min. Initial venous blood gas on ambient air showed pH 7.02, partial pressure of carbon dioxide 3.4 kPa, and partial pressure of oxygen 4.1 kPa. Laboratory studies revealed blood glucose 7.1 mmol/L (reference range 4.4-6.1), lactic acid 6.6 mmol/L (0.5-2.2), serum anion gap 19 mmol/L (8-16), serum osmolality 318 mmol/kg (275-295), serum osmolal gap 20 mmol/kg (<10), and acute kidney injury with creatinine 141 μmol/L (70-120). Blood ethanol was undetectable and urine drug screen was negative. Urinalysis showed haematuria and no ketones.
Toxic alcohol ingestion causing severe high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, elevated osmolal gap, acute kidney injury, and calcium oxalate crystal deposition in urine.
symptoms_in_common: Tachypnea with deep respirations consistent with respiratory compensation for metabolic acidosis
Urine microscopy appearance consistent with calcium oxalate crystals
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported history of antifreeze or toxic alcohol ingestion

data.description: Toxic alcohol ingestion that produces formic acid, causing high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, elevated osmolal gap, neurologic symptoms, and potentially visual toxicity.
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute kidney injury is less characteristic than in ethylene glycol poisoning
Haematuria is not typical
Urinary calcium oxalate crystals are not typical
No visual complaints such as blurred vision, photophobia, or blindness are reported

data.description: A metabolic emergency caused by insulin deficiency, characterized by hyperglycemia, ketone production, high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, dehydration, and Kussmaul respirations.
symptoms_in_common: Acute kidney injury that could occur with dehydration
symptoms_not_in_common: Blood glucose is only mildly elevated rather than markedly elevated
Urine ketones are absent
Elevated osmolal gap is not typical
Haematuria is not typical
Urinary calcium oxalate crystals are not typical

data.description: Aspirin or salicylate toxicity causes respiratory alkalosis with concurrent high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, tachypnea, altered mental status, and sometimes elevated lactate.
symptoms_in_common: Acute kidney injury can occur in severe poisoning
symptoms_not_in_common: The blood gas does not show the typical prominent respiratory alkalosis
Elevated osmolal gap is not typical
Haematuria is not typical
Urinary calcium oxalate crystals are not typical
No tinnitus, fever, diaphoresis, nausea, or vomiting is reported

data.description: 36-year-old man with 18 days of fever to 39.5°C, preceded by throat swelling sensation. He developed fever 3 days after symptom onset and was treated with amoxicillin-clavulanate for presumed streptococcal pharyngitis after tonsillar white spots were seen, but fevers persisted with headaches and fatigue. He also reported lower neck swelling and discomfort with neck movement, without dysphagia, odynophagia, rhinorrhea, or rash. Past history notable for seasonal allergies. Recent travel to the southwestern United States 2 weeks before symptom onset; his wife had a self-limited febrile sore throat during the trip. On examination, he was afebrile, tachycardic, with normal oropharynx, no lymphadenopathy, and a firm, nontender palpable thyroid in the anterior neck.

A self-limited inflammatory thyroid disorder, often following a viral upper respiratory illness, causing thyroid enlargement, fever, systemic symptoms, and sometimes transient thyrotoxicosis. CT may show diffuse thyroid enlargement with heterogeneous low attenuation.
symptoms_in_common: Recent exposure to a close contact with a self-limited febrile sore throat
symptoms_not_in_common: Nontender thyroid on examination
No reported palpitations, tremor, heat intolerance, weight loss, or other overt thyrotoxic symptoms
No preceding rhinorrhea or typical upper-respiratory symptoms

data.description: A rare bacterial infection of the thyroid that can cause fever, neck swelling, painful thyroid enlargement, and occasionally thyroid abscess formation. It is more likely in patients with anatomic fistulas, immunocompromise, or preexisting thyroid disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: Thyroid was nontender rather than markedly painful
No dysphagia or odynophagia
No erythema or warmth of the neck described
No cervical lymphadenopathy
No improvement despite broad oral antibiotic therapy
No reported abscess, fluctuance, or purulent collection on imaging

data.description: An autoimmune disorder in which thyroid-stimulating antibodies cause diffuse thyroid enlargement and hyperthyroidism. It commonly presents with tachycardia, heat intolerance, tremor, weight loss, and sometimes eye disease.
symptoms_in_common: Possible low-grade to moderate fever can occur in severe thyrotoxicosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Sustained fever to 39.5°C is unusual
Acute onset after a sore-throat illness is not typical
Neck discomfort and swelling sensation are not typical prominent features
No reported weight loss, tremor, heat intolerance, sweating, diarrhea, anxiety, or ophthalmopathy
Headache is nonspecific and not a typical primary presentation

data.description: A chronic autoimmune thyroiditis that causes gradual thyroid enlargement and commonly leads to hypothyroidism; an early transient inflammatory phase may occasionally cause thyrotoxic symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset over days
High persistent fever
Headache
Recent viral-like pharyngitis exposure
Neck discomfort with movement
Tachycardia without reported hypothyroid symptoms
Marked systemic inflammatory illness is not typical

data.description: A rare malignancy, usually arising in the setting of longstanding Hashimoto thyroiditis, that presents with rapidly enlarging thyroid mass and compressive neck symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 36 is younger than typical
High fever with acute infectious-like onset is uncommon
No dysphagia, dyspnea, hoarseness, or stridor
No cervical lymphadenopathy
No known history of Hashimoto thyroiditis
Recent exposure to a febrile sore-throat illness suggests an infectious or postviral trigger instead

data.description: 42-year-old man with coronary artery disease and dyslipidemia presented with 2 days of sudden left upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the back in a bandlike pattern, worsened by movement, associated with nausea and early satiety, and increasing in intensity. He also had substernal chest pressure like his usual angina but not relieved by one sublingual nitroglycerin tablet. He denied trauma, vomiting, rectal bleeding, or melena. Chronic history included diarrhea since CABG >10 years ago, worsened after a cholesterol medication dose increase 6 months earlier, plus 16 kg unintentional weight loss over 6 months, intermittent early satiety, daily headaches, frequent nocturia, and nocturnal warmth without fever or night sweats. Exam showed mild left upper quadrant tenderness without peritoneal signs. Vitals were stable. Labs showed elevated amylase, lipase, AST, and ALT with otherwise normal electrolytes, renal function, blood counts, bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, and triglycerides. ECG and chest radiograph were normal.

Acute inflammatory injury of the pancreas, commonly causing sudden upper abdominal pain and elevation of pancreatic enzymes. The CT appearance is consistent with pancreatic inflammation and peripancreatic fat stranding.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden left upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the back
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic diarrhea for 10 years
Six-month history of 16 kg unintentional weight loss
Daily headaches
Frequent nocturia
Nocturnal warmth
Substernal chest pressure resembling angina

data.description: Acute pancreatitis caused by an adverse medication reaction. Lipid-lowering agents, including some statins and other cholesterol-lowering medications, have rarely been associated with pancreatitis and gastrointestinal adverse effects.
symptoms_in_common: Acute upper abdominal pain radiating to the back
Symptoms occurring after a cholesterol medication dose increase
Normal triglyceride level, making hypertriglyceridemic pancreatitis less likely
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic diarrhea beginning years before the recent medication dose increase
Long-standing weight loss over 6 months
Daily headaches
Frequent nocturia
Nocturnal warmth
Angina-like substernal chest pressure

data.description: A form of microscopic colitis characterized by chronic nonbloody watery diarrhea, colonic mucosal inflammation, and increased intraepithelial lymphocytes on biopsy. Colonoscopy may appear grossly normal despite abnormal histology.
symptoms_in_common: Worsening diarrhea after a medication dose increase
Colonic biopsy appearance consistent with increased inflammatory cells and intraepithelial lymphocytes
symptoms_not_in_common: Sudden severe left upper quadrant pain radiating to the back
Elevated amylase and lipase
Elevated AST and ALT
Acute nausea and worsening upper abdominal pain
Substernal chest pressure resembling angina

data.description: A malignant tumor of the pancreas that can produce abdominal or back pain, early satiety, weight loss, and occasionally pancreatitis due to pancreatic duct obstruction. A pancreatic mass or obstructive jaundice is often present but is not described here.
symptoms_in_common: Upper abdominal pain radiating to the back
Acute pancreatitis can occasionally occur with pancreatic duct obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal bilirubin
Normal alkaline phosphatase
No described pancreatic mass on CT
Chronic diarrhea beginning 10 years earlier
Nocturnal warmth without fever or drenching night sweats
Acute onset over only 2 days is less typical of cancer pain

data.diagnosis: Chronic mesenteric ischemia with possible acute exacerbation
data.description: Reduced intestinal blood flow caused by mesenteric arterial atherosclerosis. It is more likely in patients with coronary artery disease and can cause postprandial pain, food avoidance, early satiety, diarrhea, and weight loss; acute ischemia usually causes more severe pain and systemic illness.
symptoms_in_common: Coronary artery disease and dyslipidemia, which increase atherosclerotic risk
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain is described as sudden left upper quadrant pain radiating to the back rather than typical postprandial diffuse pain
Elevated amylase and lipase favor pancreatitis
No peritoneal signs
Stable vital signs
No rectal bleeding or melena
No reported metabolic acidosis, leukocytosis, or elevated lactate

data.description: A 59-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital with a 9-day history of stiffness, swelling, and severe pain beginning in the metacarpophalangeal joint of the right thumb, followed by bilateral ankle involvement 3 days later. She had a history of stroke, glaucoma, and total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy 7 years prior. The patient lived in New England, worked in health care, and reported unprotected vaginal intercourse 2 weeks before presentation. Physical examination showed the right thumb metacarpophalangeal joint was erythematous, warm, and painful with movement. Both ankles showed effusion and warmth without erythema, with pain on all range of motion. No fever, chills, night sweats, or systemic symptoms were reported. Joint stiffness was not worse in the morning and did not improve throughout the day. Symptoms had not improved despite 4 days of methylprednisolone therapy.

data.diagnosis: Disseminated gonococcal infection with gonococcal septic arthritis
data.description: Hematogenous spread of Neisseria gonorrhoeae causing migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis, dermatitis, or purulent arthritis. Synovial-fluid culture and Gram stain may show gram-negative diplococci, and growth can occur on chocolate agar.
symptoms_in_common: Severe pain with range of motion
Compatible microbiology image showing diplococci and growth on enriched culture media
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or chills
No reported skin lesions
No reported tenosynovitis
Thumb metacarpophalangeal joint involvement is less classic than wrist, knee, or ankle involvement

data.description: Bacterial infection of a joint, most commonly due to Staphylococcus aureus, producing acute painful swelling, warmth, restricted movement, and joint effusion. It may involve more than one joint, particularly in patients with bacteremia or immunosuppression.
symptoms_in_common: Acute onset of severe joint pain
Pain with all ranges of motion
Erythema and warmth of the thumb joint
symptoms_not_in_common: Sequential migratory pattern involving thumb followed by both ankles
Recent unprotected sexual exposure suggesting a sexually transmitted pathogen
No fever, chills, or systemic illness
Microbiology appearance is more suggestive of diplococci than gram-positive staphylococcal clusters

data.diagnosis: Reactive arthritis due to sexually transmitted infection
data.description: A sterile inflammatory arthritis that can occur after genitourinary infection, classically Chlamydia trachomatis and less often gonorrhea. It usually causes asymmetric lower-extremity oligoarthritis and may include urethritis, conjunctivitis, enthesitis, or skin findings.
symptoms_in_common: No improvement with a short course of corticosteroids can occur in severe inflammatory disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly purulent-appearing acute arthritis of the thumb is less typical
No reported urethritis, cervicitis, dysuria, or vaginal discharge
No conjunctivitis or uveitis
No enthesitis, heel pain, dactylitis, or mucocutaneous lesions
Findings suggesting organisms in joint fluid would favor infectious septic arthritis rather than sterile reactive arthritis

data.description: Inflammatory arthritis caused by Borrelia burgdorferi infection, often occurring weeks to months after tick exposure. It most commonly causes intermittent or persistent swelling of one or a few large joints, especially the knee.
symptoms_in_common: Residence in New England, an endemic region
Absence of fever or major systemic symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: Very acute severe onset over days
Thumb metacarpophalangeal joint involvement
Bilateral ankle involvement without knee involvement
Marked erythema and severe pain with all movement are less typical
Recent unprotected intercourse provides a stronger risk factor for disseminated gonococcal infection
Microbiology findings consistent with bacterial diplococci would not be expected in Lyme arthritis

data.description: A chronic systemic autoimmune inflammatory arthritis that typically causes symmetric small-joint synovitis, prolonged morning stiffness, and gradual joint damage if untreated.
symptoms_in_common: Joint swelling, warmth, stiffness, and pain
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset over 9 days
Initial involvement of a single thumb metacarpophalangeal joint
Severe acute effusions and erythema suggesting septic arthritis
Stiffness not worse in the morning
Stiffness does not improve during the day
No response to methylprednisolone
Recent sexual exposure and culture/Gram-stain findings supporting infection

data.description: Crystal-induced inflammatory arthritis caused by deposition of calcium pyrophosphate crystals. It commonly affects knees and wrists but can affect ankles and small joints, producing abrupt pain, warmth, swelling, and effusion.
symptoms_in_common: Abrupt onset of severe inflammatory joint pain
symptoms_not_in_common: Sequential multi-joint pattern following recent unprotected intercourse
Thumb metacarpophalangeal joint involvement is less typical
No mention of chondrocalcinosis or crystals in synovial fluid
No improvement with corticosteroids
Microbiologic findings suggesting bacterial infection are not expected in pseudogout

data.description: A 29-year-old man presented to the hospital after several weeks of lumbar pain and fever up to 38°C. He had no significant past medical history. Physical examination revealed vital signs of blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, heart rate 121/min, and body temperature 38.2°C. There was no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly detected on examination.
